records.name: Hydration goal setup
records.description: Happy-path: a first-time or returning user customizes their daily hydration recommendation. Entry point: 'Calculate your goal' screen. The user opens each setting (Sex, Weight, Daily Activity, Weather) via rounded row controls that trigger bottom-sheet modals (list selection or a number picker). After each selection the large central goal number is recalculated and updated; the user can also enter a fully custom numeric goal. Exit point: user confirms the final goal with the 'DONE' control. Assumptions: user is on a mobile device, not required to be logged in, and has basic input permissions (keyboard, touch).
records.problem:
User task (user perspective): Choose personal attributes (sex, weight, activity level, local weather) or enter a custom number so the app can calculate a daily water (oz) target. The user expects quick, reversible selections, immediate feedback (new recommended oz), and a final confirmation.
System task (UI perspective): Present a clean summary screen with the current recommended goal and four editable attributes. Each attribute opens a modal (list or picker). When the user changes a value the system recalculates the hydration recommendation and animates/updates the displayed number. The system also allows entering a custom goal via a numeric entry modal which overrides the recommended value. The final result: user-perceived outcome is a visible hydration goal (e.g., 90 oz) shown on the main screen; system-level outcome is that the selected attributes and final goal are stored (persisted) and the UI returns to the main goal screen with the updated value.

steps.name: Calculate goal (summary)
steps.goal: Show the default/common hydration recommendation and let the user open attribute controls to personalize the goal.
steps.action: User views the large central value (64 oz) and taps any rounded row (Sex, Weight, Daily Activity, Weather) or taps 'CUSTOM GOAL'.
steps.system_response: Main screen stays visible; tapping a row opens a corresponding bottom-sheet modal. 'CUSTOM GOAL' leads to a numeric input modal. Top-right 'SKIP' remains available to bypass personalization.

content.description:
Overall style: Friendly, playful onboarding/goal-calculation screen with a single-column, centered layout and a bright, saturated teal background. Visual language uses large, airy typography for the numeric goal, soft rounded pill controls for inputs, light drop shadows, small line icons inside pills, and whimsical illustrations (a floating sheep and ice-like shapes) to reinforce a light, encouraging tone.

Color palette (primary):
- Teal background: #05BCDB (primary solid background)
- Very pale off-white for tiny UI accents and status area: #F8FAF9
- Accent gold for micro-highlights or brand accents: #DDBE04
- Accent yellow (for subtle glows or decorative elements): #F8ED58
- Text / dark accents: #080808 for high-contrast text when needed
- Foreground text and icons: predominantly white (#FFFFFF) and semi-transparent white (approx rgba(255,255,255,0.85) for secondary text)

Typography:
- Display numeric (64oz): very large geometric rounded sans (e.g., Avenir Next Rounded / Circular / Montserrat Alternates). Suggested size: 120–140px on a 375pt-wide screen, weight: 400–600 (medium). Line-height: 0.9 for tight numeric block. Center aligned.
- Section heading under numeric (“Calculate your goal”): medium-large weight 600, size 20–28px, line-height 1.2, centered. Color: white (#FFFFFF) or semi-opaque white.
- Small descriptor (“Common goal” with info icon): small size 12–14px, semibold 600, color: rgba(255,255,255,0.8).
- Input labels inside pills: 16–18px, weight 500, color: mostly white with reduced opacity for disabled/unselected, higher opacity for selected text.

Layout and spatial rules:
- Screen uses a full-bleed single-color background (teal) filling the safe area. Decorative translucent ice shapes are anchored left and right edges and bleed to the edges.
- Top safe-area contains phone status indicators and a small “SKIP” text button aligned top-right. Padding from edges: ~16–20px.
- Hero block centered vertically in the top half: a small playful sheep illustration floats near the top-left area of the hero region (partially overlapping the teal background), creating motion/whimsy.
- Main content is vertically stacked and centered horizontally. Vertical spacing example: status bar to hero top 24–32px; hero block (common goal) to numeric: 8–12px; numeric to subtitle: 18–28px; subtitle to control group: 36–48px.
- Control group: four full-width pill controls stacked vertically with equal spacing. Each pill has a large corner radius (capsule) approx height 56–72px, inner horizontal padding 24–28px, and spans about 82–88% of screen width and centered.
- Pill states: inactive/unfilled pills use a slightly darker teal overlay (semi-opaque) to imply disabled state; active or selectable pills use higher-contrast teal or bright cyan; selected pill is visually brighter with a subtle inner shadow and brighter icon. Each pill contains left-aligned label text and right-aligned small line icon.
- Bottom area: a lightweight text link “CUSTOM GOAL” centered, uppercase, small 12–14px, semi-opaque white.

UI elements specifics:
- Skip control top-right: small text button, 12–14px, weight 600, color rgba(255,255,255,0.65). Tap target 44px.
- Info (“i”) icon next to “Common goal”: 18–20px circular inline icon in a subtle frosted circle; tapping reveals a small tooltip or modal with explanation.
- Numeric goal (64oz): extremely prominent, white, large tracking/kern adjusted for visual balance. Include unit 'oz' as slightly smaller inline text to preserve hierarchy.
- Pills (Sex, Weight, Medium activity, Temperate): capsule-shaped controls, background a darker translucent teal (#048FAF approximated) when inactive, brighter cyan when active (#06CFE1-ish). Each pill contains a small white line icon on the right (smiley for sex, scale icon for weight, sneaker for activity, cloud/sun for climate). Pills should have subtle inner shadow (top light and bottom darker) or soft drop shadow (y-offset 4px, blur 12px, color rgba(0,0,0,0.08)) to lift them from the background.
- Icons: thin rounded stroke icons white or semi-opaque white, sized about 20–24px and vertically centered inside pill.

Interaction / states:
- Tapping a pill opens a modal or bottom sheet to pick the value (not shown) or toggles selection inline. Provide touch feedback: 0.06s scale down (0.98) and highlight overlay (rgba(255,255,255,0.06)).
- Info icon opens a short modal or tooltip with explanatory text; animate with fade + slide up (duration 220ms ease-out).
- The sheep illustration and ice shapes may have subtle parallax motion when user scrolls or tilts device: small vertical float animation (translateY ±6px) with ease-in-out, duration ~2.5s, infinite.

Accessibility:
- Ensure numeric contrast >= 4.5:1 vs background (use white for critical text). Provide accessible labels for pills and icons; hit areas >=44px.

Assets & metrics (example values for reproduction on a 375 x 812 artboard):
- Left/right margin: 24px; top safe area 44px; pill width approx 327px; pill height 64px; pill corner radius 36px; vertical gap between pills 16–20px; numeric block top margin ~64px from top safe area.

Animations:
- Micro-interactions: pill press scale 0.98 over 60ms, release spring back 160ms with ease-out. Tooltip fade/slide: 220ms ease-out (opacity 0→1, translateY 8px→0).
- Background decorative elements (ice) gentle bobbing/rotate over 3–6s with linear easing for subtle life.

This description provides enough detail for a product designer to recreate layout, style, and interaction for a similar onboarding/goal-calculation screen.
content.layout:
Overall layout: single-column, vertically stacked, centered composition.

Structure and groups (top to bottom):
1. Status/Header group (1 column): phone status area at the very top plus small "SKIP" text button aligned to the right (top-right). This is compact and occupies the safe-area.
2. Hero group (1 column): decorative illustration (sheep) positioned toward the upper-left of the hero area; centered title block containing a small caption "Common goal" with an info icon then a large numeric value "64oz" and a subtitle "Calculate your goal". All elements in this group are centered horizontally.
3. Controls group (1 column): a vertical stack of 4 capsule/pill items (Sex; Weight; Medium activity; Temperate). Each pill is full-width (approx ~82–88% of screen width), equal height, equal vertical spacing. Pills are visually grouped together with consistent spacing, forming a single column of input controls.
4. Footer/link group (1 column): a small centered text action "CUSTOM GOAL" sitting below the pill list; acts like a link or secondary action.

Columns and grids:
- Column count: 1 main column.
- No multi-column grids; no explicit use of rows-by-columns grid; pills are list-like stacked rows.
- Spacing rhythm: consistent vertical rhythm with comfortable breathing room between hero and control group; margins left/right are symmetric (approx 24px). Safe-area top padding accounts for status bar.

Layout keywords: centered single-column, stacked vertical rhythm, hero numeric, capsule controls, full-bleed background, safe-area aware, decorative illustration, equal-height pills, bottom action link, touch-friendly spacing.
content.functions:
Specific actions users can take on this screen:
- Tap "SKIP" to bypass the goal-calculation step and continue onboarding. The SKIP control sits in the top-right and provides immediate navigation away from the screen.
- Tap the small info "i" next to "Common goal" to open a short tooltip or modal that explains what the common goal means (e.g., "Default recommended daily intake based on average factors").
- Read the large numeric goal (e.g., "64oz") which communicates the immediate recommended value.
- Tap any of the pill controls (Sex, Weight, Medium activity, Temperate) to reveal a selection control (modal, picker, or inline options). These pill controls support: choosing sex (male/female/other), entering or selecting weight (numeric input or wheel picker), selecting activity level (low/medium/high), and selecting climate/temperature profile.
- Use the pill icons and labels as visual affordances; each pill shows current selection and opens the relevant selector when tapped.
- Tap the "CUSTOM GOAL" label to set an exact manual water goal rather than using the calculated one.
- The UI provides immediate visual feedback for selections (pill brightens when active/selected); pressing a pill shows short touch feedback (scale/overlay) and then opens the input.

Medium-level tasks and workflows:
- Complete the mini-questionnaire: choose sex → enter weight → select activity → select climate. Each choice updates the calculated numeric value (live recalculation or after closing each input). The UI is designed as a short interactive flow to reach a personalized goal quickly.
- Review the recommended common goal and compare against a custom goal. Users can accept the calculated value or choose to set a custom value.
- Skip the flow entirely if they prefer to configure goals later.

Broader purpose:
- The screen is an onboarding/initial-setup step whose main purpose is to provide users with a recommended daily water intake (goal) tailored by a few simple factors. It reduces friction to personalization by presenting one prominent value and four lightweight, easy-to-complete controls. The design encourages quick completion (large tappable pills, simple icons), clarity (big numeric hero), and delight (illustration and subtle animation). Ultimately, the user achieves a configured hydration goal that will be used elsewhere in the product (tracking, reminders, progress).

steps.name: Sex selection modal
steps.goal: Collect user's sex/condition to refine the recommendation.
steps.action: User taps the 'Sex' row, which opens a bottom-sheet list of options: Male, Female, Pregnant, Breastfeeding, Prefer not to say.
steps.system_response: A modal bottom-sheet slides up with selectable list items and small icons. A dismiss control (X) is visible. Selection will close the sheet and update the Sex row on the main screen.

content.description:
High-level overview
- Portrait mobile screen showing an onboarding step where a rounded white bottom sheet overlays a teal illustrated hero header. The hero area (top ~40% of screen) has a large numeric goal (“64oz”) centered, with a small label above it (“Common goal” + small info icon). The bottom sheet slides up and covers the lower ~60% of the screen and contains selectable rows (Male, Female, Pregnant, Breastfeeding, Prefer not to say), each a pill-shaped card with a left-aligned label and a right-aligned line-art icon. A circular close button with an X sits near the top-right of the sheet, overlapping slightly.

Colors
- Hero background / accent teal: #09738A (provided)
- Dark accent / icons / primary text: ~#2C3A40 (use for main labels) — approximate replacement for on-screen dark navy
- Secondary text / gray note: #9B9B9B (provided)
- White sheet background: #FFFFFF
- Row/pill background: very light gray / off-white: #F5F7F8
- Soft shadow for sheet: rgba(16,24,32,0.08)
- Small decorative/brand accents (from developer palette): #8C7404, #95851E, #382D23 (used subtly in illustrations or brand elements)

Typography
- System iOS font (SF Pro / San Francisco) recommended for faithful recreation.
- Hero large number (“64oz”): 110–140px, Heavy or Black weight (800–900), tight letter-spacing, center aligned, muted light tint (slightly desaturated on teal background) — in screenshot it appears large but slightly translucent/soft.
- Hero small label (“Common goal”): 16–18px, Medium (500–600), letter-spacing ~0.2px, center aligned, color: white with ~0.9 opacity or very light gray on teal.
- Row label text: 18–20px, Semibold (600), color #2C3A40 (dark navy), left aligned within row padding.
- Small privacy note text at sheet bottom: 13–14px, Regular (400), color #9B9B9B, center aligned.

Layout & spacing
- Full-screen container in portrait (375–430pt width typical). Safe area at top with status elements (9:41, signal icons). “SKIP” link sits top-right in hero area.
- Hero area: 1 column, centered content vertically within hero. Decorative illustrations (cloud, ice cubes) are positioned left and right behind text.
- Bottom sheet: anchored to bottom, full width minus safe area. Top corners large radius (32–36px). Sheet height ~55–65% of screen. Soft drop shadow around sheet.
- Internal sheet padding: 24px horizontal; top padding ~20–28px to allow rounded visual.
- List of options: vertical stack of 5 rows; each row is a full-width pill inside the sheet with internal horizontal padding ~20–24px and vertical padding ~18–22px. Spacing between rows: 14–18px. Each pill has border-radius ~20–24px and background #F5F7F8.
- Row internal layout: two logical columns — left column for label (auto width, left aligned), right column for icon (fixed width ~36px) with icons centered vertically. Row height approx 64px.
- Close icon: circular white button (48px diameter) with subtle shadow, positioned overlapping the right edge of the sheet’s curved top corner; X icon centered in it, stroke color dark gray ~#2C3A40.
- Privacy note sits below the last row with margin-top ~18–24px, horizontally centered.

Icons & imagery
- Row icons are line-art, rounded stroke (approx 2.5–3px) dark color (#2C3A40). They visually represent Male (face with glasses), Female (face/hairstyle), Pregnant (fetus/rounded belly), Breastfeeding (baby bottle icon), Prefer not to say (mystery / hat avatar). Icons sized ~28–36px square.
- Hero includes light, playful illustrations (clouds and ice cubes) with flat colors and simple shading — treated as decorative background elements behind the large number.

States & interaction cues
- Idle rows: pill background #F5F7F8, text #2C3A40, subtle inner shadow/emboss to create soft card look.
- Press / active row: use a slightly darker background tint (#E9EEF0) or apply 12–16% overlay, and optionally show a right-side checkmark or a left primary color accent. Use touch feedback: quick scale or opacity change.
- Disabled/secondary states (not present in screenshot): lower opacity and gray text.

Shadow & elevation
- Sheet elevation: soft, blurred shadow: 0 8px 24px rgba(16,24,32,0.08). Pill items have very subtle inner shadow to suggest pressable surface.

Animation
- Sheet entrance: slide-up from bottom with easing cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) or ease-out, duration 320–380ms. Slight overshoot bounce optional for more friendly feel.
- Row tap animation: 120ms background color fade and 80–120ms scale-to-0.99 micro-interaction.
- Icon animation: optional gentle pop or color change to indicate selection.

Accessibility
- Text sizes and contrast: keep pill text contrast >=4.5:1 against background. Use tappable target minimum 44x44pt for each row.

Recreation notes
- Recreate hero number in very large type and center it behind the sheet to match the partially-covered look. Reuse provided palette values for brand accents. Use circular close button overlapping the sheet and the row pill styles to match softness and rounded aesthetics.
content.layout:
Overall structure
- Single-column master layout across the full mobile viewport.
- Top area (hero) occupies ~35–45% of vertical space; contains centered typographic hero (two stacked typographic elements: small label + very large numeric). Decorative illustration elements are positioned around the hero text.
- Bottom sheet overlay occupies the remainder ~55–65% of the screen and is a single column container with internal vertical stack: repeated list rows and a small privacy text at the bottom.

Columns and groups
- Global grid: 1 column (full width).
- Bottom sheet internal content: 1 main column containing a vertical group of 5 identical rows (each row is a horizontal 2-column micro-layout inside the row):
  - Column A (left, flexible): label text aligned to left.
  - Column B (right, fixed ~36–44px): icon aligned to right.
- Close button exists as an overlapping floating element (not inside the main grid), aligned to the right/top of the sheet.

Rows & grid counts
- Rows: 5 rows stacked vertically.
- Each row is a card/tile spanning roughly 100% of the content width with rounded corners.
- Spacing: consistent vertical rhythm: top padding of sheet, then row, spacing, row, ... final privacy text.

Keywords to describe layout
- single-column
- bottom-sheet
- vertical-stack
- pill-cards
- overlapping-close
- hero-header
- centered-typography
- left-label-right-icon
- soft-shadow-elevation
- large-type-hero
content.functions:
Specific actions (micro-level)
- Tap a row to select an option (Male, Female, Pregnant, Breastfeeding, Prefer not to say). The row acts as a button; tapping reveals immediate visual feedback (highlight color) and records the selection.
- Tap the circular X button to dismiss the sheet and return to the underlying hero view.
- Tap the small info icon next to “Common goal” in the hero area to open a tooltip or modal that explains what the goal number means.
- Tap the “SKIP” text in the top-right of the hero to bypass the selection step.
- The sheet provides a privacy note; users can read assurance that their personal info won’t be collected or shared.

Medium-level tasks (workflows)
- Onboarding personalization: The user is guided to indicate gender/physiological state which is used to customize the product (e.g., calculate hydration goal). The sheet is part of a flow: Hero (present goal) -> open selection sheet -> choose option -> store preference locally (no account required) -> update displayed goal or proceed to next onboarding step.
- Quick decision flow: The design allows the user to choose quickly without navigating away — selection updates the app state and animates the sheet away.

High-level goal (why this screen exists)
- Personalize metrics: collect minimal profile data to generate a tailored “common goal” (64oz shown in hero). The screen balances clarity and privacy by making selection painless and showing a privacy assurance message.
- Smooth onboarding: The bottom sheet pattern keeps users in context (still seeing the goal number behind the sheet) to reduce friction and maintain continuity. It’s designed to capture a small piece of information that affects the app’s calculations while keeping the interaction quick and friendly.

steps.name: Sex selected (return)
steps.goal: Confirm and reflect the sex selection on the main screen.
steps.action: User taps an option (e.g., Male) in the bottom sheet.
steps.system_response: Modal closes and the 'Sex' row on the main screen updates to show the chosen option. The weight row remains highlighted indicating it may be the next input to set.

content.description:
Overall style: playful, friendly onboarding screen with a strong single-color brand background (bright turquoise) and rounded, soft UI components. Visual language is modern, flat, and minimal with large friendly typography and whimsical illustration (flying/rolling sheep and semi-transparent ice/rock shapes). The design uses heavy vertical rhythm, centered alignment and large negative space to focus attention on the main goal value.

Color palette (derived / approximated from screenshot):
- Primary background turquoise: #05BEDC (main screen fill)
- Secondary darker pill overlay: #0CA5B6 (darker teal for active/selected pill) or approx #06A9B5
- Very dark text / small UI: #080808 (for small status text like status bar and possibly top labels)
- Accent yellow (illustration highlight / subtle accents): #DDBF04
- Pale yellow highlight (decorative dot / sheep accent): #F8ED59
- White: #FFFFFF (major typography and icons)
- Muted overlay for disabled placeholder: rgba(8,8,8,0.12) (approx) used inside the "Weight" pill

Typography:
- Large numeric headline (64oz): a rounded geometric sans with high x‑height (e.g., Montserrat/Proxima Nova/Avenir Next Rounded). Weight: heavy/bold for the number. Approx sizes: headline number ~88–120px on a full‑height mobile canvas; smaller label above ~18–20px semi-bold; subheading "Calculate your goal" ~22–28px bold.
- Pill labels: medium weight (~18–20px), white text; placeholder text inside inactive pill uses reduced opacity white (~50%).
- All text is center aligned. Line spacing is generous — headline line-height ~0.9 for the large number (tight visually), other text ~1.2–1.4.

Layout & spacing:
- Full-screen portrait mobile layout, content vertically centered with top status area preserved. Safe-area top padding ~28–36px.
- Single column centered layout. Main vertical stack (top → bottom): small top info row ("Common goal" with info icon), very large numeric headline (64oz), subheading "Calculate your goal", a vertical stack of 4 pill selectors, and a bottom secondary link "CUSTOM GOAL".
- Pill buttons: four rounded capsule cards stacked with uniform vertical spacing (~18–28px gap). Each pill is full width with large horizontal padding and has an icon aligned to the right inside the pill. Pill height approx 64–84px, corner radius large (pill style) ~34–42px.
- The second pill (Weight) visually appears selected/active using a darker teal overlay and slightly depressed look (darker fill and subtle inner shadow). Other pills use the primary turquoise with slight elevation.
- Decorative illustration elements (ice/rocks) are positioned asymmetrically left/right behind the content with low opacity and soft edges. A sheep illustration sits near the top-right, overlapping the hero area, giving motion/whimsy.

UI elements & states:
- Skip action: small top-right text button labeled "SKIP" in semi-opaque white or muted turquoise — tappable.
- Info icon next to "Common goal": small circular icon; tapping would open a tooltip or small modal explaining how the common goal is calculated.
- Numeric headline: large, tappable? not necessary; static display of calculated common goal.
- Each pill is a tappable selection control: shows label text on left, a small line icon on the right. On tap the pill becomes the darker selected state and probably opens a sub‑screen or modal (e.g., Weight opens numeric input). The Weight pill visually shows placeholder text "Weight" in lighter tone, implying an input/selection step.
- Bottom link "CUSTOM GOAL" is a subtle uppercase link, lower contrast, centered — secondary action.

Iconography & illustration:
- Simple line icons inside pills (gender/male icon, weight scale, running shoe, weather/cloud) rendered in white outlines.
- Illustration style: flat-vector with slight shading and playful shapes.

Microinteractions & animation (recommended and implied):
- Sheep gently floating/hovering with a slow up/down loop (duration ~4–6s, ease-in-out), small parallax relative to scroll.
- Pill selection transitions: smooth background color fade + scale/press effect (scale to 0.98, 120–180ms, ease-out) and brief drop shadow change.
- Info icon opens a small popover with fade+slide (120–200ms, cubic-bezier(.22,.9,.3,1)).

Accessibility notes:
- High contrast between headline and background (white on turquoise). Ensure pill labels have sufficient contrast; active pill must meet WCAG AA for interactive controls. Hit targets for pills at least 44x44px.

Assets / export guidance:
- Export sheep and ice shapes as SVGs with separate layers for parallax animation. Provide 2 states for icons: normal (white) and disabled/placeholder (white at 50% opacity). Provide mask for safe area at top (status bar).
content.layout:
Screen layout: single-column vertical stack, centered alignment. Count of columns: 1.

Structure from top to bottom:
- Top safe-area / status bar (time and device indicators). A small right-aligned control: "SKIP" (text button).
- Decorative area (top third) with background illustration (sheep and floating shapes). This area visually flows into the main content via a soft curved or wavy top edge.
- Main content block (centered vertically):
  - Small label row: "Common goal" + info icon centered.
  - Large numeric headline (64oz) centered, taking most horizontal space.
  - Subheading: "Calculate your goal" centered below the headline.
  - Selection stack: vertical group of 4 pill-shaped selection controls. These are grouped as a single column of cards/tiles with even vertical spacing. Each pill is full-width (within horizontal padding), with rounded ends.
  - Secondary action at bottom: "CUSTOM GOAL" centered and spaced from the pills with increased margin.

Grid and spacing details:
- No multi-column grid; a single-column flow with consistent horizontal inset (approx 16–24px safe margin on each side on smaller screens, but pills appear visually full-bleed to edges with internal padding). The pill stack forms a group (treated as one visual block) with equal spacing between each pill.
- Visual hierarchy is established by scale (very large number, medium-size subhead, medium pills) and by color contrast (pills and background).
content.functions:
Specific actions users can perform on this screen:
- Read the "Common goal" numeric value (64oz) displayed prominently.
- Tap the info (i) icon next to "Common goal" to open a small explanation popover or tooltip about how the common goal was derived.
- Tap any of the pill controls to select or edit that attribute: "Male" (gender selection), "Weight" (opens a numeric input or selection modal), "Medium activity" (choose activity level), "Temperate" (choose climate). Each pill provides visual feedback on tap (color change, slight scale) and may navigate to a more detailed selector or inline picker.
- Tap "SKIP" in the top-right to bypass this step and proceed (likely to main app or next onboarding step).
- Tap "CUSTOM GOAL" at the bottom to set a manual/custom hydration target instead of using the calculated common goal.

Medium-level workflows:
- A user can configure their personal hydration parameters by tapping through the four pills in sequence (gender → weight → activity → climate), entering or selecting values. After configuring, the common goal updates to reflect the inputs.
- If the user wants a specific target not suggested, they can choose "CUSTOM GOAL" to override the calculated value and set a fixed daily target.
- The info popover provides context; the skip action allows moving forward quickly without configuring values.

Broader purpose / user goal:
- The screen is an onboarding / setup step that helps users discover or calculate a daily hydration goal (in ounces) by gathering minimal personal info. It balances rapid conversion (showing a default common goal) with the option for personalization (pill selectors and custom goal). The design reduces friction by keeping interactions simple (large tappable pills), presenting a clear numeric goal, and providing contextual help and escape (skip) to ensure users can continue even if they don’t finish setup. The result: user obtains a hydration target and proceeds with the app's tracking or reminders features.

steps.name: Weight picker modal
steps.goal: Collect user's weight using a wheel-style picker so the calculation can be personalized.
steps.action: User taps the 'Weight' row which opens a modal containing a numeric wheel picker (kg/lbs) and a prominent 'DONE' button.
steps.system_response: A white bottom-card with a wheel picker appears. The user can spin/select a weight (example 183 lbs). A privacy note is shown below. Tapping 'DONE' closes the picker and saves the weight.

content.description:
Overall composition
- Full-screen mobile onboarding/goal screen with a strong teal hero occupying the top half and a white rounded bottom sheet (modal) that slides up from the bottom to collect user input.
- The status bar (time, signal, battery) is visible at the very top overlaying a thin neutral header area.
- Background (hero) contains a large numeric KPI (“64oz”) centered vertically in the teal area, a small muted label above it (“Common goal” with a small info icon) and a subtitle below (“Calculate your goal”). Decorative flat illustrations (cloud, ice-cubes) appear at the left and right edges of the teal area as subtle visual interest.

Bottom sheet / modal
- A white bottom sheet sits on top of the hero, clipped with large top-left and top-right radii (approx. 24–32 px) and a prominent soft shadow. It covers roughly 50–60% of the screen height.
- The modal header is minimalist: a centered title “Weight” (bold) and a circular elevated close button (44 x 44 px) overlapping the top-right corner of the sheet. The close button is a circular white surface with a subtle drop shadow and a dark “X” icon centered inside.
- Under the title is a vertical wheel-style picker for weight selection. The wheel visually shows multiple numeric rows (one above, one selected, one below) with the selected row highlighted by a rounded capsule/pill background.
- The wheel area looks like two aligned columns: the numeric column (e.g., 182, 183, 184) and a small units column (kg / lbs). The selected row’s capsule spans both columns, creating a single combined selected state (pill) with a light bluish background and turquoise text for the selected values.
- Below the wheel is a small muted privacy note: “Your personal information won’t be collected or shared” — centered, very light gray, small caption size.
- The primary CTA is a large dark rounded pill button labeled “DONE” centered horizontally near the bottom of the sheet. It has strong contrast (white uppercase text on a dark charcoal/blue background), generous vertical padding and a high corner radius.

Typography (suggested to replicate)
- Display numeric (hero): large geometric sans, heavy weight. Approx sizes for a modern 375px-wide mobile canvas: hero numeric ~110–140 px (large, light weight for the numerals), letter/number spacing slightly condensed.
- Hero subtitle (“Calculate your goal”): medium/semibold geometric sans, ~24–32 px.
- Modal title (“Weight”): geometric sans, ~28–32 px, semi-bold or bold; center aligned.
- Wheel numbers: medium sans ~24–36 px for selected item (selected item heavier weight and full-color), surrounding non-selected items lighter weight and lower opacity.
- Privacy note: small sans, ~12–14 px, light gray.
- CTA button: uppercase label, ~16–18 px, bold.
- Recommended font family style: rounded geometric sans (e.g., Poppins, Circular, or Nunito) to achieve the friendly, rounded letterforms visible in the screenshot.

Color palette (main colors and usage)
- Teal hero background: #097188 (developer-provided 0x097188) — used for the top half background and for primary accent text in selected wheel rows.
- Primary accent / warm accents: #8C7404 and #9A8A22 (developer-provided) — subtle accents in illustration or micro-graphics (not dominant), can be used for small highlights or icons.
- Neutral mid-gray (muted text): #9B9B9B (developer-provided) — used for privacy note, small hint text, and inactive wheel values.
- Dark charcoal (CTA button background and primary dark text): #403122 (developer-provided) — used for the “DONE” button background, X icon color, and some headings if heavy contrast needed.
- White modal surface: #FFFFFF — bottom sheet background and pill backgrounds for selected wheel row (or a very light bluish tint).
- Selected wheel capsule background: very light blue/teal tint — approximated as #F0FBFD (use for subtle elevation of the selected row).
- Info icon (small circular) and other accents: slightly desaturated teal or light gray, e.g., #CFEFF2 for subtleness.

UI elements styling details
- Bottom sheet corner radius: ~24–32 px (large rounded corners).
- Modal shadow: soft, spread ~12 px, blur ~24 px, color rgba(16, 24, 32, 0.12).
- Close circle: 44 x 44 px, border-radius 50%, drop shadow (y-offset 6 px, blur 12 px, rgba(16,24,32,0.12)). X icon ~18–20 px dark color (#403122).
- Wheel picker: visible height ~120–160 px; single selected row height ~56–72 px; surrounding numbers partly visible above and below with ~40–60% opacity. Selected row pill inset padding ~18 px horizontal, border-radius ~28 px. Selected numeric color: teal #097188; non-selected numeric color: #9B9B9B at 40–60% opacity.
- CTA button: width ~160–220 px (or 56–65% of sheet width), height ~56 px, border-radius ~28 px, background #403122, white uppercase label, slight inner shadow to make it tactile.
- Spacing/padding: modal side padding ~20–28 px; vertical spacing between title and wheel ~16–28 px; between wheel and privacy note ~20–28 px; between privacy note and CTA ~30–40 px.

States & micro-interactions
- Wheel interaction: vertical drag inertia, snap-to-item; selected row animates into place with easing. During scroll, opacity and scale change: selected row scales up slightly (~1.05x) and non-selected rows scale down (~0.95x) and fade.
- Sheet transitions: modal enters with a smooth upward slide with spring easing (duration ~360–420ms, cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)). Dismiss/close animates sheet down off-screen.
- Close button: circular press ripple or subtle scale down (0.96) with 120–160ms duration.
- CTA press: quick darkening overlay and scale down (0.98) to indicate tap, then success state leads to sheet dismissal and hero update.

Visual style summary
- Friendly, modern onboarding visual language: large numeric hero, playful flat illustrations, and a soft, rounded modal surface. The UI balances bright teal brand color with neutral greys and a strong dark CTA to focus final action. Use of large type, generous spacing, and the wheel control gives a tactile, approachable interaction.
content.layout:
Overall layout (high-level)
- Single-column mobile layout for main content with an anchored bottom sheet. The screen is vertically stacked: status bar → hero (teal) centered content → bottom sheet overlay with form elements.

Hero area
- Height: approx top 45–55% of the canvas. Centralized alignment: vertical centered stack containing (from top to bottom) a small label + info icon, a very large numeric value (64oz), and a subtitle.
- Illustrations placed left and right, partially cropped (decorative) and visually behind the modal.

Bottom sheet / modal layout details
- The sheet acts as a single vertical column with the following groups from top to bottom:
  1) Header row (centered title) — includes an overlapping circular close control aligned to the top-right edge of the sheet (this is a separate floating group above the content column).
  2) Picker group — horizontally centered wheel picker that visually contains two logical columns (weight values and units). The visual focus is a single highlighted row (capsule) that spans both columns.
  3) Small caption row — centered privacy text beneath the picker.
  4) CTA group — centered, primary rounded pill button.

Column / grid counts
- Main layout columns: 1 primary content column.
- Inside the wheel picker: 2 logical columns (numeric column + unit column). Each behaves as an independent vertical list but visually joined by the pill highlight.

Spacing & alignment keywords
- Centered alignment for major elements, large vertical spacing between hero text and sheet, generous side padding in sheet (approx 20–28 px). The overall layout emphasizes a vertical, single-flow interaction with a strong central axis.
content.functions:
Specific actions (what users can do on this screen)
- Tap and drag the wheel picker to change the weight number; wheel snaps to discrete integer steps (e.g., 182, 183, 184).
- Tap the units column (kg or lbs) to switch units; the selected unit is shown inside the highlighted pill.
- Tap the circular X in the top-right to close/dismiss the bottom sheet without saving.
- Tap the DONE button to confirm the selected weight and close the modal (potentially returning the chosen value to the hero or next onboarding step).
- Tap the small info icon near “Common goal” in the hero to see contextual help or an explanation tooltip about how the common goal was calculated.
- Tap SKIP in the top-right of the hero to bypass this step of onboarding.

Medium-level workflows
- Onboarding step workflow: user opens the app’s onboarding, the app presents an initial common goal (64 oz) and then asks for personal details to calculate a tailored goal. The user provides weight using the wheel picker, confirms with DONE, and the app updates the target value accordingly.
- Unit conversion workflow: user toggles units (kg ↔ lbs) and wheel values update to the corresponding numeric range appropriate for the selected unit, preserving the selected item when possible.
- Dismiss/Ignore flow: user can either close the sheet with X (no change) or skip the entire onboarding step from the hero SKIP action.

Broader purpose / primary goal achieved via this screen
- Purpose: gather a single personal metric (weight) during onboarding to calculate a personalized water intake goal. The modal’s focused layout reduces friction and errors by exposing only the weight selection control and a clear confirmation CTA.
- How it facilitates that goal: large readable typography (for the current water goal), tactile wheel control (easy single-handed selection on mobile), unit toggle to ensure internationalization, prominent Done CTA for a clear next step, and a privacy reassurance line to increase user trust and completion rate.

content.description:
This is a single-screen mobile onboarding / personalization screen that helps the user set a daily hydration goal. Overall style: playful, friendly, and modern with heavy use of large, rounded shapes, soft shadows and a mascot illustration (a small fluffy sheep) floating above the main content. The visual language favors rounded corners, generous vertical spacing, and clean, geometric sans-serif typography. The layout is vertically stacked and centered, with a large numeric hero value near the top and a column of pill-shaped selection cards below.

Color palette (primary and accents):
- Primary teal / aqua background: #06C2DF (main background color filling most of the screen)
- Secondary bright yellow accents: #EBDA21 and #DEC004 (used for small highlights and accent shapes)
- Dark gray / almost black for small UI elements (DONE button outline/shadow): #2B271C
- Very light off-white for status bar / bezel area: #F5F6F0
- White for main text and icons: #FFFFFF
- Slightly translucent / lighter teal for overlay shapes and pill cards: approximate #24D4E6 (tint of #06C2DF)

Background: a solid or very subtle linear gradient in the aqua/cyan family (dominant #06C2DF); floating semi-transparent decorative blobs and ice-cube like illustrations are scattered around the left and right edges as visual texture. A small sheep illustration sits above the hero number, slightly overlapping it and implying motion. Small circular dots and soft shapes create depth.

Typography:
- Typeface: geometric sans-serif (round, friendly). Use a heavy-weight display for large numbers and medium weights for labels. Examples: Montserrat / Poppins / Avenir-like.
- Large numeric hero (the hydration goal): very large display numerals, white, thin-to-regular stroke weight but visually bold due to scale. Approx sizes: 96–140pt depending on device scale (on 375pt wide mobile, number height ~220px). Line height tight to visually group digits. Letter spacing slightly negative to tighten.
- Subhead / descriptor (“Your hydration goal”): white, medium weight (600), ~18–24pt, centered, 1.2 line height.
- Small helper label above number (“Recommended goal”) light white at 60–70% opacity, smaller ~12–14pt, with a small info icon to its right.
- Pill card labels: white, medium 16–20pt, centered vertically within each pill. Icons inside pills are white-outlined stroke icons sized ~22–28px.
- “CUSTOM GOAL” CTA near the bottom: uppercase, lighter weight, semi-transparent white (opacity ~45–60%), ~14–16pt.

UI elements & styles:
- Top status area: system status bar visible at top with battery/Wi-Fi and left time in dark text on a very light background (#F5F6F0) occupying a small curved white bezel area.
- DONE control: small rounded capsule button in the top-right, dark desaturated color (#2B271C or deep charcoal) with white uppercase text “DONE”. Button has subtle inner/outer shadow to lift it from background; corner radius ~20–26px, padding ~12–16px horizontally.
- Hero number block: very large, center-aligned numeric value (example “87.6 oz”) in white. Slight drop shadow or subtle keyline to ensure legibility over decorative shapes.
- Info label: above the number a faint caption reads “Recommended goal” with a small circular info icon (white outline) to the right; this element likely has reduced opacity to be unobtrusive.
- Pill-shaped selection cards (stack of 4): centered vertical stack of large rounded capsules with strong border radius (pill radius ~half of height). Each pill is a slightly lighter tint of the background (semi-opaque white or lighter teal), full width at around 80–86% of screen width, height approximately 56–78px depending on device density. Spacing between pills ~18–26px. Each pill contains a left-aligned label (e.g., “Male”, “183 lbs”, “Medium activity”, “Warm”) and a right-aligned circular or inline outlined white icon (face / scale / sneaker / sun) with about 18–28px icon size. Pills have a very soft inner shadow or subtle elevation to separate them from the background.
- Decorative imagery: playful sheep illustration overlaps hero area; translucent teal “splash” shapes partly obscure the numeric value as a playful, animated feel. Ice-cube shapes appear near left and right edges.
- CTA / secondary action: “CUSTOM GOAL” text link centered below pills in a lighter, semi-opaque white — small and tappable. It’s separated from pills by a larger vertical gap to indicate a secondary action.

States & affordances:
- Each pill acts like a large tap target; on tap it likely opens a selector or modal to edit that value. Visual pressed state: pill darkens slightly (decreased brightness) and icon may shift to filled variant. Default state: pills are solid lighter-teal with white text and icon.
- Info icon near “Recommended goal” presumably opens a small tooltip or modal with explanation.
- DONE button confirms selection and advances the flow.

Micro-interactions and animation (observed or implied):
- Mascot (sheep) probably has a subtle floating or bouncing animation loop (gentle vertical bob, 300–700ms easing with slow sinusoidal easing) to add personality.
- Decorative splashes could move or appear in a staggered fade-in as the screen loads. Hero number may animate from 0 to the target value (count-up animation) with ease-out timing (~900–1200ms) to draw attention.
- Pills might animate upwards from the bottom with a small overshoot (spring easing) when entering the screen.

Layout measurements & spacing (approx, in pixels for a typical 375pt wide mobile):
- Screen padding left/right: ~16–20px.
- Hero number width: ~80% of screen width, centered.
- Pill width: ~86% of screen width, height ~68px, corner radius ~34px.
- Vertical spacing: hero to first pill ~40–56px; inter-pill gap ~18–22px; pills to CUSTOM GOAL ~48–72px.

Accessibility considerations:
- High contrast white-on-teal for primary text; ensure numeric hero is readable over decorative elements (use drop shadow or semi-opaque overlay behind digits if necessary).
- Pills are large touch targets (~44–68px tall) and contain clear iconography plus text; ensure scalable fonts and proper dynamic type support.

Overall this screen is a friendly, vibrant onboarding personalization screen that uses a big numeric hero, stacked rounded selection cards, playful illustrations and a single confirm control to finish.
content.layout:
Overall layout: single-column, vertically stacked center-aligned composition. The screen is split into logical vertical groups from top to bottom:
1) System status area (very small band at the top with device time and icons) inside a light bezel.
2) Top-right action capsule (DONE) floating within the top safe area.
3) Large hero block centered horizontally containing an optional small caption line ("Recommended goal" + info icon) and the large numeric value (the hydration goal) with a small descriptive line below ("Your hydration goal"). This hero group is visually dominant and sits in the upper third of the screen.
4) Middle content: a single column of 4 rounded pill-shaped selection cards (stacked vertically, equal width, equal spacing). Each pill is a horizontal group with left-aligned label text and right-aligned icon.
5) Lower area: secondary text action "CUSTOM GOAL" centered and visually de-emphasized. Below that is the lower background space with decorative elements.

Columns / groups: exactly 1 main column. The vertical column contains 5 groups (status + done, hero, pill stack group with 4 items, custom goal link, decorative footer). The pill stack itself is a single column group with 4 homogeneous rows (each pill = 1 row).

Grid: there is no explicit multi-column grid; the design relies on a centered single-column rhythm. The pill stack forms a 4-row list grid (1 column x 4 rows).

Alignment and spacing: all elements are center-aligned horizontally with consistent left/right padding. The pills are centered and share identical widths and corner radii. Visual rhythm uses consistent vertical gaps between major groups (hero to pills larger gap; between pills smaller consistent gap). Decorative elements (ice-cubes, blobs, sheep) are positioned asymmetrically at left/right edges but do not interfere with the interaction area.

Keywords to describe layout and composition: vertical stack, single column, centered alignment, pill cards, large hero, floating action, safe-area aware, symmetric margins, stacked rows, decorative illustration.
content.functions:
Specific actions users can perform on this screen:

- Tap an individual rounded pill (Male / 183 lbs / Medium activity / Warm) to open a control for changing that specific value (e.g., a picker modal, dropdown, or another screen). The pills are large tap targets with right-side icons that visually hint at the type of value (gender icon, scale icon, shoe icon, sun icon).
- Tap the small info icon next to “Recommended goal” to view more information about how the recommended hydration target was calculated (tooltip or modal). This provides contextual help.

Medium-level tasks (workflows combining actions):

content.description:

- Pill surfaces (lighter turquoise): #2FE0EA (or same hue at +6% lightness)

content.description:
This screen is a mobile modal overlay (bottom sheet) used for entering a numeric custom goal. A rounded white sheet slides up from the bottom and covers ~60% of the screen height. The top area of the sheet has large centered numeric input reading “87.6 oz” (the unit “oz” sits to the right of the number). A vertical caret appears between digits indicating an editable text input. Directly under the number is a small sublabel “Custom goal” in medium-weight text. Below that is a large pill-shaped primary action button labeled “DONE” in all-caps. The button is a dark navy/charcoal rounded capsule with bold white text and a subtle inner shadow.

In the sheet’s top-right corner is a circular close button (white round circle with a dark “X” icon) that floats slightly above the sheet edge with a soft drop shadow. Behind the sheet the main app background is visible: a teal/blue illustrated scene with a small sheep illustration in the upper right and faint partially-obscured text (“Recommended goal”) centered behind the sheet. The phone status bar (time, signal/wifi/battery) is visible above the background.

The bottom portion of the screen contains a full-width numeric keypad (on-screen keyboard) in a light gray background. Keys are rounded rectangles arranged in a 3-column grid: rows 1–3 contain digits 1–9, the fourth row contains dot, 0, and backspace. Each key is a white rounded pill with a subtle border and drop shadow. The digit is large and centered; small uppercase letter groupings (ABC, DEF, etc.) are shown below each digit in a condensed small font. The backspace key shows an outlined delete icon. The keypad area has a slightly darker rounded top corner treatment aligning with the sheet.

Style and visual language: modern, soft, friendly and minimal. Plenty of white space, centered content, large typography for primary numeric input, clear visual hierarchy (number > sublabel > primary action). Rounded corners everywhere and soft shadows create depth.

Color palette (primary approximate values):
- Sheet background: pure white #FFFFFF
- App background / illustration teal: #205B64 (user-supplied)
- Primary button / dark text: #171310 (user-supplied; used for button background and large text)
- Keyboard background / subtle surface gray: #E9E9EB (derived from provided neutral #999896)
- Key background: #FFFFFF with a faint border #E1E1E4
- Secondary gray text (sublabel, letter hints): #999896 (user-supplied)
- Accent / decorative (from provided palette but not heavily used): #8B7304 and #928543 (can be used for subtle icon accents or states)

Typography (recommended to match the screenshot):
- Font family: San Francisco / SF Pro Display (system iOS)
- Numeric input: ~72–84px, weight 700 (heavy/bold), center aligned, line-height 1.0
- Unit (“oz”): ~28–36px, weight 600, baseline-aligned to the number
- Sublabel (“Custom goal”): 14–16px, weight 500, color #999896, center aligned
- Primary button text: 18–20px, weight 700, uppercase, color #FFFFFF
- Key digits: 26–32px, weight 600, color #171310
- Key letters (ABC): 10–12px, weight 500, uppercase, color #999896

Spacing and sizing (approximate):
- Sheet top padding: 28–36px
- Space between numeric input and sublabel: 8–12px
- Space between sublabel and DONE button: 24–32px
- Primary button size: approx 160px wide x 56–64px tall, border-radius 32px
- Close button diameter: 44–52px, positioned 16–20px from sheet right edge and visually overlapping the sheet’s rounding
- Keyboard area height: ~320px (standard mobile numeric keypad height), keys arranged in 4 rows x 3 columns
- Key size: approx 86px wide x 64px tall with 12–16px gaps and 12–16px corner radius

States & interactions:
- Primary button default: dark navy background with subtle inset/outer shadow. Press/active: 0.96 scale and slightly darker background (#0F0D0B or 10% darker). Disabled state: light gray background with text in #999896.
- Keys: default white key with subtle shadow; on press, key darkens slightly and shows a short 80–120ms ripple/scale. Backspace shows pressed state tint.
- Close button: on tap it dismisses the modal. Primary DONE button saves and dismisses the sheet.

Micro-interactions & animation:
- Sheet entrance/exit: slide up/down with easing cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) and duration ~300ms. The background slightly dims (~20% dark overlay) during sheet open.
- Caret blink: 1s step-start/step-end blink animation for the numeric caret.
- Key press: brief scale-down (0.97) and opacity change, duration ~100–120ms, easing ease-out.

Accessibility notes:
- Numeric input large and high-contrast. Ensure sufficient color contrast for primary button text. Provide alternative labels for the close/backspace icons, and ensure keyboard input is reachable and usable with assistive technologies.

- Quick corrections: use the keypad for rapid entry and the backspace to quickly fix mistyped digits.
- Modal dismissal options: close via X for cancel, or confirm/save via DONE. The modal also likely supports tapping outside the sheet to dismiss (if implemented).

Broader purpose and user goal:
- The overall purpose of this interface is to let the user set or edit a personalized numeric goal (likely a water-intake goal in ounces). The interface facilitates this by making number entry the single focused task: large readable numeric field, dedicated numeric keypad, and a single clear primary action to save. Visual hierarchy, spacing, and direct affordances (keys, delete, done) keep the flow quick and low-friction so users can set goals with minimal cognitive load. The modal pattern keeps the context (illustrated background) visible so users understand the setting while focusing on the numeric input.

content.description:
Overview
- Full-screen mobile onboarding/customization screen that asks the user to set a hydration target. Visual style is playful and friendly with a turquoise/aqua background, light illustrations (a floating sheep and ice-cube shapes), and large, rounded UI controls.

Background
- Solid turquoise/aqua background (primary color) with subtle decorative illustrations: a small sheep illustration near the top-left, semi-transparent ice/rock shapes on left and right edges, and tiny circular particle dots scattered. The background uses a single flat turquoise tone with slightly darker/lighter illustrative shapes to create depth.
- Main hex palette (provided): primary aqua #05B8D7, pale off-white #F8F9F9 for top status area and small accents, accent yellow/gold #DBBC04 / #C3A404 used sparingly for icons/accents, and dark text color #2B271C.

Header
- iOS status indicators at the very top (time left, cellular/wifi/battery) on a narrow white status bar area.
- Top-right a rounded, elevated “DONE” pill button: dark navy/dark-brown fill (close to #2B271C but slightly desaturated), inner label “DONE” in all-caps white, pill has a subtle shadow; approximate size 64x36 px on iPhone-scale; border-radius ~18px. This button floats above the primary content aligned to the right with 16–20 px margin from top and right edges.

Hero / Center content
- Large numeric headline centered vertically: “90oz” — this is the visual focal point. Type is a rounded geometric sans (friendly, humanist) with a very large size (approx. 72–110 px depending on device), medium-heavy weight (approx. 600–700). Color: pure white (#FFFFFF) or very light off-white for contrast against aqua.
- Above number, small label “Custom goal” (subtle, lowercase/ sentence case) in a light weight with an info icon to its right. Color: very pale aqua or 80% white (approx. rgba(255,255,255,0.85)). Size approx 14–16 px.
- Below numeric headline, supporting subtitle “Your hydration goal” in a rounded sans, medium weight, white, size ~18–22 px, centered.

Controls / Inputs
- Four large full-width rounded pill controls stacked vertically below the hero. Each pill is a semi-opaque darker aqua (a slightly darker shade of the background to create the appearance of inset buttons). Pill dimensions: full width with horizontal padding ~28–36 px, height ~56–64 px, border-radius ~32 px (very rounded). Spacing between pills ~16–20 px.
- Each pill contains left-aligned label (e.g., “Sex”, “Weight”, “Daily Activity”, “Weather”) in a lighter semi-opaque white text (~16–18 px, medium weight). On the far right of each pill is a small line-style icon representing the field (smiley/sex, scale for weight, sneaker for activity, cloud for weather). Icons are stroke icons, about 20–24 px square, stroke weight ~1.5–2 px, colored slightly lighter than the pill fill (near-white with reduced opacity) or matching the gold accent for emphasis for one state.
- Pills look like selectable controls; current visual state shows them as inactive with soft inset shadow; selected/active states would shift to a brighter outline or a slightly elevated look.

Footer / Secondary action
- Small, centered text near the bottom: “CUSTOM GOAL” in uppercase, light weight, small size (~12–14 px), colored pale white with slightly higher transparency to indicate a secondary action; this likely acts as a manual override link.

Spacing & Alignment
- Overall layout is single column, vertically centered hero and stacked controls beneath. Left and right decorative illustrations live in the gutter areas allowing central content to remain clear and readable.
- Horizontal padding: ~18–24 px safe area on each side. Top safe area increases to include the status bar.

Typography
- Type family: rounded geometric sans (suggested: Nunito, Poppins, or Avenir Next Rounded). Use rounded corners and soft curves to match illustration style.
- Suggested sizes (phone reference): small label 14–16 px (300–400 line-height), section subtitle 18–22 px (line-height 26–30 px), hero numeric 72–110 px (tight line-height, 0.9–1.0), pill labels 16–18 px.
- Weights: small label 400–500, subheader 600, numeric 600–700.

Colors (suggested exact values)
- Background aqua: #05B8D7 (primary)
- Accent light off-white / status area: #F8F9F9
- Accent yellow/gold: #DBBC04 and #C3A404 (use sparingly for icon highlights or micro-animations)
- Dark text / CTA: #2B271C (used for dark buttons or high-contrast elements like DONE)
- Pill controls: darker aqua fill: rgba(12,135,150,0.15) on top of primary aqua (or a 10–18% darker variant of #05B8D7). Pill text: rgba(255,255,255,0.9).

Iconography
- Thin stroke icons inside each pill, single-color (white with 70–90% opacity) and sized ~20–24 px. Use friendly, rounded strokes to match overall aesthetic.

Shadows & Depth
- Subtle soft drop shadow under the DONE pill and slight inner shadow on the pill controls to create a pressed/inset look. Shadows are very soft: rgba(0,0,0,0.12), blur 8–12 px, y-offset 2–4 px.

Interactions & Animations
- Pill tap: quick scale-down (0.98) with 120 ms ease-out, then light elevation change or color brightening. Selected pill expands slightly to show selection or reveals a modal/selector.
- DONE: when active, micro-interaction: ripple or quick color shift to indicate save. Easing: cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) for lively feel.

Accessibility

Notes for replication
- Use a non-photorealistic, vector illustration style for the sheep and ice cubes; keep them light and slightly desaturated so they don’t compete with the central text. Keep the central numeric content perfectly centered and scale responsively.

- Save/finish: tapping the top-right DONE button persists the selected/custom goal and exits this flow.
- Manual override: tapping the “CUSTOM GOAL” text at the bottom likely opens a numeric input to set a custom oz value directly.
- Access info: tapping the small info icon adjacent to “Custom goal” will show clarification/help text describing how the goal is computed.

Medium-level workflows
- Goal personalization: user moves through one or multiple pill controls, adjusting sex, weight, activity level, and weather conditions. Each parameter either opens a compact selector (wheel or sheet) or pushes a detail screen where the user picks options; the main screen updates the large numeric hero in real time.
- Quick finish: a user can accept the computed number if satisfied and hit DONE to save; or they can choose CUSTOM GOAL to manually set a number.
- Lightweight preview: as the user adjusts inputs, subtle animations and number transitions (animated count) show how the goal changes.

Broader purpose / outcome
- Primary purpose: let the user configure and confirm a personalized daily hydration goal. This screen is part of onboarding or settings where the app calculates recommended water intake from several input factors.
- UX goals: clarity (single prominent number), easy exploration of contributing factors (stacked labeled pills), and a fast save/confirm action (DONE). The design emphasizes quick comprehension and low-effort personalization while retaining a playful, friendly brand tone.

records.name: Subscription Checkout & Confirmation
records.description: A single-screen subscription purchase sheet that presents two pricing options (one-time lifetime purchase vs. a 3‑day free trial leading to an annual subscription), additional marketing content (awards, features, reviews) and a persistent CTA. Entry point: user opens the subscription/premium upsell. Exit points: purchase confirmed (success alert) or modal closed. Assumptions: user is on iOS, within the product and not on a platform-level App Store purchase screen when they first see the upsell. The primary call-to-action uses the platform purchase flow (Apple Pay / App Store confirmation).
records.problem: User goal: choose a pricing option (one-time lifetime purchase or free-trial subscription) and complete a purchase or trial enrollment. From the user's perspective they want clear pricing, trial details, and an easy way to start the trial or buy once. They expect to read benefits/awards and reviews before committing, and to use native payment confirmation to finish. From the interface perspective the UI: - Presents two selectable pricing cards (lifetime vs. free-trial) with clear prices and callouts. - Keeps a large, prominent CTA visible as the user scrolls through supporting content (awards, features, reviews). - Uses the platform (Apple) purchase sheet for final confirmation and side-button authentication. Result: user-perceived outcome is a completed subscription/trial enrollment with a confirmation message. System-level outcome (visible in UI): Apple payment sheet shown and then a success confirmation alert; modal returns to app content after the alert.

content.description:
Overall style: A friendly, colorful mobile paywall / subscription modal with playful illustration, strong visual hierarchy and generous white space. Visual language uses rounded shapes, soft shadows, bright accent colors and a modern rounded sans type (similar to SF Pro / Inter / Poppins). Layout is vertically stacked, center-aligned, single-column mobile composition with segmented content blocks.

Color palette (use given brand colors):
- Dark navy / CTA background: #3E3227 (use for main CTA background or deep text — provided as main color)
- Accent orange: #CC441E (used for small accent text and strike-through original price)
- Accent yellow: #E4C810 (used in award medal)
- Cyan / Teal bright: #45D9EA (used for primary selected pricing card background and headline price text)
- Indigo / Blue: #413FDF (can be used for decorative shapes or secondary illustrations)
- Light background: #FAFBFB or #FFFFFF (page background)
- Pale cyan card background: rgba(69,217,234,0.12) / #E8FBFF (for secondary pricing option background)
- Pink promo ribbon: #FF3B9E (approx) with white text.

Typography:
- H1 (hero): font-family: SF Pro / Inter / Poppins; weight: 700; size: 24-28px; line-height: 32px; color: #222 (dark, high contrast); center-aligned.
- Lead / small headline (orange check line): font-weight: 600; size: 14px; color: #CC441E; letter-spacing: 0.2px; centered; includes a small check icon left.
- Pricing title inside cards: weight: 600-700; size: 18-20px; color: white on teal card; color: #057078 (or #045A63) on pale card.
- Secondary / explanatory text (subscription details): weight: 400; size: 14px; color: #333; line-height: 20px.
- Button label: weight: 700; size: 16-18px; color: #FFF (on dark CTA); padding: 18-20px vertical.

Key components and sizes:
- Status bar area: top safe area with time & device status. Top-right floating circular close button (48x48 px) with subtle drop shadow; icon: X (16-18px stroke), background: white, shadow: 0 6px 18px rgba(0,0,0,0.08).
- Hero illustration: centered mascot illustration (approx 120-150px tall) with generous top margin ~24-32px below status bar.
- Small orange subtitle row: contains a small inline check icon (~16px) and text “9 healthy Challenges” in orange (#CC441E), centered; margin-bottom ~10px.
- H1 headline: “Become a hydration hero!” centered under subtitle. Margin-bottom ~22px.

Pricing selection cards (stacked vertical list):
- Card container width: full minus horizontal padding (screen width - 32px); card height variable; corner radius: 24-32px (very rounded pill-like). Vertical spacing between cards: 12-18px.
- Selected card (primary): background: #45D9EA (teal); text: white; inner padding: 18-22px; left side a small circular selection indicator (34x34 px) slightly overlapping outside card with white circle and teal check icon; inner content: title "Lifetime, Pay once" (bold), secondary line shows original price struck-through in small red then new price bold (e.g. 34,99€ struck-through, 14,99€ highlighted). On the top-right corner of this card a pink ribbon/pill overlays with text "-57% ENDS SOON"; ribbon radius 12px, padding 8px 12px, white uppercase text, small shadow.
- Secondary card: background: very pale cyan (#E8FBFF); text primary color: teal (#45D9EA) for headline "0.00€ due now" (bold); subtext: grey (#6B6B6B) explaining the trial "3 days Free, then 8,99€/year". Card corner radius same as primary. This card is unselected (no selection marker). The selection markers behave as radio controls (only one selected at once).
- Typographic treatment within cards: headline ~18-20px bold; subtext 13-15px regular; strike-through original price using thin red line and slightly smaller size.

CTA button:
- Large full-width rounded pill button centered below the pricing stack. Background: deep navy (#3E3227) (or near-black); label: "Continue" in white bold, size 16-18px; horizontal padding 28-32px; vertical padding 18-20px; corner radius 40px; subtle inner shadow/pressed state on tap; drop shadow: 0 6px 12px rgba(62,50,39,0.12).

Social proof / award row:
- Beneath CTA, a horizontal block shows left column: muted editorial logos (Forbes, Cosmopolitan, TechCrunch, Vogue, ABC News) vertically stacked in light grey; center: circular gold award medal (flat illustration) with text "APPLE DESIGN AWARD"; right: rating block with large text "250,000+" and 5 yellow stars beneath plus the label "RATINGS" in grey. All items center-aligned in a 3-column visual composition but flow vertically on narrow screens. Colors for medal: gold #E4C810 with darker gold accents and a subtle inner shadow.
- Spacing around award: 20-28px top and bottom.

Micro-interactions & states:
- Card selection: tap card to select; selected card visually elevated with slightly stronger shadow and the check indicator visible. Unselected card slightly translucent and no check.
- CTA button: disabled state (if no selection) uses 60% opacity; active state: full color; tap: quick scale down (0.98) with 100ms ease.
- Promo ribbon: tapping opens modal with promotion details or countdown.
- Close X: dismisses modal (slide down or fade) with ease-out 250ms.

Spacing & layout metrics (approx):
- Screen horizontal padding: 16px (left/right)
- Hero top margin: 20-28px
- Heading to card spacing: 18-26px
- Card corner radius: 24-32px
- Selection circle: 34x34px positioned -16px left of card left edge, vertically centered with card content
- CTA height: ~64px including vertical padding and font

Accessibility notes:
- Use 44x44pt minimum touch targets for close button and cards.
- Maintain contrast for text over colored cards (white on teal passes WCAG AA if tested).
- Provide alternative text for award badges and logos.

Assets & icons:
- Vector mascot illustration (transparent PNG / SVG)
- Check icon (SVG) white on teal circle for selected card
- Star icons for rating (filled yellow)
- Editorial logos as muted greyscale PNGs

Deliverables a designer should export:
- Full-screen modal prototype (iPhone safe area) in light and dark variations
- Components: Pricing Card (selected / unselected), CTA button states (default/pressed/disabled), Floating close button, Promo ribbon, Award medal asset
- Spacing spec & token file (colors, font sizes, radii)

Animation suggestions:
- Modal entrance: fade + upward slide 220ms, easing: cubic-bezier(.22,.8,.32,1)
- Card selection: scale 1.02 + shadow lift 160ms, easing: ease-out
- Button press: quick scale 0.98, 100ms
- Promo ribbon: slight wobble/attention animation loop once (subtle) when discount is active.
content.layout:
Single-column, vertically stacked mobile modal with centered alignment. The screen is effectively divided into 6 stacked groups from top to bottom:
1) Status area with floating close control (safe area) — one column.
2) Hero illustration + small orange subtitle + H1 headline — centered single column.
3) Price-selection group — a vertical list of two full-width cards (1 column, 2 rows). Cards visually grouped as radio options; the selected card includes an overlapping selection circle and an overlay promo ribbon.
4) Primary CTA — full-width rounded pill button centered (1 column).
5) Social proof / awards — three visual columns inside one horizontal band: left (editorial logos, vertical stack), center (award medal), right (rating + stars). On narrow widths this band stacks vertically but visually reads as three columns; treat as a 3-column group within the single-column flow.
6) Secondary content header and product highlight/card below — single column with additional rounded content cards.

Grid details: there is no multi-column content except the award band which visually uses a 3-column arrangement. Overall layout uses a 1-column responsive grid with rows: header, hero, pricing cards (2 rows), CTA, social proof row (3 visual columns), secondary content.

Alignment & padding:
- Main content horizontally centered with side padding ~16px.
- Cards and CTA use full available width within padding constraints.
- Vertical rhythm: 12–28px spacing between elements depending on prominence.

Keywords to describe layout: stacked, centered, single-column, card-list, hero-top, full-width-cta, modal, badge-overlay, three-column-band, rounded-pill
content.functions:
Specific on-screen actions (micro tasks):
- Tap a pricing card to select a plan (selection indicated by a circular check control). The UI gives immediate visual feedback (checkmark appears, card gets highlighted and elevated).
- Read pricing details: view original price (struck-through), discounted price, trial period and yearly subscription price in the secondary card.
- Tap the pink promo ribbon to view discount details or terms (likely opens a small modal or tooltip).
- Tap the large "Continue" button to proceed to the next step (payment confirmation, system purchase sheet, or account upgrade flow).
- Tap the floating close (X) button to dismiss the modal and return to the previous screen.
- Scroll the modal vertically to reveal social proof, awards and further information about the product.
- Tap logos or awards (optional) to view press mentions or award details (possible links or lightboxes).

Medium-level tasks / short workflows:
- Choose a subscription plan (lifetime pay-once vs. free trial / yearly plan) and press Continue to move to checkout or to the app-store purchase flow.
- Review discount terms and pricing details before confirming purchase (tap promo ribbon or pricing fine print).
- Use the close action to exit the paywall without subscribing (preserve selection state if reopened).

Broader user goal:
- Convert free users into paying customers by clearly presenting pricing options, a strong value proposition (hero + awards), and a prominent call-to-action to complete purchase. The screen is designed to reduce friction (one-tap selection and continue), provide trust signals (editorial logos, Apple Design Award, star ratings), and highlight savings (promo ribbon and struck-through original price) to drive conversion.
