content.description:
Mobile screenshot of an iOS purchase/subscription confirmation overlay (Apple Pay style) presented as a frosted-glass bottom sheet over a blurred background. Overall style: native iOS, translucent/frosted glass, high corner radii, soft shadows, neutral/pastel pink tint for the sheet and dark dim overlay for background. Canvas: full-phone vertical layout (approx. 375pt wide). Background: blurred content visible (card carousel with bright colors) with a semi-opaque dark overlay centered behind the modal (rgba(0,0,0,0.35)) so background shapes are visible but muted.

Modal / Bottom sheet: centered horizontally and anchored to bottom, occupying ~55–65% of screen height. Corner radius large (approx. 24–30px). Background uses an iOS frosted blur (UIVisualEffectView) with a pinkish tint (use color overlay #BDB2D0 @ 18–30% opacity or rgba(189,178,208,0.25)) and a subtle inner highlight at the top (linear gradient: rgba(255,255,255,0.18) -> transparent). Modal has a subtle drop shadow: 0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.18).

Header area: left-aligned Apple Pay logo at top-left of the modal (black Apple icon + "Pay" wordmark, using SF Pro Text Bold ~18pt). The header area vertical padding ~12–16px. Top-right has a circular close button (diameter ~40px) with a faint white translucent background and an 'X' icon centered (stroke ~2px, color #2B0E13). The close button sits inside the modal top-right, with a subtle inner shadow and 12px margin from edges.

Main content: inside the sheet there is a card-like content area with white background (slightly elevated, radius ~14px) and internal padding ~16–20px. At the top-left of this content area is the application icon (square rounded 12px, size ~56x56px) showing the product / app illustration. To the right of the icon is the title & subtitle block: Title uses SF Pro Display Semibold 16–18pt, dark gray (#545353 or near black). Subtitle (app category + "Subscription" / age badge) uses SF Pro Regular 12–13pt, muted gray (#C9C8D1), all left-aligned. Spacing between icon and text ~12–14px. The content block divider is a thin hairline rule (1px, color #E9E7EA) spanning the card width below the header area.

Price / Offer area: Large stacked typographic block. Top line: promotional microcopy "3-day free trial" in medium weight (SF Pro Semibold 15–16pt, #1B1049 or dark charcoal). Under it a small caption "Starting today" in regular 12–13pt muted gray (#C9C8D1). Next the price line is prominent: "8,99 € per year" in bold SF Pro Display 22–26pt, color near black (#2B0E13 or #545353). Below price smaller gray caption with start date text in 12pt regular. These price lines have generous vertical spacing: 8–12px between lines.

Legal text: paragraph copy in small regular weight (SF Pro Regular 12pt, color #545353 with 60–70% opacity), left-aligned. Use 1.2 line-height. The paragraph is separated from price area by another thin divider. At the bottom of the white card area is a gray account email label in smaller type (11–12pt), muted (#C9C8D1).

Footer / confirm area: the modal bottom area outside the white card has extra vertical space with a circular blue/white icon representing the side-button double-click action (approx 48px diameter) centered horizontally. Beneath that icon is the instruction text: "Confirm with Side Button" (SF Pro Regular 14–15pt, #545353) centered. This footer area uses the same frosted background but slightly darker to visually separate it from the white content card. Footer vertical padding ~16–20px.

Overlays & chrome: A dark rounded pill (approx 220 x 48 px) with a centered loading spinner is overlayed near the top-middle of the screen (outside the modal) — this pill is dark navy (#1B1049) with a subtle inner glow and a white spinner (8–10px spokes). On the right of the screen is an iOS-style vertical scroll thumb: narrow rounded rectangle (width ~8–10px, height ~30–35% of screen) in white with rounded corners and a slight drop shadow. Also visible in the background (behind modal) is a large rating card with five yellow stars and a headline; these are part of the blurred app content.

Colors (approx):
- Dim overlay: rgba(0,0,0,0.35)
- Modal frosted tint: rgba(189,178,208,0.25) (hex 0xBDB2D0 used as soft tint)
- Primary text / headings: #2B0E13 (deep maroon/charcoal) or #545353 for general headings
- Muted / secondary text: #C9C8D1
- Accent / deep background: #1B1049 (navy) used for spinner pill
- Subtle dark gray: #545353 (body text)
- Stars / rating (background element): #FFD400 (approx)

Typography: SF Pro Display/Text (iOS system font). Suggested sizes & weights: title 17–18pt Semibold, subtitle 12–13pt Regular, price 22–26pt Bold (700), offer headline 15–16pt Medium, legal copy 11–12pt Regular. Line-height approx 1.2–1.4 depending on element. Left text alignment inside content card, centered alignment for footer icon + instruction.

Spacing & sizing: modal horizontal margin 12–16px to screen edge. Content card padding 16–20px. App icon 56x56px. Close button 40px diameter with 12px internal padding from edge. Hairline dividers 1px (#E9E7EA). Corner radii: modal 24–30px, internal content card 12–16px.

States & animation hints: modal enters with upward slide + fade (200–300ms ease-out). Frost blur increases during animation. Spinner rotates continuously (1s linear infinite). Close button press: scale 0.96 and slight darken. Footer confirm instruction is static — actual device confirmation occurs physically (side button).
content.layout:
Single-column, stacked layout inside a bottom-anchored modal (bottom sheet). The screen is organized into three main vertical groups: 1) modal header (Apple Pay brand left, close icon right), 2) main content card (app icon + title row, price/trial block, legal copy, account email), 3) modal footer (confirm icon + instruction). There is an additional transient top overlay element (dark rounded pill with centered spinner) which sits above the blurred background and overlaps the top of the modal area.

Column/grid details: the modal content uses a single primary column for text; the only horizontal subdivision is the app icon + text row which functions as two columns within that row (left column fixed 56px icon, right flexible text column). Dividers create clear horizontal grouping. No multi-column grid beyond that single two-column row.

Counts: 1 primary column, 1 two-column row group for header/icon area, 3 vertical groups (header, content card, footer). Visual alignment is left within the content card and centered for the footer instruction.

Keywords for layout: bottom-sheet, single-column, two-column-header-row, centered-footer, frosted-glass, large-corner-radius, hairline-dividers, left-aligned-typography, stacked-typography, transient-overlay
content.functions:
Immediate actions available on this screen (micro-level):
- Read subscription metadata: user can scan the app icon, app name/title, minor category text, and identify the subscription type and age tag. The layout prioritizes the title and price so the user can quickly comprehend the offer.
- Inspect trial & start dates: the UI displays a bold trial headline, a small caption showing when the trial starts, and the subscription cost line (price + period) with an effective start date beneath it. These are selectable by eye only (no inline editing on this modal).
- Dismiss modal: user can cancel/exit by tapping the X close button at the top-right of the modal.
- Confirm purchase: the prominent confirmation instruction at the bottom tells the user to "Confirm with Side Button" (physical device action). The UI gives a clear affordance and icon for how to complete the purchase.
- View account: the account email is displayed so the user can confirm which Apple ID will be billed.
- Read legal & renewal info: small fine-print explains cancellation policy and automatic renewal; users can scan this and mentally accept terms before confirming.

Medium-level tasks / workflows enabled by this screen:
- Completing an in-app subscription purchase flow: The modal acts as the final confirmation before billing, combining offer summary, price, trial terms, and explicit confirm action.
- Verifying account/billing identity: user verifies the displayed account email and payment prompt before committing.
- Cancelling or denying purchase: the close button and tapping outside (if allowed) returns the user to the previous screen without subscribing.

Broader purpose and how this screen helps accomplish it:
- The broader goal is to convert a user into a paying subscriber or to present the final confirmation step for a subscription. The design prioritizes clarity of offer (trial + price), short legal transparency (renewal & cancellation), and an explicit tactile confirmation mechanism (side-button double-click), which reduces accidental purchases. Visual hierarchy (title, price, trial, legal) and the frosted modal isolate this decision and reduce distractions so the user can make a deliberate choice quickly.

steps.name: Restore purchases & legal links
steps.goal: Provide account recovery and legal information at the bottom of the sheet.
steps.action: User can tap 'Restore Purchases' or access 'Terms & Privacy' / 'Help & Support'.
steps.system_response: Tapping 'Restore Purchases' starts the platform restore flow (or presents the platform's restore UI). Terms and support links navigate to their respective screens or external pages.

content.description:
Full-screen iPhone view showing a subscription / purchase flow with a centered success confirmation modal over a dimmed background. Background: a horizontal carousel of large rounded cards (deep maroon/red card is centered) with a visible avatar (round), five yellow star icons and a white headline copy. The carousel cards have large 24–28px corner radii and are horizontally stacked so neighbouring cards are partially visible on left and right. At the very top, a dark navy rounded capsule (pill) overlays the carousel and contains a centered spinner/loader icon (white radial). Top-right there is a circular close button (light circle with an “X” glyph) that sits above the carousel.

Foreground modal: A medium-height rounded rectangle (large corner radius ~22–28px) with a soft pink gradient background (lighter at top, slightly darker at bottom). The modal casts a subtle drop shadow and sits centered horizontally about 40% down from top of screen. Inside the modal: heading text “You’re all set” in bold (approx 20–22px), subtext “Your purchase was successful.” in regular weight (~15–16px) with comfortable line-height (1.3). Beneath the text is a large primary action button: full-width, pill-shaped (corner radius ~28–32px), bright saturated blue background with white uppercase label “OK” (16–18px semibold). The button sits inside the modal with inner padding so it visually appears inset from the modal edges.

Background overlay: the entire background is dimmed with a semi-opaque layer (black at ~30–45% opacity) so the carousel is still visible but de-emphasized. Footer: below the carousel there is small legal copy / subscription details in grey (~12px) and a teal/blue link “Restore Purchases” centered above a small two-column row of secondary links (“Terms & Privacy” and “Help & Support”) spaced horizontally.

Visual style & assets: iOS native look (SF Pro system font), large rounded shapes, saturated accent colors (deep maroon card, yellow star icons), soft rounded modal with pastel pink gradient, prominent blue primary CTA. Subtle realistic shadow on modal and soft pressed look for button. The spinner in the top capsule is animated (rotating). All elements use plenty of vertical spacing and centred alignment for the modal content.

Exact colors (approx):
- Deep purple / navy overlay capsule: #2B1677 (provided)
- Maroon card background: #7A162E (provided)
- Accent orange (used on left card edge): #D46305 (provided)
- Mid grey body/footer text: #929192 (provided)
- Light lavender accent (used sparingly around UI): #C1B5F3 (provided)
- Modal pink gradient range: top #FFD9DF → bottom #F7B9C0 (approximate)
- Primary button blue: #0A62FF (approximate)
- Stars: #FFD400 (yellow)
- Overlay dim: rgba(0,0,0,0.35)

Typography (recommended for recreation): SF Pro Text / SF Pro Display
- Modal heading: 20–22pt, bold, center-aligned
- Modal body: 15–16pt, regular, center-aligned, 1.25–1.4 line-height
- Button label: 16–17pt, semibold, uppercase, centered
- Carousel headline on card: 18–20pt, bold, left-aligned within card padding
- Footer legal text: 11–12pt, regular, centered, reduced opacity (~60%)

Spacing & sizing (approx):
- Screen safe area margins left/right: 16–20pt
- Carousel card horizontal padding inside bounds: 20–24pt
- Modal width: 74–86% of screen width (leaving visible card edges)
- Modal vertical padding: 20–24pt top/bottom, 18–20pt left/right
- Button height: 48–54pt, full modal-width minus inner padding
- Modal to top capsule gap: ~22–28pt
- Spinner capsule size: 240–260pt wide, 48–56pt tall, centered

Micro-interactions & animation:
- Spinner: continuous rotation at ~1s per rotation with ease-linear
- Modal open/close: ease-out scale from 0.96→1 and fade (duration 220–320ms)
- Button press: quick scale-down 0.98 with 100–120ms duration and subtle shadow reduction
- Carousel: horizontal scroll with subtle parallax; neighboring cards visible with slight scale reduction (~0.94) and dim overlay

Accessibility notes: high contrast primary CTA, text readable against pink background using bold for heading and sufficient size for body text; ensure voiceover reads modal as an alert and focus jumps to the OK button when opened.
content.layout:
Overall layout: single-column, full-screen mobile layout with a centered floating modal over a horizontally scrolling card carousel and bottom footer.

Structure & columns:
- Primary layout column: one main vertical column centered on the screen (content stacked vertically: top capsule loader → carousel area → footer text & links).
- Carousel area: a single-row horizontal carousel comprised of large rounded cards stacked side-by-side. The carousel shows 1 focused card in the center and partial glimpses of adjacent cards left and right (so effectively 3 card positions visible but one primary).
- Modal overlay: a centered floating single column (modal) that sits above the carousel; the modal itself contains stacked elements (heading → subtext → primary action button).
- Footer area: below the carousel is a centered block of legal copy (multi-line), then a single-line primary link (“Restore Purchases”), followed by a two-column row of small links horizontally spaced.

Grids & groups:
- Carousel grid: 1 row × 3 visible card positions (central card full, left/right partial). Cards are grouped visually as a carousel/card-stack.
- Modal internal grid: single column stack with consistent vertical spacing. The primary CTA is horizontally full-width within the modal’s inner padding.

Alignment & padding:
- All main elements are center-aligned horizontally (modal, footer links). Text inside cards is left-aligned to create contrast with center-aligned modal copy.
- Standard horizontal safe-area padding: ~16–20pt. Modal width is narrower than full-bleed carousel so that card edges remain visible.

Key layout keywords: centered modal overlay, single-column stack, horizontal carousel, card-stack, large corner radii, full-width primary button, dimmed backdrop, top capsule loader, footer links row, floating circular close.
content.functions:
Specific single-screen actions:
- Read confirmation: The user can read the modal heading and supporting copy to learn the purchase succeeded.
- Dismiss success modal: Tap the large blue “OK” button to dismiss the confirmation and return to the underlying screen.
- Close overlay: Tap the circular “X” in the top-right to close the paywall/overlay without interacting with the modal (alternative exit).
- Interact with the carousel behind the modal: swipe horizontally to see other review cards in the background carousel (partial peeks indicate more items).
- Trigger spinner state: The navy capsule with spinner indicates a background loading process (e.g., restoring purchases or verifying receipt).
- Restore purchases: Tap the centered “Restore Purchases” link in the footer to initiate an account restore flow.
- Access legal/help links: Tap “Terms & Privacy” or “Help & Support” to open related documents or support flows.

Medium-level workflows enabled by this interface:
- Complete in-app purchase flow: user purchases a subscription or one-time item; the app confirms the purchase with the success modal and provides CTA to continue.
- Restore/verify purchases: user can restore prior purchases from the footer link; the spinner and capsule indicate verification/network state.
- Read reviews before buying: user can browse the carousel of testimonial/review cards behind the modal to evaluate the product/service prior to confirming.

Broader goals achieved:
- Provide a clear, immediate confirmation that the user’s transaction succeeded, reducing uncertainty.
- Offer recovery and legal actions (restore purchases, terms, support) to maintain trust and comply with platform rules.
- Maintain continuity with the rest of the paywall/subscription interface via visible review cards and a consistent visual language (rounded shapes, bold colors) so users can proceed seamlessly after confirmation.

records.name: Share Card to Social
records.description: Happy path: A mobile user views a generated promotional card (WaterLlama) and chooses a social channel to share it. Entry point: user reaches the card preview with sharing CTAs. Exit point: the chosen share channel’s composer opens (example shows iOS Messages composer). Assumptions: mobile (iPhone) device, user has network connectivity and the target sharing apps (Messages / Messenger / Instagram / Facebook) available. The app provides a visual preview of the card, a social handle prompt, and large tappable “pill” buttons for common channels. Tapping a channel hands off to the native share/composer UI for that service with the image and a prefilled caption/link.
records.problem: User task (user perspective): Share the custom WaterLlama card with friends or social channels quickly, optionally tagging the app. The user expects a clear preview of what will be shared, large, obvious sharing options, and the ability to edit or send the prefilled message once the target composer opens. Interface/system perspective: The UI must display the generated card preview, a call-to-action encouraging tagging (@waterllama_app), and channel-specific share buttons that invoke the appropriate OS or third-party composer with the card image and a prefilled caption + link. End result: user-perceived outcome — the user sees the card preview, selects a channel, sees the native composer populated with image and message, edits if desired, and sends. System-level outcome — the app passes the image and text payload to the chosen share target (native Messages or other app) for delivery; the sharing action is performed by the target app/OS share sheet.

steps.name: Share Options / Card Preview
steps.goal: Let the user review the generated WaterLlama card and choose where to share it.
steps.action: User views the centered card preview, reads the 'Sharing to social? Tag us' prompt with the @waterllama_app handle, and taps one of the large pill-style buttons (Messages, Messenger, Instagram, Facebook) or closes the screen via the top-right X.
steps.system_response: The app prepares a payload (image + prompt/link) for the selected channel and invokes the corresponding share/composer interface. The screen remains as the origin while the OS or target app is launched to handle the share.

content.description:
Overview
- Full-screen mobile share modal presenting a centered promotional preview (poster) with large vertical list of social-share destination buttons below. The modal has a very light off-white background, a floating circular close button at top-right, and the phone status bar visible at top.

Visual style
- Playful, friendly, colorful, and highly illustrated aesthetic (childlike mascot illustration, soft rounded shapes, pastel backgrounds for action buttons). The overall style aligns with consumer mobile branding for kids/family/health products.

Color palette (observed + developer-provided)
- Primary accent purple: #C348B6 (used in brand text/Instagram accent)
- Secondary yellow: #D0B72E (used in small decorative elements in illustration)
- Teal / blue: #52B8EB (used in brand name, some button accents)
- Deep brown / near-black for body text: #352830 (heading/body text color)
- Bright green: #3ECC27 (used for Messages icon/text color)
- Background / cards: near-white / very pale gray: #FAFBFA (page background)
- Preview frame border: light gray: #D9D9D9
- Buttons backgrounds are pastel tints derived from the social brand colors: mint green (Messages), lavender (Messenger), pastel pink (Instagram), pale blue (Facebook)

Typography
- iOS system/modern geometric sans feel (likely SF Pro or Avenir Next). Use centered alignment for main copy. Suggested type tokens (approx):
  - Title / prompt (“Sharing to social? …”): 18–20pt, semibold (600), color #352830, line-height 24pt, center-aligned.
  - Social handle link (“@waterllama_app”): 16–18pt, regular or medium, color teal #52B8EB, center-aligned, slight tracking +0.2.
  - Button labels: 18–20pt, semibold (600), colored to match icon accent (green/purple/pink/blue), left-aligned within pill with 16–20px icon left margin.
  - Small legal or logo text under preview: 12–14pt, regular, color #6B6B6B.

Layout & spacing (approx, for iPhone 375pt width)
- Screen width baseline: 375pt. Safe area respected.
- Top status bar plus ~24–32pt top padding before content.
- Preview card: centered horizontally, width ≈ 260–280pt, height ≈ 420–460pt, thin border stroke 4pt color #D9D9D9, slight corner radius 4–6pt. Inside the preview a large llama illustration is vertically centered with brand text at top and small logo + tagline near the bottom of the card. There is generous white space around the illustration.
- Vertical rhythm: preview → 28–36pt gap → prompt text (two lines) → 16pt gap → social handle → 28–36pt gap → first pill button → 16–18pt gap between successive pills.
- Pill buttons: full-width minus 40–48pt side margins (i.e., 24pt left/right safe margin + 8–12pt). Height ≈ 54–64pt. Border radius ~32pt to create elongated pill shape. Icon on the left (36–44pt square with 8–12pt internal padding), label vertically centered. Each pill uses a soft pastel background (subtle tint of brand color) and uses the social icon gradient or colored glyph on the left.
- Floating Close Button: circular 48pt diameter, white fill, subtle drop shadow (rgba(0,0,0,0.12) offset 0 6px 12px), X glyph centered in dark gray #352830. Positioned near top-right of safe area with 12–16pt margin.

UI elements (visual specifics)
- Preview card: gray 4pt border, white inner background. Illustration centered with 28–36pt internal top/bottom padding.
- Illustration: detailed colorful flat/soft-shaded vector llama on a surfboard. Colors drawn from palette; decorative garlands and sunglasses.
- Prompt copy: centered friendly sentence including an emoji. Uses a medium weight with relaxed line-height.
- Social handle: tappable-looking turquoise/teal text (blue-green) centered.
- Share destination pill buttons: four vertically stacked large pill CTAs: Messages (mint green background, Messages glyph, label in bright green #3ECC27), Messenger (lavender background, purple gradient brand glyph, label in purple #5B4AEF), Instagram (pale pink background, Instagram gradient glyph, label in pink #C348B6), Facebook (pale blue background, FB glyph, label in blue #2D66D6). Each pill has subtle inner shadow or elevation and a consistent left icon + label layout.

States & interactions
- Tap on any pill triggers the system-level share flow / opens corresponding messaging surface for sending the preview image. Visual feedback: pill press uses subtle darken or scale (e.g., scale to 0.98) and quick 120ms ease-out.
- Close button dismisses the overlay with a fast fade + downward slide (duration 180–240ms, cubic-bezier .22,.9,.34,1). Background dimming is minimal (modal uses full-screen but keeps background very pale).
- The social handle is tappable (copies handle or opens the brand profile) — show subtle underline or color change on press.

Accessibility
- Buttons are tall (54–64pt) for easy tapping. Color contrast between pill label and background is sufficient for legibility due to saturated label hues.
- Emoji in prompt adds a friendly tone but should not be the only instruction.

Animations
- Modal enter: content fades in from 0 → 100% opacity with small upward translation (12–18px) for the preview and buttons; durations: 220–320ms, easing cubic-bezier(.2,.9,.3,1).
- Button presses use quick scale 0.98 with 80–120ms duration and ease-out.

Designer notes
- Keep pill corner radius large for the soft, friendly look. Reuse brand gradient for the Instagram/Messenger glyphs. Use system type for consistent iOS feel (SF Pro). Maintain large touch targets and center alignment for a clear single-column flow. Preview card should preserve aspect ratio of the poster and include a thin neutral frame to separate it from background.
content.layout:
Overall structure
- Single column centered vertical layout (one main column). All content is center-aligned horizontally.
- Stacked groups (from top to bottom): status bar area → floating close button overlay (top-right) → framed preview card (centered) → prompt text and brand handle → vertical list of 4 pill CTAs.

Preview card group
- Group count: 1 card in the center column. Card is visually boxed (thin border) and contains three inner groups: brand headline (top), mascot illustration (center), small logo + tagline (bottom). The card maintains internal vertical rhythm and white space.

Buttons group
- Vertical stack of 4 equal-width pill buttons, each occupying its own row; rows spaced evenly with consistent vertical gaps (≈16–20pt). Buttons share identical height and corner radius. Icon and label form a two-column micro-layout inside each pill (icon column fixed width ~44pt, label column fluid).

Columns & grid
- No multi-column or grid layout — single centered column. Inside each pill there are effectively two columns (icon column + text column). The preview card uses a single centered column for its inner content.

Spacing & alignment specifics (approx)
- Left/right outer margins: ~24–28pt.
- Preview card top offset from status bar: ~56–72pt.
- Vertical spacing between major groups: 24–36pt.

Keywords describing layout
- single-column
- centered-alignment
- vertical-stack
- full-screen-modal
- framed-preview
- pill-buttons
- floating-close
- icon-left-label-right
- generous-whitespace
- safe-area-aware
content.functions:
Specific actions (micro-level)
- Tap the circular X in the top-right to dismiss the modal.
- Tap the preview image to open a full-screen preview (or long-press to save or copy image) — the image is presented as a framed card with a visible border.
- Tap the @waterllama_app handle to open the brand's social profile or copy the handle to clipboard.
- Tap any of the four large pill CTAs (Messages, Messenger, Instagram, Facebook) to invoke the platform-specific share or message composer, prefilled with the poster image and suggested caption.
- Each pill contains an icon and a tappable label area — the whole pill acts as one button.

Medium-level tasks (workflows)
- Share workflow: user chooses a destination, taps a pill, which opens the chosen messaging/social composer with the preview image attached. The app should provide feedback on success or failure of the share (e.g., toast or post-share success screen).
- Tagging & engagement: the prompt encourages the user to tag the brand when sharing. Tapping the handle allows quick access to the brand profile to follow or message.
- Dismiss and return workflow: user can dismiss quickly with the close button or system back gesture and return to the previous screen.

Broader goal (macro-level)
- The screen’s purpose is to drive user sharing of brand content to social and messaging channels — increasing brand visibility and encouraging user engagement. It simplifies sharing by providing one-tap CTAs for popular destinations and highlights the brand handle to encourage tagging. The layout prioritizes the visual asset (poster/mascot) and then presents clear social CTAs to minimize friction when users want to share.

How UI supports tasks
- A single-column vertical stack focuses user attention top-to-bottom: preview first (visual hook), prompt & tag next (instruction), then large tappable CTAs (action). The big pill CTAs reduce cognitive load and are easy to target on mobile. The floating close button and status bar presence make the overlay feel native to the OS.

steps.name: iOS Messages Composer (example)
steps.goal: Open the Messages composer with the card preview and a prefilled message so the user can choose recipients, edit text, and send.
steps.action: User selects a recipient in the 'To:' field (example shows 'Matt Lam'), optionally edits the message text and/or removes/changes the image, then taps the send arrow to send or taps the X to cancel and return.
steps.system_response: The device displays the native Messages compose overlay prefilled with the card image and caption/link. Sending is handled by the Messages app/OS; cancelling or dismissing returns control to the originating app or previous screen.

content.description:
Overall visual summary
- This is an iOS-style message-composition overlay (share/composer) shown above the onscreen keyboard. The composer is presented as a rounded, white, semi-elevated card / bottom sheet with heavy blur on the underlying content. The card has large corner radii and subtle inner padding; it contains a "To:" recipient input as a pill, a large content preview card (image + link preview + body text), and a circular send control. There is a small circular close button (X) floating near the top-right of the overlay.

Style & visual language
- Platform: iOS (San Francisco system font, large, airy spacing, translucent backgrounds, subtle shadows). Use SF Pro Text / SF Pro Display for accurate look.
- Visual style: soft, highly rounded shapes, translucent frosted glass background behind the card, full-bleed keyboard at bottom, high-contrast large message text for readability. Subtle drop shadow under the composer to suggest elevation.

Color palette (recommendations and approximations from screenshot)
- Dark / primary accent (used sparingly for icons/badges / background content): #1E1B1F
- Primary blue accent (links, selected pill text color, send arrow highlight): #61C4E5
- Medium gray (secondary text, separators, keyboard key outlines): #6E6E70
- Warm accent (used in small graphic elements / illustration): #D3AB33
- Muted brown (illustration detail): #815E5E
- Card background (main composer / share preview bg): #FFFFFF (100% opaque) with slight inner elevation and 2–6% black overlay at edges to simulate depth or use white at 98% opacity over blur.
- Backdrop blur: neutral translucent gray ~ rgba(240,240,240,0.6) with heavy blur (iOS vibrancy feel).

Typography
- System font: SF Pro (San Francisco). Use the platform-weighted styles to match iOS.
- Header / small labels: 14–16pt medium (e.g., "To:"). Weight: Medium (500).
- Recipient pill text: 16–17pt Semibold (600). Blue accent color (#61C4E5) for the link-styled name; pill background: very light gray/blue, e.g., rgba(97,196,229,0.08) or white with 1–2px border.
- Message body / preview text: large, readable — 18–22pt Regular (400) with 1.1–1.2 line-height. In screenshot the card text is large and left aligned; keep the link and emoji inline.
- Small preview meta (site name): 11–12pt Medium, colored #6E6E70 or a slightly dimmed blue for the domain.

UI elements — spacing, sizes, radii, and states
- Composer card: width ≈ screen width minus 28–36px horizontal margin; corner radius ≈ 22–28px; padding inside card: top 14–18px, horizontal 14–18px, bottom 12–16px.
- Top recipient row: a pill-style input field that stretches horizontally. Height ≈ 40–44px. Left label "To:" on same line (12–14pt). Recipient token (Matt Lam) is a rounded capsule about 28–36px high, with horizontal padding 10–14px and corner radius ~18px.
- Add contact (+) button: circular 36–44px diameter, light stroke or subtle background; placed at the right end of the recipient field.
- Content preview card: a contained white tile within the composer (rounded corners ≈ 12–16px) with an illustration/photo at the top (centered) and textual preview below. Use inner padding 12–18px. The image sits centered with generous whitespace around it.
- Send control: circular primary action button located at the lower-right of the preview card (floating half-over card). Diameter ≈ 36–44px. Background: #61C4E5 (blue), icon: upward arrow/chevron in white. Press state: slightly darker blue (#4DA6C8) with 0.95 scale or simple iOS opacity on touch.
- Secondary floating add button: circular + on the left edge of the content area (diameter ≈ 38–44px) — light background, subtle stroke, uses same border radius as other bubbles.
- Close (X) control: circular close affordance near top-right corner of overlay (diameter ≈ 40px) with soft pinkish background and thin border; icon dark (#1E1B1F) or subtle gray.
- Keyboard: iOS style rounded keys, light gray background (#F3F4F6), key corner radius ~8–12px, normal heights ~300px for portrait. Microphone icon on the right of the keyboard in black.

Layout & structure
- Status bar at very top (9:41 and system indicators). Under that you can see the blurred content of the previous screen (slightly visible at the top behind the overlay). The composer sits centered horizontally and is vertically anchored above the keyboard with a small gap (~8–12px) respecting the safe area.
- Vertical stacking inside composer: recipient row near top → content preview card (image + meta + long message text) → the keyboard below (native). The send button overlaps the bottom-right of the preview card.

Interaction & micro-interactions
- Composer appears with a smooth upward slide and fade (duration 220–320ms, easing cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) for springy iOS feel). Underlay content blurs gradually and reduces brightness.
- Recipient token: tappable (edits name, reveals contact quick actions). Pressing + shows contact selector sheet.
- Send button: active (blue) only with non-empty message or valid recipient; tap triggers a subtle scale animation (0.95 -> 1) and an instantaneous send feedback (haptic on device). After send, composer dismisses with upward fade and a short success toast (optional).
- Content preview card: tapping the image or header opens the shared link in a new view; long press opens context menu (Copy Link, Preview, Remove Preview).

Recreate notes (exact assets)
- Use a high-resolution llama illustration (rounded, colorful), place it in the preview card with generous white space and rounded corners. Use the provided accent palette for small highlights in the illustration.
- Recreate the translucent frosted background via a gaussian blur + tint overlay (light gray), and place a subtle drop shadow beneath the composer card (y: 6, blur: 20, opacity: 0.12).
- Use semantic spacing: grid of 8px increments for padding and margins.

Animations (if implemented)
- Composer entrance: translateY 16–24px and fade in from 0% -> 100% over 260ms with ease-out cubic bezier; backdrop blur grows from 0 to final in same duration.
- Send button tap: 120ms scale to 0.96 then back, simultaneous micro-haptic feedback.

Accessibility
- Large readable message text (>= 18pt) for sighted users. Ensure color contrast for interactive items meets WCAG (send button icon white on blue, recipient text uses blue on light background with sufficient contrast). Provide VoiceOver labels for To: field, send button, and preview card. Respect dynamic type and provide scalable text styles.
content.layout:
Overall structure and grid
- Screen is composed top-to-bottom in three vertical zones: (1) status/blurred header of the app beneath, (2) central floating composer card, (3) system keyboard docked to the bottom.
- Composer card is horizontally centered with side margins of approximately 14–18px. It behaves visually like a single-column layout (one main column) with nested groups inside.

Count of columns and groups
- Primary column count: 1 (single-column vertical stack).
- Groups inside the column: 3 main groups
  1) Recipient row (label "To:", recipient tokens, add button)
  2) Content preview tile (image block, small site label, large message text) with overlapping send control
  3) Floating action / quick-add on left edge of the preview area (a circular add button)

Grid details
- No explicit multi-column grid inside the composer; content preview uses a simple vertical flow: image (centered) -> meta line (left small badge) -> multi-line body text (left-aligned). The send button is absolutely positioned to overlap the bottom-right of the preview tile.
- Keyboard uses native grid of keys—occupies full width and stable height aligned to bottom safe area.

Spacing & alignment
- Horizontal padding for composer: 16px; inner padding for the preview tile: 12–16px.
- Recipient pill aligns left under the top of the composer; add button aligns to end of the pill row (right).
- All elements are left-aligned inside the preview card except the centered image.
- Keep content within safe area insets; top status area has slight gap from the composer to avoid overlap with system status bar.

Keywords that describe the layout
- single-column
- vertical-stack
- bottom-anchored
- frosted-backdrop
- rounded-card
- overlap-action (send button)
- pill-input
- centered-illustration
- safe-area-aware
- native-keyboard
content.functions:
Specific (lowest-level) actions users can do on this screen
- Tap the recipient pill to edit the selected contact name or open a contact picker.
- Type to add or remove recipients in the "To:" text field; press return to confirm a recipient token.
- Tap the circular + next to the recipient field to open the contact selector or add more recipients.
- Tap inside the main message body area to place the cursor and enter or edit the composed message text using the onscreen keyboard.
- Tap the small circular + on the left of the preview area to attach additional content (stickers, images, or other attachments).
- Tap the image/preview card to open the link or content (full preview in the originating app or web view).
- Long-press the preview to reveal contextual actions (copy link, remove preview, share options).
- Tap the circular send arrow (blue) to send the composed message immediately; tapping gives immediate visual/tactile feedback and then dismisses the composer.
- Tap the top-right circular X to close/dismiss the composer without sending.
- Use the microphone icon on the keyboard for voice input or press keyboard keys to type characters.

Medium-level tasks (multi-step flows composed of the above actions)
- Create and send a link share: open composer -> confirm recipient(s) -> optionally edit/add message text -> press send.
- Add multiple recipients: tap + or type addresses -> convert typed names to recipient tokens -> continue editing message -> send.
- Modify share preview: long-press preview -> choose to remove or replace preview -> finalize message -> send.
- Attach additional media: tap left + -> pick photo/sticker -> attach preview shows inside content card -> send.

Higher-level goals (why the user is on this screen)
- Quickly share a link or media from another app into the Messages conversation (share-to-contact flow).
- Compose a short message with a rich preview and send it to one or more contacts while staying within the originating app context.
- Preview what will be sent (image and formatted text) and edit before confirming transmission.

How UI supports these goals
- The recipient pill and visible "To:" field clarify who receives the message; the + affordance provides a clear next step to add recipients.
- Large readable message preview allows quick verification of link content and message text before sending.
- Blue circular send button is visually prominent and positioned where users expect a primary action (lower-right), giving a clear CTA.
- Frosted backdrop and rounded card visually separate composition from background content, reducing distraction and focusing attention on composition tasks.
- Keyboard presence and large text fields enable quick text input with native behavior and voice input (microphone) support.

records.name: Custom Beverage Creation
records.description: The user starts in a beverage library and adds a custom beverage. They select an existing beverage as a similarity reference, rename it to Pumpkin Latte, then configure its size, icon, color, animation, hydration, and alcohol attributes. The user saves the completed beverage and returns to the library, where Pumpkin Latte appears as a new beverage with its configured hydration and caffeine values. The flow is shown on a mobile device. No login or permission state is visible.
records.problem:
From the user's perspective, the task is to add a personally relevant beverage that is not already in the library, using an existing similar beverage to establish reference information, and then customize its identifying and nutritional properties. The user expects to be able to name the drink, choose its serving size and visual appearance, configure animation, and confirm hydration, caffeine, and alcohol values before saving.

From the interface perspective, the system provides an Add entry point, a searchable or scrollable list of existing beverages for similarity selection, editable beverage attributes, and separate selection screens for each configurable property. The system previews changes immediately, preserves selected values when the user returns to the editor, and requires the user to save the completed beverage.

The user-perceived result is a saved Pumpkin Latte beverage shown in the beverage list with a custom icon, hydration value of 70%, and caffeine value of 75mg. The system-level result is a new custom beverage record, increasing the total beverage count from 116 to 117 and adding a Custom category.

content.description:
High-level visual style: Soft, friendly iOS-style mobile interface with generous white space, rounded shapes and subtle shadows. The visual language uses large rounded pills for categories, full-width rounded cards for each beverage row, colorful flat illustrations for each drink, a prominent centered section title, and a bright teal accent for primary actions and toggles.

Color palette (primary + supporting):
- Deep charcoal (headline, selected pill background): #3A3636
- Accent teal (primary action, toggles, icons): #09BCD7
- Warm gold (accent / small highlights): #DCBC05
- Medium neutral (muted text / subtitles): #ABADA8
- Page background / near-white: #FBFBFB
- Card background: very light grey / white: #FFFFFF
- Inactive pill / subtle UI surfaces: #F4F5F6 (approx)
- Toggle knob: #FFFFFF

Typography (recommended font = SF Pro / Inter):
- Page title "Beverages": 34px, 600/700 weight (Semibold/Bold), letter-spacing 0, centered, line-height ~40px, color #3A3636
- Category pill text: 16px, 600 weight for selected, 500/600 for unselected; selected pill text white (#FFFFFF), unselected text #ABADA8; pill height ~40px
- Section label (small caps like HYDRATION): 12px, 600 weight, letter-spacing 1px, color #ABADA8, centered above list
- List item title (e.g., "Green Tea"): 18px, 600 weight, color #3A3636, line-height ~22px
- List item subtitle (e.g., "25mg caffeine"): 13px, 400/500 weight, color #ABADA8, margin-top 4px
- Hydration % value: 16px, 600 weight, color #ABADA8 (slightly lighter than headlines)

Global layout & spacing:
- Safe area top (iPhone status bar) preserved. Top nav area (back button left, +Add pill right) sits in first 56–64px zone.
- Screen uses a single vertical scroll column. Content is center aligned horizontally with side padding ~20–24px.
- Category chips live in a wrapping flow container directly under the title, with vertical spacing of ~18–22px between rows.
- Spacing between card rows ~14–18px. Each card has internal vertical padding ~18–20px and horizontal padding ~18–22px.

Category chips (pills):
- Shape: pill / capsule with full border radius (height/2). Typical size: height 40px, horizontal padding 18px.
- Selected state: background color #3A3636, text white; subtle inner shadow or glow to indicate active. Unselected: background #F4F5F6, text #ABADA8.
- Chips arranged center-aligned and wrap into multiple rows. Some chips include a numeric badge e.g. "All 116" shown as filled capsule.

Top bar & actions:
- Back control: circular button 44x44, soft white background, subtle drop shadow, icon caret left (#3A3636) centered.
- +Add button: rounded capsule ~56x34, filled with teal #09BCD7, white + icon and label "+Add" inside, soft shadow for elevation.

Section header:
- Title "Beverages" centered, large semibold. Small secondary section label "HYDRATION" in uppercase and muted color (#ABADA8) above the list.

List / Rows (Cards & Tiles):
- Each beverage is inside a full-width rounded card with background white (#FFFFFF) and a very subtle drop shadow. Card corner radius ~16–20px.
- Row internal layout: three main horizontal zones (left icon, center content, right actions):
  - Left icon column: fixed width ~44–56px, center vertically. Contains a flat colorful beverage illustration (approx 36x36) with no label inside. Illustrations use saturated colors that visually contrast with the teal accent (examples: green for tea, brown for coffee, yellow for juice, red for soda).
  - Center content column: flexible width, contains title (18px semibold) and optional subtitle (13px regular) stacked vertically, left aligned.
  - Right actions column: percentage value (16px medium) aligned slightly left of the toggle, then the toggle control itself aligned to far right. There is also a vertical drag/reorder affordance (two chevrons) in faint grey to the far right.
- Card height: ~72–84px depending on subtitle presence. Internal vertical padding ~16px.
- Water row shows only title and a 100% value with no toggle (example of conditional controls per item).

Toggle control:
- Capsule slider toggle: track size ~52x30px, filled teal (#09BCD7) when ON, track light grey #E9E9E9 when OFF. Circular knob ~26px, white (#FFFFFF). Interaction: drag or tap.
- Animation: toggle slide transition 180–240ms with cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1) easing. On toggle, the track color cross-fades and knob translates horizontally.

Micro-interactions & states:
- Tapping a category chip animates a fast color transition (120–160ms) and updates the list content.
- Tapping +Add opens a modal/drawer to add a beverage.
- Row swipe or long-press may reveal reorder controls (the chevrons at right suggest ordering). Reordering uses lift-and-drag animation with 200–300ms easing.

Icons & imagery:
- Beverage icons are simple flat vector illustrations with 2–3 colors each, no gradients. They are visually distinct and sized to align with headline text baseline.
- Small caret icon for Back is simple stroke 2px, dark color #3A3636.

Accessibility notes:
- Tap targets all >=44x44 px.
- Contrast: ensure dark headline #3A3636 on white meets contrast for body text; percentage text and small caps use #ABADA8 which is lower contrast but readable for secondary information.

Assets to reproduce: vector beverage icons (water cup, teacup with leaf, milk bottle, coffee cup, juice cup with straw, soda can, beer glass), small chevron handle icon for reordering, capsule toggle component, capsule filter chip component, circular back button, teal +Add pill.

Exact measurements (approx):
- Screen side padding: 20px
- Title top margin from safe area: 16–20px
- Pill height: 40px, corner radius 20px
- Pill horizontal gap: 12px, vertical gap: 12–16px
- Card radius: 18px
- Card horizontal padding: 18–20px
- Left icon area width: 56px
- Right actions column width: 110px (percentage + toggle)
- Row vertical padding: 16–18px
- Toggle track: 52x30, knob diameter 26

This description should allow another designer to accurately recreate the composition, style, spacing and interactions of the provided screen.
content.layout:
Overall layout: a single scrollable vertical column with the following stacked sections from top to bottom: status/top bar, centered page title, multi-row chip filter group (wrapping), a small uppercase section label, then a vertical list of full-width rounded cards (one per beverage). The content is horizontally center-aligned with equal left/right padding.

Detailed row (card) layout (per beverage): three main horizontal columns plus a tiny reorder handle column at far right:
- Column 1 (left icon): fixed width ~56px, contains a centered square/vector illustration (approx 36x36).
- Column 2 (content): flexible width, contains vertical stack: title (top) and optional subtitle (below). Left aligned.
- Column 3 (right actions): fixed width ~110px, contains numeric hydration % followed by the toggle control aligned to the far right of the card.
- Column 4 (reorder handle): narrow 20–24px area with faint chevrons used for drag/reorder.

The category chips occupy a wrapping grid-like flow: they are not strict columns but behave like a fluid inline grid — approximate counts: 3–4 chips per row depending on device width. Chips are centered as a group horizontally.

Cards are stacked vertically with equal gaps between them and each card uses internal horizontal padding. All rows share the same height rules creating a consistent rhythm down the list.

Keywords to describe layout: single-column; centered-header; wrapping-chips; card-list; three-column-rows; left-icon; right-actions; vertical-scroll; large-padding; rounded-corners
content.functions:
Specific actions available on this screen:
- Tap the back button (top-left) to return to the previous view.
- Tap the +Add pill (top-right) to open an add-new-beverage flow (modal or sheet).
- Tap any category chip (e.g., All, Tea, Coffee, Milk) to filter the list. Chips are toggle/selection controls (single or multi-select depending on implementation). The selected chip visually inverts (dark background + white text).
- Scroll vertically through the beverage list to view more items.
- Tap a card to open or edit that beverage’s details (if implemented) or to view more info.

- Reorder items via the reorder handle (two chevrons) — long-press and drag to change the list order if supported.
- Read the hydration percentage for each beverage shown to the right of the item title.

Medium-level workflows enabled:
- Filter and browse beverage categories to find relevant items quickly using the collection of chips.
- Enable/disable beverage types for inclusion in hydration tracking using per-row toggles.
- Add new beverage types into the catalog via the +Add control.
- Inspect caffeine or alcohol metadata (subtitle text) for items that include it.
- Reorder priority of beverages (e.g., frequently used items at top) if reorder is supported.

Broader user goals achieved by this screen:
- Configure which beverages should be counted toward a hydration or nutrition model (e.g., a water-tracking or caffeine budget feature).
- Quickly assess the hydration or relative contribution percent of common beverages and tailor the tracked list for personal preferences or dietary needs.
- Maintain and extend a personal beverage catalog so downstream tracking and summaries (daily hydration, caffeine intake) are accurate. The screen is designed to make these tasks efficient and visually scannable with clear affordances for selection, configuration, and creation.

content.description:
Mobile portrait screen (iPhone-style status bar) for creating/editing a beverage/template. Overall style: soft, friendly, rounded shapes with lots of white space and subtle shadows. Layout is single-column. Top area: left-aligned rounded ghost button labeled “CANCEL” (light grey background, soft inner shadow, uppercase light-weight text, ~14px). Top-right: prominent dark rounded pill button labeled “SAVE” (dark charcoal fill, white uppercase text, subtle drop shadow). Centered under the status bar is a rounded beige/orange pill (chip) with the label “Similar to: Starbucks Pumpkin Spice Latte” and a small chevron/down arrow on the right indicating a dropdown/select; the chip uses a warm pale-beige background (#FFEBD7 or #FBE8D6) with orange text (#E37304). Hero illustration: large flat vector of a mug with whipped top, filled with solid brand-orange (#E37304). Illustration is centered horizontally and takes large vertical space (roughly 40–45% of the screen height), visually acting as a preview of the selected beverage icon/color.

Below the illustration is a vertical list of rounded, pill-style form rows (cards). Each row is a full-width rounded rectangle with a very light off-white / warm-grey background (#FBFBFB) and subtle inner shadow or elevation. Row structure: left side has a small 24–28px stroke icon (line icon, dark charcoal #3C3128) in its own padding; next to it is the field label text (“Name”, “Size”, “Icon”, “Color”) in a medium-weight 16px font (dark #3C3128). On the far right of each row is the field value or indicator in muted grey (#9FAEBE) — e.g., “New Beverage”, “16oz” — or a small thumbnail of the chosen icon (a tiny orange mug) or a circular color dot for the color selector. Rows have generous horizontal padding (~20px) and vertical height around 64–78px, with corner radius around 20–28px. There is a thin, subtle divider line between logical groups (a faint horizontal hairline, #F0F2F4).

Visual details and system: overall palette uses the provided colors — primary orange #E37304 for illustration and accents; secondary deep blue #0474E4 is not prominent in this screen (could be brand color elsewhere); text / icon color is deep charcoal #3C3128; backgrounds and cards use near-white #FBFBFB; secondary text / placeholders use #9FAEBE. Typography appears to follow an iOS system sans (SF Pro / rounded variant) with good weight contrast: labels = 16px semi-bold (600), values/placeholder = 14px regular/medium (500), chip/button uppercase microcopy = 12-13px semi-bold. Line-height ~18–20px for body labels.

Touch targets and states: buttons and rows use large pill shapes for comfortable touch targets (min height ~44–56px). Active/pressed states use slightly darker fill or inner shadow. The dropdown chip shows a small chevron indicating opening a list. Icons use a 2–3px stroke weight and consistent rounded line endings. Shadows: soft drop shadow under top pill buttons and subtle card shadows (rgba(60,49,40,0.06) 0px 8px 20px) to lift elements.

Spacing and dimensions (approx): safe area top 12–18px (status bar). Horizontal content inset 18–24px. Hero illustration bounding box ~300–360px square depending on device height. Inter-row vertical margin ~18–24px. Card corner radius ~24px. Button pill sizes: Cancel ~84px x 36px, Save ~84px x 40px. Icon size inside rows 24px, thumbnail preview ~28px. Divider hairline ~1px with 8–12px vertical spacing around it.

Microcopy and affordances: labels are clear and explicit (Name, Size, Icon, Color). Right-aligned value text uses muted color to show editable state but not primary. The chip “Similar to…” suggests pre-filled template/suggestion; tapping it opens a selection list. Tapping rows opens inline editor or a modal/picker (e.g., color palette or icon library). The large illustration updates live as users change icon/color selections.

Animation hints (recommended to replicate): subtle crossfade when changing the hero illustration or thumbnail (200–250ms ease-out). Buttons have quick scale-down touch feedback (120ms). Dropdown expansion uses 240ms ease-in-out with a small vertical slide and opacity fade. Card press uses 100ms color change and slight upward shadow increase.

Overall impression: clean product customization form with friendly rounded visuals, strong orange brand accent, and clear, large preview to help users visualize changes in real time.
content.layout:
Single-column vertical layout divided into three main vertical groups:
1) Header group (top strip): status bar; left aligned ghost button "CANCEL"; center chip "Similar to: ..."; right aligned solid "SAVE" button. These controls are placed in the top safe area and spaced horizontally with insets ~18–24px.
2) Hero / Preview group (center): large centered illustration (solid orange mug) occupying a large vertical portion of the screen. The illustration is centered horizontally with generous top and bottom margins to separate it from header and form rows.
3) Form list group (bottom): stacked rounded cards (pill-shaped rows). Each row is a full-width card with: left icon, label, and right-side value/thumbnail/dot. The list contains at least four rows (Name, Size, divider, Icon, Color). Rows are grouped logically (basic info rows then visual/appearance rows) separated by a faint divider line.
Columns: effectively 1 content column. Internally each list row has three informal columns: icon column (left, fixed width ~48px), label column (center, flexible), value/thumbnail column (right, fixed width ~56–72px).
Grid: none — vertical stack. No multi-column grids used.
Key layout counts: 1 main column; each row is a single grouped card; hero takes up 1 large centered block.
Keywords to describe layout: single-column, stacked-cards, hero-centered, pill-controls, top-bar-controls, full-width-rows, left-icon-rows, right-value-column, large-preview, generous-whitespace
content.functions:
Specific actions available on this screen:
- Tap the Cancel button to discard changes and navigate back. Visual: ghost pill on top-left.
- Tap the Save button to persist the beverage configuration. Visual: dark pill on top-right.
- Tap the beige ‘Similar to: …’ chip to open a dropdown or list of suggested templates; select another template to pre-fill the fields. Visual cue: chevron on the chip.
- Tap the Name row to enter edit mode (onscreen keyboard): edit the beverage name. The right area shows the current name as placeholder/value.
- Tap the Size row to open a size picker (modal or wheel picker) and change the serving size; selected size updates the right-hand value.
- Tap the Icon row to open an icon picker gallery; selecting an icon updates the thumbnail on the row and updates the large hero illustration.
- Tap the Color row to open a color picker or palette; selecting a color updates the color dot on the row and the hero illustration’s fill color.
- Visual preview: the large centered illustration updates in real-time when Icon or Color are changed to give immediate feedback.

Medium-level tasks / workflows:
- Create a new beverage template: choose a suggested template, change name/size/icon/color, preview changes, and save.
- Edit an existing beverage: adjust properties (name, size, icon, color) and save or cancel.
- Browse suggested templates from the Similar chip to copy an existing flavor and tweak properties.

Broader goal accomplished by this screen:
- The user creates or customizes a beverage product/template (likely for a drink tracker, menu, or recipe app). The screen is optimized for clarity and quick iteration — large visual preview and single-column form rows make it easy to understand the configuration and make changes before saving. The interface reduces friction by exposing common controls (name, size, icon, color) with instant visual feedback, ensuring users can finalize and save a custom beverage quickly and confidently.

content.description:
Vertical, single-column mobile list showing beverage items in large rounded “pill” cards on a very light background. Overall style: modern, minimal, friendly — lots of white space, soft shadows, large touch targets and simple flat illustrations for each beverage. Visual hierarchy is clear: bold product name (dark color) on the first line, smaller muted subtitle (caffeine amount) on the second line. Cards have full-width horizontal layout with an illustrated drink icon on the far left, two-line text block aligned left, and an optional selection control (filled circular check) aligned to the right of the card when selected. There is a small centered section heading (“EUROPE”) in uppercase and muted grey that separates groups. Top area shows the device status bar and a circular close button (white circular background with X icon) floating near the top-right, slightly overlapping content.

Color palette (derived / recommended hex):
- Screen background: #FBFBFB (very light/off-white)
- Card background: #F6F7F7 (very pale gray — use 98% white) or rgba(0,0,0,0.02)
- Primary text (titles): #3C3228 (dark warm brown / near-black)
- Secondary text (subtitles, mg info, headings): #A8A7A6 (muted grey)
- Accent / selection circle (filled): #257FE0 (deep blue) with white check (#FFFFFF)
- Accent bright (icons / brand chips): #4DCFE6 plus other bright colors used per icon (orange, green, pink) — icons use saturated flat colors for quick recognition
- Card shadow: rgba(60,50,40,0.03)

Typography (recommendation to match visual):
- Font family: System San Francisco / Inter / Roboto (san-serif). Use system font for native feeling.
- Title: 18–20pt (approx 16–18px on web), weight 600–700 (SemiBold / Bold), line-height 24pt, color #3C3228, left aligned.
- Subtitle: 13–15pt, weight 400 (Regular), line-height 18pt, color #A8A7A6, left aligned and stacked under title.
- Section header (EUROPE): 12pt, weight 600, all-caps, letter-spacing 1.2px, color #A8A7A6, centered with vertical padding.
- Close X: 16–18pt icon weight, color #3C3228 on white circle with subtle shadow.

Card / element sizes and spacing (designed for a 375pt wide phone width):
- Horizontal screen padding: 16–20pt left and right.
- Card width: full width minus horizontal padding.
- Card height: 64–76pt (comfortable touch target), corner radius: 18–22pt (pill-shaped).
- Card inner horizontal padding: 16–20pt.
- Icon (illustration) size: 28–36pt square, left aligned and vertically centered.
- Spacing between icon and text: 12–16pt.
- Title font-size: 18pt, subtitle font-size: 13–14pt.
- Spacing between stacked text lines: 4–6pt.
- Vertical spacing between cards (stack gap): 12–18pt.
- Section header spacing: 24pt above, 12pt below.
- Close button diameter: 44pt circle with 12–14pt icon, positioned ~16pt from right edge and overlapping top card area; shadow: 0 6px 16px rgba(0,0,0,0.06).
- Selection check control: 36pt circular indicator aligned to the right edge of the card (inner padding 12–16pt), filled with #257FE0 when selected, white check icon centered. Unselected state shows no control (or a subtle outline circle in #E7E9EA at 36pt) — in screenshot only selected items show filled indicator.

Icons and imagery:
- Icons are flat, minimal beverage illustrations (bottle, can, cup) rendered in single solid colors (bright saturated hues) that contrast with the pale card background. Keep them simple silhouette style with slight details.

Shadows & surfaces:
- Cards use a very soft shadow for subtle elevation: 0px 6px 20px rgba(60,50,40,0.03) and a slight inner highlight to appear slightly lifted from background.

Interactions & states (animation):
- Tap card: quick touch ripple or opacity change (150ms) and slight scale (0.98) to provide feedback.
- Selecting: when a user taps an unselected card, animate the selection check circle: fade + scale up from 0.7 to 1.0 and a 120–180ms ease-out; also animate the card background slightly to show active state (tint to 0.98 * brightness) for 180ms.
- Scroll: smooth vertical scroll with overscroll rubber banding.

Accessibility considerations:
- Ensure minimum touch target 44pt for icons and selection controls. Use sufficient contrast for primary text (#3C3228 on #FBFBFB) and readable subtitle contrast (try to keep >4.5:1 for titles and >3:1 for subtitles). Provide dynamic type support for larger fonts.

Layout notes to replicate exact composition:
- The list is a single vertical column (one card per row) with consistent left icon alignment and text baseline. Cards are grouped by region with a centered uppercase divider label. The close button floats above the list in the top-right corner (circular white surface), slightly overlapping the first visible card. The device status bar sits at the very top and should be accounted for (time on left, status icons on right).
content.layout:
Overall structure: a single vertical column (1 column) containing stacked groups of card rows. Each group is separated by a centered uppercase section header. Cards are arranged in a single-column list (rows). Count: 1 column, multiple row groups. No multi-column grid.

Card groupings: The list is visually divided into groups (e.g., default group, then a "EUROPE" group). Each group contains repeated card rows stacked vertically. There are no left-side navigation columns or sidebars.

Grid details: The layout is not a grid of columns but a repeating row grid: 1 column x N rows per group. Each row is a card with three logical horizontal regions: left icon (fixed width), middle text block (flexible width), right control area (fixed width for selection indicator). Cards align vertically so icons and text baselines line up across rows.

Spacing and alignment: consistent horizontal padding (16–20pt), vertical spacing between cards ~12–18pt, card corner radius ~18–22pt. Section header is centered horizontally and uses extra vertical margin to separate groups (about 24pt above).

Keywords to describe layout: single-column, pill-cards, vertical list, grouped sections, centered section header, left icon alignment, right selection control, generous whitespace, floating close button, full-width rows.
content.functions:
Specific actions available on this screen:
- Scroll vertically through a list of beverages — the main navigation gesture is vertical scrolling.
- Tap a card to select that beverage; selection visually indicated by a filled circular check on the right side of the card.
- Read secondary information (caffeine amount) shown as a subtitle beneath the item name.
- Recognize groupings using centered section headers (e.g., "EUROPE") to filter mental categories while browsing.
- Dismiss the list / modal by tapping the circular close button (X) in the top-right.

Medium-level workflows:
- Browse beverages by region and visually scan icons and names to find a match quickly. Large icons and bold titles speed recognition.
- Select one or more beverages (single-select or multi-select depending on context) to add to a profile, a consumption log, or to set preferences. The UI gives clear immediate feedback on selection state and confirms the chosen item via the right-side check.
- Compare caffeine values between items because each card includes a subtitle with mg information; users can quickly compare options without deeper navigation.

Broader purpose achieved by this screen:
- Acts as a lightweight catalog/chooser that allows users to discover and pick beverages from a pre-defined list grouped by region. The design prioritizes clarity and speed: finger-friendly rows, distinct visuals per item, clear labeling, and lightweight selection controls help users make quick choices (e.g., logging a drink, setting a preference, or adding to a list). The centered section headers support discoverability and cognitive grouping for large lists. The prominent close control allows users to exit the selection flow at any point.

content.description:
Single-column, full-screen iOS-style editor for naming/renaming an item. White background (#FFFFFF) with a large centered illustrative orange mug (primary accent orange #E17306 / rgba(225,115,6,1)). The illustration sits in the upper third of the screen and is flat, slightly rounded and filled with the orange color. Below the illustration is a single-line text editing region containing the placeholder/entered text “New Beverage”. The text is currently selected (light-blue semi-opaque highlight) and shows two circular blue text-selection handles (handle color ~#0574E4). The selected text uses a bold/semibold rounded sans typeface (similar to SF Pro Rounded / or Avenir Next Rounded) colored dark navy (#322A22). The selection highlight is a pale blue (approx #D9EEFF) with the selection handles as solid medium-blue circles (#0574E4) that cast a small soft shadow to indicate touch affordance.

Below the editable text are two horizontally aligned pill-shaped buttons centered on the screen with generous spacing between them. Left button: “Cancel” — white background (#FFFFFF) with subtle inner/outer soft shadow and dark navy text (#322A22). Right button: “Apply” — dark navy rounded pill (#322A22) with white text (#FFFFFF). Both buttons are large, touch-friendly (approx 56–64px tall), have heavy corner radius (fully rounded/oval), and soft diffuse drop shadows (low-opacity, blur ~20–30px) creating a floating effect. The buttons have subtle pressed/active states: slight inner inset or reduced shadow (not visible in static screenshot).

The lower half of the screen is occupied by an iOS system keyboard (rounded keys with white keycaps and black letters). The keyboard occupies roughly 45-50% of the vertical space and overlays the bottom portion of the screen. The keyboard’s return/confirm key is highlighted blue (system blue ~#0574E4) with a white checkmark icon. The whole composition is vertically centered with large top/bottom padding to accommodate the keyboard and to place primary controls in the natural thumb zone.

Color palette used:
- Primary orange (illustration): #E17306
- Accent orange (slightly lighter accent if needed): #F97D06
- Dark navy / primary text & apply button: #322A22
- Selection handle / action blue: #0574E4
- Light neutral / soft shadow / subtle surface: #E3E3E2
- Background: #FFFFFF

Typography:
- Head / editable label: Rounded geometric sans (SF Pro Rounded / Avenir Next Rounded likeness). Size approx 28–34pt for the editable text, semibold (600) or bold (700). Letter spacing tight to normal (0 to +0.5px). Line-height single-line (1.0–1.2). Center aligned.
- Buttons: Button text ~16–18pt, semibold. Cancel button text colored dark navy; Apply button white text.
- Status/time text (top-left) uses small system font ~12–13pt, medium weight.

Spacing and sizing (approximate):
- Top safe area: ~24–32px. Illustration size ~160–220px square centered. Space between illustration and editable text ~28–36px. Text editing block height ~48–56px with left/right padding ~20–28px. Space between text and buttons ~28–36px. Button height ~56px, width each ~140–160px, gap between buttons ~18–22px. Keyboard overlays bottom area occupying ~50% height.

Visual states:

content.description:
Single-column, center-aligned mobile screen (portrait) with a clean, minimal aesthetic and generous white space. Top area: standard iOS status indicators (time left aligned, signal/Wi‑Fi/battery right aligned) on a white background. Below that, a large flat-style beverage illustration (mug with whipped top) centered horizontally. Illustration color: strong warm orange (use #E27305 or #FA7C06 for the main fill) with a small white accent for the whipped-cream curl. The illustration sits with substantial top margin (~48–72 px from top safe area) and occupies roughly 30–38% of the vertical space on a 375pt-wide canvas (approx 140–170 px square).

Below the illustration: a single-line editable text field showing the product name “Pumpkin Latte” with the caret at the right edge. Typography is rounded and friendly — use a geometric rounded display: SF Pro Rounded / Nunito / Poppins with a medium-heavy weight. Suggested sizes: headline ~34–40 px (approx 28–34 pt depending on font metrics); letter-spacing normal; line-height ~1.05–1.2. Text color is a very dark desaturated navy/brown (#342C24 or #0F2430). The input does not have a visible rectangular border; instead it uses inline editing with a thin blue caret and subtle underline focus state (accent color ~#0474E4). Placeholder/selection text styling matches the headline style.

Action area: horizontally centered row of two large pill-shaped buttons under the text. Left button: “Cancel” — white fill (#FFFFFF) with subtle inner shadow and a light gray border or raised soft shadow; label uses dark text (#342C24) medium weight. Right button: “Apply” — dark, nearly-black navy fill (#342C24 or #0F2430) with white label, medium/semibold weight. Buttons are large (height ~56–68 px, width ~140–160 px each), border-radius ~32–36 px to create a pill. Buttons are separated by 16–24 px horizontal gap and are placed inside a subtle drop shadow area (soft diffuse shadow to create depth). The entire action row sits with ~40 px vertical spacing below the input.

Bottom area: the native iOS keyboard overlays bottom ~40–45% of the screen. Keyboard keys are light rounded rectangles with white keycaps and subtle shadows. Above the keyboard there is the iOS predictive-text bar showing suggestions ("Latte", "Lattes", "Latte's"). The keyboard’s Return key is blue with a white check mark. The keyboard visually crops the page, so the bottom safe area is covered.

Spacing/padding: overall horizontal padding ~24 px from screen edges; central alignment. Use large negative space between the illustration and name to create a focus on the editable title. Visual hierarchy: illustration -> title (largest) -> action buttons (secondary) -> keyboard.

Shadows & effects: soft drop shadows for the pill buttons (blur ~30 px, 0%–20% opacity black), subtle inner bevel on white pill. Illustration is flat (no heavy gradients) but can include tiny texture speckles in a slightly lighter orange (#FA7C06) for character. Background is solid off-white (#FFFFFF or very pale #F7F7F7).

Micro-interactions/animations: when the text field is focused, animate caret blink and optionally a thin underline fade in (0.18–0.25s ease-out). Button taps animate with a quick scale down 0.96 and shadow reduction (150–200 ms, ease-out). Keyboard appearing should push content up with a smooth system animation. When Apply is successful, show a short confirmation toast or success micro-animation (tick) — 300–500 ms.

Accessibility: ensure high contrast between text and backgrounds; buttons are large for touch (min 44x44 pt). Input supports autocorrect and suggestions as shown.

Columns and groups: The visible content is a 1-column layout. The action buttons form a 2-column group inside the single column: two pill-shaped columns side-by-side (left: Cancel, right: Apply). The keyboard forms a full-width bottom container overlaying the lower portion of the single column.

Grid & spacing: Not a formal grid — use vertical rhythm with generous spacing. Vertical spacing examples (on 375pt width baseline): status bar to illustration top ~48–72 px; illustration height ~140–170 px; illustration to title ~28–36 px; title to button row ~28–40 px; button height ~56–68 px; horizontal padding ~24 px; inter-button gap ~16–24 px.
