content.description:
Single-screen screenshot showing an iOS Apple Pay confirmation bottom sheet over a blurred app background. Visual hierarchy: the background content (illustrated promotional cards) is visible but blurred/dimmed; the foreground is a centered, rounded bottom sheet that occupies roughly the lower 55–65% of the screen height and is inset horizontally by ~8–16px from device edges.

Sheet container
- Shape: rounded rectangle with large corner radius (approx. 24–32px). Smooth shadow/overlay beneath. The sheet uses a frosted glass effect (translucent white with heavy background blur). Visual fill: white at ~85–95% opacity over Gaussian blur.
- Border: subtle semi-opaque border/stroke to separate from background (#C9CACB at 10–18% opacity).
- Drop shadow: soft, nearly flat shadow with small vertical offset (blur radius ~12–18px, spread 0, color black at 8–12% opacity).
- Width: full device width minus ~16px total horizontal margin. Height: about 55–65% of screen; content scrollable vertically (visible narrow system-style scroll bar on right edge of sheet).

Top area (header of sheet)
- Left: Apple Pay brand mark (black Apple logo + word “Pay”) aligned top-left inside sheet; font weight semibold.
- Right/top corner: circular dismiss control (round white/transparent button with small 'x' icon); diameter approx 36–44px, positioned overlapping top-right of sheet interior. X icon is dark/charcoal (#0A2841 or #535150) at 60–80% opacity.

Payment method row
- A rounded rectangular list row card (subtly elevated) near the top: left shows a tiny card thumbnail image (Visa/white card) with subtle rounded corner, center displays payment method title “Revolut Visa”, right shows truncated card number “•••• 4400”. Row background: white with slight transparency, border radius 14–18px, inner padding ~14–16px. Text color: dark charcoal (#0A2841) for method name, muted grey (#535150 at 60% opacity) for card number.
- Size: row height ~64–72px. Spacing between items: ~12–16px.

Change Payment Method row
- Secondary row under payment method with label “Change Payment Method” and a chevron on the right (›). Row style matches list rows: white, rounded corners, left-aligned label in regular weight, right chevron in muted grey. Padding similar to payment method row.

Purchase details card (main body)
- A larger white rounded card containing item icon (left), title, subtitle and metadata. Left: 56–64px square app icon (rounded corners) with colorful illustration (the Waterllama mascot). Right of icon: stacked text — top line bold title “Supporter” (SF Pro Display, 17–20pt semibold), second line small grey subtitle “Water tracker Waterllama 9+” and “In‑App Purchase” (regular 12–14pt, #535150 at 60% opacity).
- Below the item block is pricing and charge type: large price text “1,99 €” (bold, ~22–26pt, #0A2841) followed by small label “One-time charge” (12–14pt, #535150 60% opacity). A faint divider line separates the content sections.
- At bottom of the card: account email in small muted text (10–12pt, #C9CACB / #535150 at low opacity).
- Card corner radius ~14–18px and internal padding ~16–20px.

Bottom confirmation area
- Centered circular blue outline icon (system pay/side-button indicator) above a small instruction label “Confirm with Side Button”. Icon diameter ~48px with simple stroke and arrow motif in light blue (#0A94FF or similar). Instruction text is centered, regular weight, ~14pt, dark grey.
- To the right edge outside the sheet (overlayed over background) is the iOS system text “Double Click to Pay” in white (or slightly translucent) vertically stacked; this text belongs to underlying system overlay and is visible because sheet is not full-screen.

Typography
- System type: San Francisco (SF Pro Display for headings, SF Pro Text for body). Use weights: Title ~Semibold/600, Body text regular 400, Secondary/muted 300–400. Example sizes: main item title 18–22pt semibold, price 22–26pt bold, body 14–16pt regular, captions 11–13pt regular.
- Line heights: 1.2–1.4x depending on weight. Text alignment: left-aligned for content; some system centered copy at bottom.

Colors
- Use the provided palette for reference and accents: deep navy/charcoal for primary text (#0A2841), mid grey for supporting text (#535150), off-white / sheet base (#F8F8F8 used as blurred background white), light border / muted grey (#C9CACB), deep brown accent (#392509) used in background illustrations. Foreground sheet white should be slightly translucent (rgba(255,255,255,0.90)).

Icons & microcopy
- Small payment card thumbnail, chevron accessory, circular close button with X, and the side-button icon at the bottom. All icons are simple line icons with ~2pt stroke, color #535150.

States / interactions
- Rows are tappable: highlight state is subtle grey overlay (rgba(10,40,65,0.04)). The sheet supports vertical scrolling; rows can be tapped to change payment method or view details. Close button dismisses sheet. Confirm action is triggered by physical side button (text instructs user). If key actions are disabled, their opacity reduces to ~50%.

Animation
- Entry/exit: sheet slides up from bottom with a spring/damping curve and a fade-in on backdrop. Duration ~300–400ms; easing: cubic-bezier(.22,.9,.32,1) (easeOutBack-like). Micro-interactions (row tap) use 120–180ms opacity change.

Other details
- There is a thin system scroll bar on right of screen (light grey track). The background app content (cards with deer illustrations) is visible above the sheet and blurred by the sheet’s backdrop effect. The whole composition uses generous spacing and modern iOS native patterns so it reads as a system modal rather than a custom full-screen form.
content.layout:
Overall layout: single-column stacked card layout inside a modal bottom sheet. The sheet itself contains a vertical stack of grouped rows/cards and a final centered confirmation area at the bottom.

Column and grouping details
- Main container: 1 primary column (the bottom sheet). Inside that column content is vertically stacked.
- Group 1 (header row): horizontal cluster that contains left-aligned Apple Pay label and right-aligned circular dismiss control (X). This is effectively a 2-column row (left content / right control) inside the top area.
- Group 2 (payment method row): single row card occupying full width of the column. Internally, this row is a three-part horizontal layout: thumbnail (left ~56px), title/body (center, flexible), trailing text (right, fixed width ~80–110px).
- Group 3 (change payment row): single full-width row with left label and right chevron (two-column row internally).
- Group 4 (purchase details card): full-width card made of a two-column sublayout for the top section (icon left ~60px, stacked text right), then full-width stacked elements below it (price row, small caption rows). Dividers separate sections.
- Group 5 (footer confirm area): single centered column with icon and caption, centered horizontally.

Spacing & grid
- Vertical spacing between groups ~12–20px; internal paddings: 14–20px all around for rows; card corner radii consistent across elements (14–32px depending on prominence). There is a small right-side system scroll indicator aligned to the device edge.

Responsive notes
- On different devices, the sheet width remains inset with consistent horizontal margins and the content scales by type size (San Francisco dynamic type). Scrolling is vertical only.
content.functions:
Specific actions users can take on this screen
- Read purchase details: users can scan the purchase card to check the item name (Supporter), description, age rating and that it is an in‑app purchase.
- Verify price and charge type: users can see the price (1,99 €) and the billing type (“One-time charge”) and their account email used for the purchase.
- Review and select payment method: users can view the currently selected payment card (Revolut Visa •••• 4400). Tap the payment method row to open a selector or edit.
- Change payment method: tap the “Change Payment Method” row to navigate to payment method management.
- Dismiss modal: tap the circular X or tap outside the sheet (if allowed) to cancel the flow.
- Scroll for more info: the sheet content is vertically scrollable when content overflows.
- Confirm the purchase: the primary confirmation is performed via the device hardware (side button double-click) — the screen instructs and waits for the user to physically confirm.

Medium-level workflows enabled by the screen
- Completing an in‑purchase flow: user verifies item and payment method, optionally changes payment method, then confirms with the side button to complete the purchase.
- Quick payment method swap: user taps change-payment, selects another card, and returns to this screen to confirm.
- Abort and return: user cancels the modal to return to the previous app view without completing the purchase.

Broader purpose
- This interface is a payment confirmation and authorization surface for an in‑purchase flow (Apple Pay / App Store purchase). The sheet’s design emphasizes clarity and safety: it surfaces the charge amount, the account identity, and the chosen payment method while providing an explicit physical confirmation step. The UI reduces accidental purchases through clear labels, a separate change-payment action, and requiring a hardware confirmation (side button), ensuring both clarity and security.

Visual style: friendly, playful, illustration-forward, soft rounded geometry and generous whitespace. The card is a rounded rectangle with a thin aqua/teal outline and very soft inner shadow; corner radius ~24–32px. The card background is a very pale cyan/ice (#E6F4F6 ~approx) while the thin border and accent lines use a bright teal (#0C7A9C). Primary CTA button is a full-width pill with saturated teal/turquoise fill (#0C7A9C) and white bold label. Secondary actions are low-emphasis text buttons (DISMISS) in a muted gray (#B2B3AA). The slider/progress track is a horizontal segmented track (4 nodes) using a light teal track and circular node markers; active node is filled teal, inactive nodes are pale. Small candy icon (round colorful) sits at the start of the slider as a visual indicator of the reward. The large right-side illustration (an Okapi-like animal wearing a patterned scarf/chain) visually overlaps the card edge and is cropped so only its upper-right body is visible — the illustration uses warm accent colors (mustard #A28809, maroon #692126, dark navy #1C1B63) that contrast with the pale card background. The overall result is a high-contrast illustration combined with soft UI surfaces.

Spacing & layout metrics (approx): Outer card horizontal margin ~20–24px from screen edges. Card vertical padding: 24–28px top, 24–28px bottom. Internal left content column width ~56–62% of card width; right illustration column ~38–44% (illustration intentionally overflows/clips). Inter-element vertical spacing: heading to body ~12–16px, body to options ~18–22px, options to price/slider ~16–20px, slider to CTA ~18–24px. Drop shadow: small soft shadow under card (rgba(12,122,156,0.08), y 6px, blur 20px) to lift it from the blurred background.

Small uppercase label (e.g., challenge label) 10–12px, 700 weight, color #A28809 (mustard). Body text: 14–16px, 400 weight, color #6F7B80, line-height 20–24px. CTA text: 16–18px, 700 weight, color #FFFFFF. Dismiss text: 12–14px, 600 weight, color #B2B3AA.

Slider nodes animate when moved or when an option is chosen: node scale from 1.0 to 1.12 and fill color transitions to teal over 160–220ms with ease-out. Dismiss is a low-contrast text button that closes the sheet.

Accessibility notes: Large CTA with high contrast, clear radio states, and visible focus outlines. Text sizes suitable for reading; maintain at least 3:1 contrast for body on background where possible.

- View the price badge (e.g., "1,99€") which updates based on selected frequency or slider.

- Tap the large teal CTA button "Get candy for creators!" to confirm the payment/donation flow; this triggers the payment/checkout workflow. 
- Tap the low-contrast "DISMISS" link to close the card without action.
- Visual recognition: the character illustration provides an incentive / reward preview; small candy icon communicates reward type.

Medium-level tasks (composed actions):
- Select donation frequency and amount tier, then submit via CTA — the UI guides the user from reading the reward description to choosing frequency, adjusting amount, and completing the support action. 
- Preview the unlockable character visually while adjusting payment options, using the illustration as feedback and motivation.
- Dismiss or defer the offer if not interested.

Broader goal (macro-level):
- This interface is a micro-conversion flow whose purpose is to convert users into supporters/paid contributors by presenting a simple, visual, low-friction payment selection and CTA. It balances persuasion (illustration and reward copy) with clear controls for choosing payment cadence and amount, and an obvious primary CTA for completing the transaction. It functions as a lightweight paywall/subscription/pledge UI optimized for mobile, encouraging one-time or recurring support and communicating the reward for doing so.

steps.name: Initiate Payment (CTA)

content.description:
Portrait mobile screenshot showing a full-screen app view with a translucent frosted-glass confirmation modal centered over dimmed content. Overall style: playful, colorful, and rounded with large illustrated cards in the background and an iOS-like system modal in the foreground.

Background / underlying screen:
- Entire screen background is lightly dimmed by a semi-opaque overlay (approx rgba(0,0,0,0.22)) when the modal is shown. The underlying content is visible but blurred/desaturated by the overlay.
- The content behind the modal consists of vertically stacked rounded cards with generous corner radii (~24–32 px). Topmost visible card is a bright yellow rounded rectangle with a deer illustration on the right and large heading text on the left (“Drop Beer Deer”). Below that is another large rounded card in light teal with an illustration of an animal peeking from the right side.
- Cards use thick inner padding (approx 20–28 px) and large type for headings. Cards have subtle inner shadows and thin border outlines (1 px, light teal/gray) to separate them from the background.
- At the top-left of the screen a circular progress/step badge appears—small circle with numeric “1” and a blue arc indicating progress. Top status bar shows 9:41 and iOS-style status icons in white.

Foreground modal (primary focus):
- Modal is a centered rounded rectangle with heavy corner radius (approx 18–28 px). It uses a frosted glass effect: a semi-opaque white fill with strong blur and slight translucency so the background imagery is visible behind it. The modal has a soft outer drop shadow (vertical offset ~6–12 px, blur 18–28 px, rgba(0,0,0,0.20)).
- Width: ~78–86% of screen width. Height: compact (about 140–190 px). Positioned slightly above vertical center so the OK CTA sits clearly above the underlying large card’s content.
- Modal content is vertically stacked and center-aligned: 
  - Title line: “You’re all set” — large, bold, left-aligned inside the modal. Typography approximates Apple SF Pro (or similar humanist sans). Size ~20–22 px, weight 700. Color: near-black #000000 (or very dark gray).
  - Body text: “Your purchase was successful.” — regular weight, ~14–16 px, line-height ~20 px, color medium gray (#6B6B6B).
  - Primary CTA: large pill-shaped blue button labeled “OK”. Button fills almost the full modal width horizontally with left/right padding and large corner radius (~28–32 px). Button height ~48 px. Button color is vivid saturated blue (approx #0A74FF to #007AFF) with a subtle vertical gradient and inner gloss. Button label is white, medium-large (approx 17–18 px, weight 600).
- Modal interior spacing: title has ~16 px top padding, body text ~8–10 px below title, then ~18–22 px to the CTA. Horizontal padding inside modal ~18–20 px.
- Visual treatment of button states: default shows saturated blue with faint inner shadow; pressed state scales to 0.98 with darker blue overlay; disabled state would be desaturated gray (not shown).

Typography & spacing:
- System-like sans (SF Pro or similar) used: heavy for title, regular for body. Hierarchy is clear: title ~22 px semibold/bold, body ~15 px regular, button label ~17 px semibold.
- Generous whitespace and consistent rounded corners across elements provide a soft, friendly look.

Colors (observed / approximated):
- Primary dark teal/blue (used in badges, accents): #10476D (provided main color)
- Very light neutral background / card background: #DCDAD7 (provided)
- Warm accent / mustard-yellow card: #A76E05 (provided)
- Muted gray-brown for secondary text: #918E8A (provided)
- Deep accent / maroon details: #52171B (provided)
- Modal white/frost: #FFFFFF with opacity ~0.92 and blurred background
- CTA primary blue: approx #007AFF (approximation; bright saturated blue)
- Overlay dim color: rgba(0,0,0,0.22)

Iconography & illustrations:
- Playful illustrated animals (vector-style, flat with subtle texture) appear inside cards. Illustrations use saturated colors and occupy right side of each card with the heading text left-aligned.
- System icons in the status bar (signal, Wi-Fi, battery) are white.

Microinteractions / animations (inferred):
- Modal likely animates in with a combined fade and scale (scale from 0.96 to 1.0) and backdrop blur fade over ~240–320 ms using an ease-out cubic curve (e.g., cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)).
- Button has quick tap feedback: brief scale/opacity change (120 ms) and an active color change.
- Underlying cards may have subtle parallax/blur while modal is open.

Accessibility notes:
- Contrast: title and button label are high contrast (dark/white on bright blue); body text is medium contrast but readable against the semi-opaque modal background. Large rounded touch targets for primary CTA (height ~48 px) support easy tapping.
content.layout:
Overall layout is a vertical single-column stack behind a centered modal overlay. Detailed structure:
- Root container: full-screen portrait (one main column).
- Background layer (layer 1): a vertical stack of large rounded cards (each card spans nearly full width with left/right margin ~16 px). Count of visible card rows: at least two visible stacked cards (top yellow card, second teal card). Cards have inner content arranged as a two-column layout: left column for heading text and small controls (one-time/monthly, price), right column reserved for an illustration that overlaps card edge.
- Foreground modal layer (layer 2): centered floating panel with single-column content: title, body text, and a full-width CTA button. Modal is not full-width — it uses horizontal margins that align visually with underlying card padding.
- Overlays: a semi-opaque full-screen scrim sits between background and modal to dim and de-emphasize background content.
- Minor components: a small circular step/progress badge is positioned near the top-left corner of the screen, overlapping the top card (this is a floating element not in the main stack). The status bar is fixed at top.

Columns & grouping: 
- Primary grid is 1 column for main vertical flow.
- Each card internally behaves like 2 columns: left text column (~60–70% width) and right illustration column (~30–40% width) with the image often breaking the card bounds for visual interest.

Spacing & alignment:
- Cards have consistent vertical spacing between them (~20–28 px). Modal uses centered alignment with symmetric horizontal padding (~18–22 px). Text inside modal is left-aligned but visually centered within the modal block; CTA is horizontally centered.
content.functions:
Small, specific actions available on this screen:
- Tap the primary CTA (“OK”) to dismiss the confirmation modal. The button provides clear visual affordance (full-width pill button, high contrast) and immediate feedback on tap.
- Read the confirmation text: user can scan the title and supporting text to confirm the purchase outcome.
- Observe the underlying content (cards) through the translucent modal; while the modal is active, underlying interactive elements are visually de-emphasized and not tappable.

Medium-level tasks / flows enabled by the interface:
- Complete a purchase flow: this modal appears as the final confirmation after the user selects purchase options (e.g., one-time vs monthly) and taps a purchase button. It confirms success and provides a simple way to continue.
- Dismiss and return to the previous screen or continue exploring promotional cards and creator offers. The modal’s single primary action simplifies the post-purchase decision (dismiss or acknowledge).
- Scan visual progress: the small circular badge/step indicator at the top-left and progress nodes on the underlying card allow users to see where they are in a multi-step or points progression.

Broader purpose / outcome supported by this screen:
- The screen’s ultimate goal is to provide clear, immediate feedback that a financial transaction was successful and to let the user acknowledge that result and continue interacting with the app. The design prioritizes clarity (succinct success copy), low friction (single prominent CTA), and reassurance (friendly visuals + confirmation message). The modal ensures the message is prominent and unambiguous while preserving context by keeping the underlying content visible.

content.description:
Overall style: A clean, playful mobile splash/welcome screen with large rounded display typography and a central hand-drawn / flat vector mascot illustration (an okapi wearing a patterned coat). The composition is minimal with large white negative space, bold two-line headline at the top-left/center, a large mascot illustration occupying the middle area, and a small brand block (square app icon, brand name, and short tagline) positioned near the lower third. Style language: friendly, childlike, illustrative, rounded corners and soft shapes, saturated playful color palette.

Color palette (primary colors used / approximate HEX):
- Cyan / Teal for "Water" text and tagline accent: #1EC7E2 (provided)
- Bright purple/lavender for second part of headline: #A676FF (visual match; developer-provided pink/purple: #E05CA5 also present for accent)
- Deep blue (accent / potential CTA / small text): #153A8C (provided)
- Warm golden yellow decorative trim on mascot: #D4B934 (provided)
- Dark brown for okapi fur/outline detail: #311F1D (provided)
- Background: solid white #FFFFFF

Typography:
- Display / headline font: heavy, rounded display (examples: Fredoka One, Baloo 2, or Nunito ExtraBold). Two-line headline layout where each word group is visually separated by color. Font weight: 700–900 (extra-bold). Letter spacing: -0.5 to 0 px for compact look. Line height: ~0.9 of font size to keep lines tight and stacked.
- Headline sizes (on standard 375pt wide mobile): first line approx 56–72 pt; second line approx 56–72 pt — visually balanced to occupy the top quarter of the screen. If converting to px at @2x, headline size ~112–144px.
- Subhead / brand name: semi-bold grotesque (e.g., Inter/SF Pro Display SemiBold) ~16–18 pt, color #153A8C or near-black.
- Tagline: friendly rounded sans, medium weight ~16 pt, color #1EC7E2, letter spacing 0.2–0.5 px.

Mascot illustration:
- Full-bleed center-left aligned vector illustration of an okapi occupying roughly 45–55% of vertical space. The illustration uses flat fills with subtle internal shape shadows and patterned clothing (light blue coat with small pink/blue motifs and a yellow trim). Edge strokes are minimal to none; shapes are clean vector fills with small internal highlights.
- Colors for mascot: warm brown fur (#311F1D family), cream markings (#F6EDE8), light blue coat (#CFF3FA / accented with #1EC7E2), pink pattern elements (#F7C9DF / near #E05CA5), yellow trim (#D4B934).
- Small decorative charm/necklace on the okapi (letter charms) using saturated cyan and purple for contrast.

Layout & Spacing:
- Safe area: top status bar is visible (time and system indicators). Headline sits below the status bar with generous top margin (approx 48–72 pt from top edge on mobile). Left alignment of headline is slightly inset (approx 16–28 pt), but visually it appears centered-left because the headline is wide and stacked.
- Vertical flow: status bar -> large stacked headline -> mascot illustration centered in the content column -> brand block (icon + two-line label/tagline) near lower third -> large whitespace bottom.
- Headline block: stacked into two / three words ("WaterOkapi" and "Penelope" in the example). Each word group uses different color and same rounded display font. Text block has no visible background or container.
- Brand block: small rounded-square icon (approx 44–56 px) on the left, to its right a two-line text stack: brand name (dark color) and tagline (cyan). Horizontal spacing between icon and text ~12–16 px. This block sits roughly centered horizontally but lower on the vertical axis (about 60–70% down the viewport).

Element details / states:
- No visible buttons or inputs on this screen; interaction likely tap-to-continue or auto-transition. If interactive, a subtle fade-in animation for headline and illustration on load is expected.
- Illustration entry animations: a gentle scale-from-0.95 to 1.0 and opacity 0 -> 1 over 400–600ms with an ease-out cubic (e.g., cubic-bezier(.22,.9,.33,1)). Headline has a staggered slide-up and fade-in (duration 350–500ms, easing ease-out).

Iconography & small elements:
- App icon uses stacked colorful shapes (rounded blobs) inside a rounded square. App icon corner radius ~12–16 px on a 44–56 px square.
- No visible navigation controls or bottom tab bar. Status bar remains visible.

Pixel / measurement guidance (for 375 x 812pt reference):
- Top safe area: 44pt (status bar) + 24pt margin -> headline top at ~68pt.
- Headline height: ~160–200pt block (two lines combined).
- Mascot illustration bounding box: width ~310–340pt, height ~360–420pt; centered horizontally with slight left offset so illustration and headline visually balance.
- Brand block height ~56pt from its top to bottom, placed with its top at ~540–580pt.

Accessibility notes:
- High contrast between headline colors and white background; ensure purple/cyan meet AA contrast where used for functional text. The small brand name should use the deep blue #153A8C or near-black for legibility. Provide alt text for the mascot for screen readers (e.g., "Illustrated okapi mascot wearing a patterned coat – Penelope").

Replication summary: Use a rounded heavy display font for the headline with split-color treatment (cyan for the first word, purple for the next line). Place a large flat vector mascot centrally below the headline. Add a small brand block (rounded-square icon + brand name + cyan tagline) near the lower third. Keep everything on a white background and use generous vertical whitespace. Add subtle entrance animations: staggered fade/slide for headline and scale/fade for illustration using 350–600ms easing out.
content.layout:
Overall layout: single-column vertical layout (1 main column). Visual hierarchy flows top-to-bottom: status bar -> large stacked headline (two lines) -> large mascot illustration -> small brand block (icon + name + tagline) -> white space.

Columns and groups: 1 column. Within that column there are 3 main grouped vertical blocks: 1) Headline group (multi-line text block) 2) Illustration group (large vector) 3) Brand block group (icon + two-line text). The illustration group is the largest and visually dominant.

Grid / alignment: center-aligned composition with slight left bias for the headline and illustration to visually balance each other. Use a 12-column invisible grid for alignment on large devices if needed, but on narrow mobile it behaves as one centered column with 16–24pt side gutters.

Spacing: large vertical gutters between groups (approx 24–48pt on mobile, scaled proportionally). Generous bottom whitespace to create a calm, spacious feel.

Keywords describing layout details: centered column, stacked blocks, single-column, generous whitespace, top-left headline bias, centered illustration, lower third footer block, large hero, minimal chrome.
content.functions:
Specific visible actions on this screen: users can read the headline and tagline, observe the mascot illustration, and (implicitly) tap or wait for the app to continue to the next step. Visual cues: large headline and mascot build brand recognition; the small brand block suggests the identity and the CTA that follows will be related to hydration.

Medium-level tasks supported: this screen acts as an entry/welcome/branding step. It prepares users for onboarding or sign-in by introducing the brand personality and tone. From here users would be transitioned to authentication, onboarding checklists, or the main product flow. The design supports recognition (big logo/name), trust (consistent brand colours and friendly illustration), and lightweight conversion (readable brand name + tagline encouraging the product promise: "Stay hydrated & happy!").

Broader user goals achieved: primary purpose is brand introduction and first-impression — it communicates product identity, core messaging (hydration/wellness), and sets user expectation. Secondarily it functions as a launch/splash screen that bridges app cold-start to interactive content. The screen is optimized for clarity and emotional connection rather than direct task completion; it funnels users towards deeper flows (create account, sign in, or continue to app content) while delivering delight and memorability.

steps.name: Purchase Success Modal

content.description:
Full-screen mobile share modal / overlay with a centered preview image and four large, rounded “share” action buttons stacked vertically. Background: very light off-white / near-white (#FBFFFF or #FCFEFE) with subtle top-to-bottom soft gradient fade. Top area shows the native status bar (time left aligned, cellular/Wi‑Fi/battery icons right). Top-right is a circular floating close button (white circle, subtle drop shadow, inner X icon in dark bluish-gray #2F3A40).

Centered preview card: a vertical rectangular mockup centered horizontally with generous top margin. The preview has a 6–8 px light gray border (#DADADA) and rounded corners (~6px). Inside is an illustration (an okapi in patterned sweater) and a small brand mark / URL near the lower-left of the preview. The preview sits on a white canvas and has a subtle inner padding and no heavy shadow — the border defines it.

Below the preview is a short instruction / caption block, center aligned: first line “Sharing to social?” (system font, medium weight), then an emoji, then “Tag us & we'll reply!” — secondary line displays the brand handle in bright teal / cyan (#0BB8D1 or #00B3C4) as a tappable handle. Text color for the primary caption is dark gray (#2F3A40). Font is the iOS system/SF Pro (or Inter) with sizes approximately: caption headline ~16–18pt semibold, handle ~16pt medium and colored.

Primary actions: four full-width pill buttons stacked vertically with generous spacing (~16–22px). Each pill is a large rounded rectangle (height ~64px, border-radius = height/2 for fully rounded ends), internal horizontal padding ~20–24px. Left inside each pill is a circular or rounded-square platform icon (platform logo in a compact container). To the right of the icon is the label text (platform name) in a bold/semibold weight. Buttons use pastel-filled backgrounds that match each platform’s visual identity in soft tints:
- Messages: mint / light green background (#DFFCF0 -> approximate #DFFCF0). Icon: iMessage bubble green gradient; label text: bright green (#00C853 or #00B140). 
- Messenger: light lavender background (#EEF0FF). Icon: messenger gradient (purple/blue); label text: deep blue/purple (#5B4AF0 or #4C3EDD).
- Instagram: soft pink background (#FFEAF0). Icon: Instagram gradient square; label text: warm magenta/pink (#FF3B7A).
- Facebook: pale blue background (#EAF6FF). Icon: Facebook round; label text: Facebook blue (#1877F2).

Button visual details: icons sized about 36–42px square; label text size ~20–22pt semibold, left aligned vertically with icon; buttons have subtle inner shadow or soft glow to separate them from background. Each pill's content is horizontally centered with left icon + text block. Buttons are large, high-contrast labels to be comfortable for touch.

Spacing & alignment: everything is center-aligned on a single vertical column. Left/right margins from screen edges ~28–36px. Visual rhythm: top status area -> preview card -> caption -> handle -> stacked action buttons -> bottom padding. Colors are pastel and friendly, with saturated label colors for clear affordance. Typography uses system rounded sans (SF Pro or Inter), weights: captions regular/medium, buttons semibold.

Micro-interactions & states: on press, pill button animates with a slight scale (0.97) and a short shadow increase; active state darkens the label color and slightly deepens the background tint. Disabled state (if present) reduces opacity to 40%. The close button has a tap target of ~48px and gives a subtle press feedback (scale and shadow). Entry animation: modal content slides up from bottom with a small overshoot easing and buttons fade/slide in staggered (delay 40–80ms between each).

Overall style: friendly, playful, minimal, and tactile — pastel color palette, large touch targets, rounded shapes, clear platform branding. The illustration-centered preview keeps focus on shared artwork while the actions below are designed for fast thumb reach and recognition.
content.layout:
Single-column vertical layout centered on screen. Layout groups:
- Top cluster: native status bar area (time left aligned; signal, Wi‑Fi, battery right). A floating circular close button sits in the top-right overlapping safe area (one floating element).
- Content column: centered preview card (one column wide) — it occupies about 50–60% of the screen height in this layout. The preview is a framed rectangle with uniform border and rounded corners.
- Caption group: two-row center-aligned text block (headline + handle) directly below the preview with moderate spacing (~20px).
- Action group: stacked grid of 1 column x 4 rows (four pill-shaped action buttons). Each row is one full-width pill button with consistent height (~64px) and vertical spacing (~16–22px). Buttons are grouped as a single block with equal widths and consistent internal horizontal padding.
- Bottom spacing: generous bottom padding to keep last button above device home indicator.

No multi-column structure — the screen is a single centered column. If considered as a grid, the action area is a 1x4 grid (rows x columns = 4 rows, 1 column). The overall composition emphasizes symmetry and vertical flow. Key layout details: horizontal margin ~28–36px, vertical spacing between major groups ~18–36px, pill corner radius = half of pill height (fully rounded), preview border thickness ~6px.
content.functions:
Specific actions users can take on this screen:
- Tap the circular close (X) button to dismiss the share overlay. The close button offers immediate feedback (tap highlight) and returns the user to the previous screen.
- Tap the preview image to open it full screen or to reveal additional sharing options (long press may reveal context menu such as save, copy, or share to other services).
- Tap any of the four large pill buttons (Messages, Messenger, Instagram, Facebook) to start a share flow targeted at that platform. Each button uses a platform icon + label for quick recognition. Tapping initiates the platform-specific share intent or opens the selected target with the preview attached.
- Tap the @handle link to copy the handle to clipboard or to open the brand’s profile (depending on implementation). The handle is colored to indicate interactivity and may show a tooltip or toast confirming copy.

Medium-level tasks that combine actions into workflows:
- Quickly choose a destination (one of the large buttons), confirm (if needed) and send the preview to a contact or feed — the UI supports a two-tap flow: choose destination > select recipient/share. The large, clearly labeled buttons minimize errors and speed up decision-making.
- Dismiss or cancel the share operation with the close control, or tap the preview to edit/crop before sharing (if editing flow is provided).
- Tag the app/brand on the chosen social platform by tapping the handle or following the on-screen prompt — the caption encourages tagging and user engagement.

Broader goal enabled by this screen:
- The primary goal is to let users share the generated content (illustration/poster) to external social and messaging platforms quickly and comfortably. The screen reduces friction with large touch targets, brand-consistent cues, and a clear linear flow (preview -> prompt -> destination buttons). It also promotes social engagement by nudging users to tag the brand handle, increasing discoverability and responses from the brand. Accessibility and clarity are supported via high contrast labels, large tap zones, and predictable button states.

steps.name: Unlocked Character Splash
steps.goal: Show the unlocked reward and give sharing affordances
steps.action: View the full-screen reward illustration; tap screen or a CTA to continue to sharing options or collection
steps.system_response: A share screen/preview appears (thumbnail + sharing buttons) and the new character is marked as unlocked in the user's inventory.

content.description:
Two stacked content sections presented inside a full‑screen mobile modal/overlay with a white/very‑light cream background (approx. #FBFAF9). Top system status bar is visible (time, signal, wifi, battery). Top-left a small rounded white pill button labelled "SHUFFLE" in a dark slate font; top-right a circular white close button with a dark X icon. Large section title row: a dark rounded badge containing a fraction (e.g., "0/10") followed by a large headline “Holiday Challenges” in a bold, rounded sans-serif (heavy weight). Subhead paragraph below in mid‑gray describing the section (regular weight, comfortable line-height). Under the subhead is a 2‑row grid composed of 10 rounded rectangular tiles (5 columns × 2 rows). Each tile is a soft pastel background (pale pastel variants across tiles) with a thin inner outline of an animal silhouette as a placeholder for locked content (very low contrast gray stroke). Tiles have large corner radius (~14–18px), subtle inner shadow or inset stroke and light drop shadow. The tiles are spaced evenly with consistent gutters and padding; tiles appear disabled/ghosted (low saturation) when locked.

Below, a second section with the same structure: a colored circular/rounded badge with a fraction ("2/6") in bright cyan/turquoise (#2EC2E0) on a matching filled pill background, followed by the headline “Supporter” in the same bold rounded font but in cyan, and a short explanatory subhead in mid‑gray. Under that is another horizontal row of 5 rounded tiles (same size/style) showing silhouettes as locked placeholders. Two tiles in the supporter grid are unlocked: small illustrated full‑color characters inside the rounded tile (full-bleed centered illustration with white/very pale blue tile background). One unlocked tile (lower-left) is emphasized with small cyan confetti dots or animated particles surrounding it to suggest unlocking or celebration. The illustrated characters are playful, slightly stylized vector illustrations with soft shadows. 

Spacing and alignment: generous top/bottom whitespace; main content centered left-aligned headline and left margin equal to grid left edge. Typography: headline approx. 28–36px (large mobile H1), heavy weight (700–800), rounded geometric sans (e.g., similar to Nunito/Quicksand/Rounded Pro). Subhead text ~15–17px regular (400) with 1.4 line-height and mid-gray color (#7D6B62 or #7B7B7B). Badge text ~13–15px white on colored pill; pill background dark navy for the first badge (#342F2F) and cyan for the second (#2EC2E0). Tile size: visually ~64–90 px square on mobile with 12–16px internal padding and corner radius 14–18px. Grid gutters ~12–18px. The "Shuffle" button is small (about 80–100px wide, 34–40px tall) with subtle rounded corners and a dark text color. The close button is a 44px circle with center X icon.

Color palette: background very pale cream #FBFAF9; dark headline/nav color #342F2F; supportive midgray #7D6B62; accent bright yellow (used elsewhere) #D6BB11 (not dominant on this screen); cyan/turquoise accent #2EC2E0 used for the Supporter badge and headline; tile pastels are low‑saturation variants (pale pink, pale blue, pale green, pale lavender) approximately RGBA whites with slight hue. Tile silhouette stroke: pale gray #CFCFCF. Illustrations: multi‑color vector palette with saturated colors but kept on soft pale tile backgrounds. Shadows: subtle soft drop shadow (rgba(18,21,25,0.06)) under tiles. 

States & affordances: Locked tiles use an outline silhouette and low opacity to indicate incomplete/locked; unlocked tiles show full color illustration, slightly larger saturation, and occasionally celebratory particles. Tapping a tile likely shows detail modal or unlock flow. The fraction badge visually communicates progress; badges use high contrast colors to draw attention. The layout is mobile-first and breathes with generous whitespace.

Animation suggestions: micro‑interactions on unlock: small confetti particle burst (20–30px dots) with ease-out cubic for 600–900ms; tile press uses a quick scale down (0.96) and scale up with 140ms ease-out; badge count may animate numerically when updated with a 300ms counter easing; the modal close uses fade plus slide‑down 240ms ease-in-out.
content.layout:
Mobile full-screen single column scroll layout with two main stacked content groups. Each content group has: left-aligned horizontal header row (badge + headline) followed by a short descriptive paragraph and a fixed 5-column tile grid. Layout details:
- Overall page: single column, center-left aligned content with large vertical rhythm; content width occupies ~92–96% of safe area with side gutters.
- Header row: a small circular/rounded badge at the left (inline), headline text immediately to the right, baseline aligned. Badge size approx 36–44px tall; headline sits vertically centered to the badge.
- Subhead: block text under header with full content width and comfortable line-height.
- Tile grid: 5 columns across (equal width), with 2 rows for the Holiday Challenges group (total 10 tiles) and typically 1–2 rows in the Supporter group depending on count. Tiles are equal-sized squares with consistent horizontal and vertical gutters.
- Visual grouping: each section is a group/stack with its own top and bottom padding; sections are separated by a large vertical gap.
- Top controls: a small control row near the top-left containing the 'SHUFFLE' pill and the top-right close button. These sit above the first content group, inside the modal safe area.
Grid specifics: 5 columns, 2 rows (Holiday Challenges), 5 columns, 1–2 rows (Supporter). Gutter spacing between tiles: ~12–18px. Tile corner radius ~14–18px. Headline-to-grid vertical spacing ~20–28px. Left margin and grid left edge aligned with headline left baseline.
content.functions:
Smallest (atomic) actions users can perform on this screen:
- Tap the round X close control to dismiss the overlay.
- Tap the "SHUFFLE" pill to reorder or randomize the tiles presented (visual feedback: press state with slight darkening).
- Inspect progress badges (read-only) that show counts like 0/10 or 2/6.
- Tap an individual tile to view details about that character/challenge (locked tiles show availability hint or unlock CTA; unlocked tiles open a preview or larger art).
- Tap an unlocked tile to see its full artwork and metadata, possibly trigger an animation or larger modal.
- Tap a Supporter/Unlock CTA (not visible but implied) to start a purchase or subscription flow that unlocks additional characters.

Medium-level tasks / workflows supported:

content.description:
High-level overview
- This is a vertically scrollable single-column feed made of large rounded cards. The screen shows multiple stacked cards: a cropped red card at the top (partially visible), a full-width yellow hero card labelled “10‑DAY CHALLENGE / Drop Beer Deer”, and below it a pale-cyan rounded card (tall callout) titled “BECOME A SUPPORTER” with an illustration and a single wide pill CTA labelled “HIDE”. The UI is illustration-forward and playful, using heavy corner radii and generous white space.

Color palette (from provided colors + supporting values)
- Primary navy/purple: #2D2D94 (used for heavy text, small accents)
- Accent cyan (bright): #05BCEB (used for small progress accents and icon highlights)
- Warm yellow: #E3B80A (hero card background)
- Deep maroon: #912026 (top card background / decorative)
- Pale blue: #9CC1EF (supporter card border / very light fill)
- Background / card interior white: #FFFFFF
- Supporter card very light fill (derived): #EAF9FC (approx; used for large pale panel)
- Text dark (for high contrast): rgba(0,0,0,0.85) for smaller text; large teal/cyan headline: #05BCEB or slightly darker #00AFCF depending on contrast needs.

Typography
- Font family: friendly rounded geometric (suggest Quicksand / Poppins / Nunito). Use the same rounded family across the screen for harmony.
- H1 / hero title (e.g., “Drop Beer Deer”): 28–32 pt, Weight 700 (Bold), letter‑spacing normal, left padding inside card, color #FFFFFF on the yellow hero.
- Small uppercase label (e.g., “10‑DAY CHALLENGE”): 12–14 pt, Weight 600, letter‑spacing 1.2px, color: slightly desaturated purple (#2D2D94 with 40% opacity) or a muted variant of the card background.
- Supporter card header (“BECOME A SUPPORTER”): 12–14 pt, Weight 700 (uppercase), tracking +1px, color #05BCEB (or darker teal) centered.
- Body text (supporter message): 20–24 pt, Weight 700 (semi-bold), center-aligned, line-height 1.1–1.3 (tight but readable). Color: #05BCEB / teal for emphasis.
- CTA label (“HIDE”): 16–18 pt, Weight 700, uppercase, center aligned, color #05BCEB (or darker teal) on a very pale cyan pill background.

Layout and spacing
- Single column, full-bleed to phone safe area with 16–20 px horizontal margins inside each card.
- Vertical spacing between cards: ~24–36 px; top of yellow hero is 12–16 px below top red card crop.
- Yellow hero card: full-width within safe margins, height approx 120–140 px, large corner radius 24–32 px, internal left padding 24 px (title left-aligned), image/illustration anchored to right edge and cropped.
- Supporter card (pale cyan): tall panel, occupying most of remaining viewport height. Outer border: subtle 2 px stroke in #9CC1EF (pale cyan) with large radius 22–30 px. Internal padding: ~28–36 px top and sides. Inner content is vertically stacked and center aligned: small header, small mascot illustration (center), large centered message text, large pill CTA near bottom.
- CTA pill: width 70–80% of card width, height 48–56 px, corner radius 28 px, filled with very pale cyan (#EAF9FC) and subtle inner shadow. Text is bold, teal (#05BCEB).
- Small floating controls: top-left circular badge (brown circle with small blue progress arc, diameter ~44 px), top-right circular pink/peach round icon (diameter ~44 px) with a wavy icon inside.

UI elements & states
- Cards are touchable; hover state not shown (on mobile: press opacity change 0.85). Active/tap: slight scale down (0.98) and shadow increase.
- CTA pill states: default (pale fill + teal text), pressed state (darker fill #9CC1EF, white text), disabled (opacity 40%).
- Supporter card close/dismiss via the HIDE button removes the card with a 240ms slide-down + fade-out (ease-out cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)).
- Scrolling: vertical momentum scrolling; cards should have subtle elevation (shadow) when separated from background.

Imagery & icons
- Mascots are flat/vector illustrations with simple shading — deer on yellow card (right-aligned) and three fluffy mascot faces centered on the supporter card.
- Small badge top-left is a circular progress indicator with a partial cyan arc (uses #05BCEB) and a brown circular background.
- Top-right round control is a pink circular button (peach gradient) with a dark wavy icon in center. Both are elevated, cast tiny shadow.

Microcopy & tone
- Playful, friendly tone. Big, bold center-aligned messages to communicate gratitude and calls to action.

Accessibility
- Ensure sufficient contrast for the main CTA text on its background; if teal text on pale cyan is low contrast, invert CTA to teal fill with white text when needed.
- Large readable font sizes for the main message (20–24 pt) and clear tappable areas (≥44×44 px for circular buttons).

Developer handoff notes
- Provide SVGs for all mascot illustrations and exported PNGs for preview. Use rounded corner constants (30 px) for consistent radii. Export the pale cyan panel as a component with configurable copy and illustration slot. Provide motion specs for card dismiss (240ms ease-out) and subtle press scale (98%).
content.layout:
Overall layout
- Single-column vertical layout (one main column). All content is stacked vertically from top to bottom.
- There are 3 visually distinct vertical groups observed:
  1) Top status / cropped hero group (partial red card visible at very top, acts as previous list item). This occupies the first band of the column.
  2) Middle hero card group (yellow 10‑day challenge card). Full width within safe margins; acts as a primary card in row 2.
  3) Supporter callout group (pale cyan tall card). Large panel occupying most of the bottom area of the viewport.
- No multi-column grid; not divided into sidebars. The screen is a single column with nested vertical stacks inside each card.

Card internals
- Yellow hero card: 1 row internal layout — title text left, decorative illustration anchored to the right. Use flex layout: horizontal container, title left (flex: 1), image right (fixed width ~30–40% of card).
- Supporter card: single-column stack (center aligned). Sub-rows inside: small uppercase header; mascot illustration row; large multi-line message row (centered); CTA row (centered pill button).

Counts and grouping
- Columns: 1 main column.
- Groups of columns: none (single grouped column only).
- Grid: vertically repeating list; effectively a 1-column grid with N rows (here you see at least 3 rows / cards).

Spacing & padding (approx)
- Outer safe area margins: 12–20 px from device edges.
- Card horizontal padding: 20–24 px.
- Card corner radii: 24–30 px on hero and 28–34 px on the supporter panel.
- Gap between vertical groups: 20–36 px.

Keywords to describe layout: single-column, stacked-cards, large-hero, centered-content, wide-pill-cta, full-width-cards, generous-white-space, illustration-led, rounded-corners, floating-controls
content.functions:
Specific actions (micro-interactions)
- Scroll vertically through a stack of content cards (tap or swipe).
- Tap a hero/challenge card (e.g., the yellow “Drop Beer Deer” card) to open details for that challenge.
- Tap the circular badge (top-left) to view progress or streak details; it visually indicates a numeric state ("1").
- Tap the round pink control (top-right) to open a menu or context actions (likely filter/overflow).
- Read the supporter message and press the large pill CTA labeled “HIDE” to dismiss this supporter callout.

Medium-level tasks (workflows)
- Browse challenges: user scrolls through cards, identifies an interesting challenge (visually prominent hero card), and taps to view or join the challenge.
- Manage in-screen hints/promotions: user can dismiss promotional/supporter messages with the prominent HIDE CTA; the system remembers preference and collapses or hides the panel on future visits.
- Access contextual actions: use the small floating icons for quick access to profile/filters/progress without leaving the feed.

Broader user goals
- Discover engaging, illustration-rich challenges and content quickly through large hero cards.
- Receive contextual messaging from the product team (supporter ask / donation gratitude) and control whether those messages remain visible.
- Stay oriented and access secondary actions (progress, menu) via small persistent floating controls. The screen facilitates discovery and light interaction with strong visual hierarchy and clear single primary action per card (tap to view, or dismiss/hide for promo).

records.name: Apple Health Sync Setup
records.description: Happy path: A signed-in user navigates from the app's settings list to enable two-way synchronization with Apple Health. The user taps the 'Apple Health Sync' row, views a short product-modal explaining sync, and follows a two-step onboarding screen which then triggers the iOS Health permission sheet. After granting permission, the app shows the sync settings screen with a toggle and an optional 'Sync all-time data now' action. The user starts a full data sync, sees a progress modal, and receives a success confirmation when finished. Entry point: Settings list where "Apple Health Sync" is listed. Exit point: Success confirmation and returned settings screen. Assumptions: user is on an iOS device with Apple Health present and the app has network access; user is at the settings area and not currently syncing.
records.problem: User task (user perspective): Turn on automatic synchronization between this app and Apple Health so intake data (water, caffeine, alcohol, etc.) is exported to and imported from Apple Health. The user expects clear guidance, required iOS permissions, an option to sync historical records, visible progress, and a confirmation of completion. System task (interface perspective): 1) Present an entry point to start Health sync. 2) Educate and request consent via an in-app modal and an instructional screen. 3) Launch the iOS Health permission sheet and capture the user's allow/deny choice. 4) Persist the enabled sync setting and expose a manual 'Sync all-time data' action. 5) Run a background sync operation while keeping the app open, show progress (records count and spinner), and show success/failure feedback. End result: User-perceived outcome — Health sync enabled and historical data imported/exported with a success message. System-level outcome — app obtains HealthKit write/read permissions, sets an internal sync flag, and imports/exports the specified data types; a background process completes record-by-record sync and reports completion.

steps.name: Settings - Health Row
steps.goal: Find and open the Apple Health synchronization option in settings.

steps.system_response: App navigates to or presents the first in-app modal / onboarding for Apple Health Sync.

content.description: Full-screen vertical settings list styled for iOS: single-column, full-bleed layout with a very light background (#FBFBFB). Each setting is represented as a rounded rectangular card (soft corner radius ~20–24px) that spans almost the full width with horizontal side insets (~16–20px). Card background is slightly off-white / white (#FFFFFF) and sits on top of the page background with a very subtle drop shadow (blur ~8px, spread 0, color ~#EDEDED at 8%-12% opacity) or an inset ambient outline to create separation. Inside every card, on the left there is a circular or rounded square colorful icon (approx. 36–44px) with a pastel fill (examples seen: pink stopwatch, yellow flame, orange ruler, purple speaker, blue cloud) and often a small icon glyph centered inside the circle. Icon colors include accent tones consistent with the provided palette: sky blue (#40C1F7), warm yellow/gold (#DFCC49) and neutral greys (#9D9FA3) used for some icons and labels. Primary text on each card is left-aligned, vertically centered relative to the icon, using a heavy/semibold humanist system font (iOS San Francisco / SF Pro Text). Primary title color is a deep charcoal/dark brown (#3C3126). Font size for each row title is roughly 17–18px (semibold, 600). Subtle secondary metadata (for items that show current value like "12:00 AM", "oz", "On", "Connect") is placed at the far right of the card in a smaller size (13–15px regular) and colored light grey (#9D9FA3). A small chevron (>) or right arrow icon is placed at the far right edge of the card indicating navigation; sometimes the right-side metadata replaces the chevron visually but usually both exist (metadata + chevron). Row heights are generous for touch targets — roughly 68–86px per row with vertical padding ~18–22px. Vertical spacing between cards is approx. 12–18px. Section separators are subtle — either an empty divider with a faint horizontal hairline or more vertical spacing. The top navigation area includes a circular back button on the top-left (44px diameter, white circular background, subtle shadow) and a pill-shaped action on the top-right labeled "WHAT'S NEW" (uppercase, dark text on a white pill, rounded corners ~18px). The faint page header text at the top (very light) reads "Add/Edit Beverages" but is subdued. Overall look: soft, airy, minimal, with friendly rounded shapes, pastel iconography, and clear affordances (chevrons and right-side labels) for navigation into deeper settings screens. Interaction states: card tap -> highlight/ink (light grey) then navigate; icons and pill buttons have pressed states with slight scale or opacity change. No heavy animations visible other than standard iOS push navigation and a gentle ripple/opacity change on row tap. Typography: SF Pro Text/SF Pro Display; Title: 17–18px semibold; Secondary metadata: 13–15px regular; Top pill label: 13–14px bold uppercase; Item icon size: 36–44px; Card corner radius: 20–24px; Card horizontal padding: 16–20px.
content.layout: Single-column vertical list layout. There is one main column of full-width rounded cards inset from the screen edges. The screen uses consistent left and right content gutters (approx. 16–20px). Each row (card) contains three horizontal groups: Group A (left) = icon block (circular pastel background + glyph, 36–44px) and small left padding; Group B (center) = primary title text (17–18px semibold) vertically centered; Group C (right) = small secondary metadata text (13–15px regular) and a chevron icon indicating navigation. Rows are stacked with equal vertical spacing (~12–18px). There is a top navigation area occupying the safe-area with a back control at the top-left and a pill action at the top-right. Section breaks are represented by increased vertical spacing and a faint horizontal hairline divider. Columns: 1 primary column. Grids: none. Count of visible rows on the screenshot: 9–11 depending on screen height. Visual alignment: icons, titles and right metadata use baseline alignment so the visual center of each row is horizontally aligned. Touch target sizes: each row ~68–86px tall, icons ~44px square, chevron ~16–18px. Corner radii: cards ~20–24px.
content.functions: Small actions (per-row): - Tap a row to navigate to a deeper settings view for that specific feature (e.g., "Widgets", "App icon", "Day Reset Time, Week"). - Tap the left icon area is decorative but may also provide a preview depending on row (mostly serves as a visual marker). - Tap right-side chevron or metadata text also triggers navigation. - Tap the top-left circular back button to return to the previous screen. - Tap the top-right "WHAT'S NEW" pill to open a changelog or promotional overlay. - Some rows display the current state inline (e.g., "12:00 AM", "oz", "On", "Connect") to show the current setting without opening the detail screen. Medium-level workflows: - Browse and discover available app configuration options grouped visually as cards. - Enter a detail screen from any row to change settings (for example: change measurement units, toggle calories, set reset time, connect to Apple Health, configure Apple Watch). - Connect or authenticate external services (Apple Health Sync, iCloud Backup) from the respective detail flows. - Customize visual elements (app icon, widgets) via dedicated flows. Broader goals: This interface helps users configure and personalize the product's behavior and integrations (units, notifications, health sync, watch integration, backups) and offers quick access to each preference via an easily scannable, touch-friendly list. The design prioritizes clarity (clear labels and metadata), discoverability (icons + titles), and efficient navigation into deeper settings.

content.description:
Mobile (iOS-style) settings screen with a full-width, rounded-corner bottom sheet modal that slides up from the bottom and covers roughly the lower 55–65% of the screen. Background: the parent Settings list remains visible but is dimmed and blurred by a semi-opaque overlay (frosted effect). Underlying list rows use rounded cards with left icons and right chevrons, muted light-gray backgrounds and dark text.

Modal container: white card with a large top radius (approx. 20–28 px) and a soft drop-shadow. The top corners are rounded; the modal overlaps the underlying content. A circular close button (white circle with an X) sits near the top-right of the modal content area and visually overlaps the card edge. The modal content is vertically stacked and center-aligned.

Header: large, heavy headline reading "Apple Health Sync" (centered). Use a bold, rounded, San Francisco / system font equivalent; font-size approximately 28–34 pt (mobile-scaled), weight 700. Color is a deep desaturated navy/charcoal (very dark, near-black with cool undertone) for high contrast.

Subheader: beneath the headline a short paragraph in a muted gray (lighter than the headline) describing the action: "If you want to automatically sync your intake data with Apple Health, tap Continue below". Font: regular system, size about 14–16 pt, weight 400–500, line-height ~20 px, center aligned, color #9B9798 (provided main gray) or similar.

Icon row: a horizontal centered row containing three primary items: left: a rounded square app icon (illustration colorful stack), center: a small two-way arrow icon in cyan/blue (#05AEF8) representing sync, right: a rounded square Apple Health heart icon (pink/gradient). Each rounded square icon sits inside a subtle rounded-corner card with a very light gray background and a faint inner shadow. Icon cards size approx. 72–88 px square with radius ~14 px. Spacing: generous gap between left icon and arrow and between arrow and right icon (~24–36 px). The arrow is smaller (approx. 28–36 px high) and vertically centered.

Primary CTA: a large pill-shaped button labeled "CONTINUE" centered horizontally at the bottom portion of the modal. Button width ~60–72% of modal width (or approx. 300 px on 375 px wide screen), height ~56–64 px, border-radius large (30–36 px). Button background is a dark desaturated navy/charcoal (#3E342A is provided as a main color but actual is near-dark blue/grey) with a subtle inner shadow. Label is uppercase, white, bold (16–18 pt), letter-spacing slightly increased. Button has a subtle drop shadow and a pressed state that reduces shadow and darkens fill slightly. There is generous vertical spacing above the CTA and below the icon row.

Close control: circular button ~44 px diameter, white background, small dark X icon centered; subtle shadow; placed top-right overlapping the modal content, with ~12–16 px offset from card edge. Tapping closes the modal.

Visual style: soft, friendly, modern iOS aesthetic. Lots of white space, center-aligned content, rounded shapes everywhere. Use subtle shadows and translucency for depth. Accent colors come from the app illustration (multicolor: magenta/pink #AA568A, cyan #05AEF8, yellow #E4BC0E) and the provided gray palette (#9B9798) for secondary type.

Color palette (recommend):
- Modal background: #FFFFFF (white)
- Overlay/dim: rgba(36, 40, 45, 0.35) (dark overlay to dim background)
- Headline text: #1F2B33 (very dark charcoal/navy)
- Subheader text: #9B9798 (provided)
- Primary CTA background: #27323A or #3E342A (use #3E342A as dark accent from provided colors)
- CTA text: #FFFFFF
- Icon arrow: #05AEF8 (provided cyan)
- Illustration accents: #AA568A (pink), #E4BC0E (yellow), #05AEF8 (cyan)
- Soft card backgrounds for icon tiles: #F6F7F8 or rgba(0,0,0,0.02)

Typography (recommend using San Francisco / system font):
- Headline: SF Pro Display / system, 32 px, 700 (Bold), center, line-height 38 px
- Subheader: SF Pro Text / system, 15 px, 400, center, line-height 20 px, color #9B9798
- CTA label: SF Pro Text / system, 16–18 px, 700, uppercase, letter-spacing 1–2 px
- Small captions (list rows behind): 14 px, 500, color #27313A

Spacing & layout metrics (based on 375 px width mobile):
- Modal horizontal padding: 24 px
- Vertical stack spacing: 18 px between headline and subheader; 28–36 px between subheader and icon row; 30–36 px between icon row and CTA
- Icon card size: 80 x 80 px; icon inner padding ~14 px; arrow 32 x 32 px
- Modal corner radius: 24 px
- Close button: 44 x 44 px, placed 16 px from right edge of modal card top

States & interaction:
- Open animation: modal slides up from bottom over 320 ms with ease-out cubic-bezier (0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) and the overlay fades in (opacity 0 -> 0.35). Content elements (headline, subtext) fade/slide up with a 40–60 ms stagger.
- Close animation: modal slides down and overlay fades out.
- CTA press: scale down to 0.98 and shadow reduces over 120 ms, then revert.
- Icon tiles: lightly elevate on press (shadow increase and translateY -2 px).

Accessibility notes: large hit target for CTA and close button (44 px minimum), high contrast between CTA text and background, readable subheader, center alignment for clarity.
content.layout:
Overall structure: a full-height mobile screen with a scrollable settings list in the background and a modal bottom sheet anchored at the bottom covering ~55–65% of height.

Background layout: vertical single-column list. Each row is a full-width rounded card with left icon, middle title text, and right-side metadata/chevron. Rows stack vertically with consistent vertical spacing and side margins.

Modal layout: one column, center-aligned content group with three logical vertical sections:
  1) Header block (headline and subheader) – stacked vertically and centered.
  2) Icon illustration row – a single horizontal row containing 3 visual groups arranged in 3 columns: left icon card, center arrow glyph, right icon card. This row uses centered alignment and even spacing between the three columns.
  3) CTA area – single column centered with large pill CTA and comfortable bottom padding.

Columns / groups count:
- Background list: single-column vertical list.
- Modal icon row: effectively 3 columns (left icon, center arrow, right icon).

Grid behavior:
- Modal uses a centered vertical flow layout (not a grid). Content is constrained to modal width (screen width minus horizontal padding). Elements are horizontally centered. The modal's internal layout is one main column plus an inner 3-column icon row.

Layout details:
- Modal width: full device width with horizontal padding 24 px.
- Modal top radius: ~24 px.
- Icon row spacing: equal gaps on left and right of arrow; icon cards aligned on same baseline; arrow vertically centered.
- CTA horizontally centered with symmetric side margins and bottom margin to modal edge.

Keywords to describe layout: centered, bottom-sheet, single-column, stacked, three-column-row, rounded-corners, overlay, card-list, pill-CTA, icon-row.
content.functions:
Specific actions on this screen:
- Tap the circular close button (X) to dismiss the bottom sheet and return to the settings list. Visual feedback: the X button depresses and the modal animates downwards.
- Tap the CONTINUE button to start the Apple Health sync flow; this triggers a permission/consent dialog or navigates into the system Health permissions screen. The button shows pressed state and then either displays a loading indicator or navigates away.
- Tap anywhere on the dimmed background (optional, depending on implementation) to dismiss the modal if dismissible.
- Tap the left or right icon on the icon row (optional) to show more detail about each service (e.g., app info or Apple Health info) if implemented.

Medium-level tasks enabled by the screen:
- Begin the process of granting permission to read/write data with Apple Health so the app can automatically sync intake data.
- Learn what syncing will do via the short explanatory text and illustration, providing clarity before granting permission.
- Cancel or postpone sync by dismissing the modal and continue adjusting other settings in the underlying Settings list.

Broader purpose / user goal:
This interface is a contextual permission/feature onboarding prompt inside the app's Settings flow. Its broad goal is to get users to connect the product with Apple Health to enable automatic syncing of intake data. It reduces friction by explaining the benefit, showing an intuitive visual metaphor (app ↔ Health), and providing a single, prominent CTA to continue with the sync setup. The design emphasizes clarity, trust, and an easy one-tap path to enable the integration.

content.description: Single-column, full-screen onboarding/permission instruction. Background: solid white (#FFFFFF). Top safe area contains status bar elements (time at left; signal/Wi‑Fi/battery at right). Main headline: “Allow Apple Health Access” centered horizontally, large heavy geometric/rounded sans-serif (similar to Avenir Next / Circular), approx. 36–44px on a 375px-wide viewport, color dark brown/near-black (#382D27). Below headline are two numbered step rows. Each step row is left-aligned under the headline and includes: a circular pink badge (hot pink) with white step number inside (badge diameter ≈ 36–44px), and to its right a short instruction text in hot pink (approx. 18–20px, semibold). Step 1 text: Tap "Turn On All"; Step 2 text: Tap "Allow". Vertical spacing: headline to first step ≈ 20–28px; step rows stacked with 12–16px between them. Center of screen contains a large rounded-corner illustration/phone mock inside a cyan rounded rectangle (background tile). Cyan tile color approximates #05ABCC; tile has large corner radius (≈32px) and horizontal padding so phone mock appears inset. Phone mock silhouette is dark navy/charcoal (#382D27) with a lighter inner screen area showing an iOS Health permission modal screenshot. The inner permission modal image includes a small heart icon and the text “Health”, a magenta top-left “Don’t Allow” and top-right “Allow” hint — these are part of the embedded photo/illustration (use a clipped screenshot inside the phone mock). The mock image should have realistic inner content but visually treated as an image (drop shadow subtle). Beneath the illustration is generous white space. Bottom-center: a large rounded pill CTA labeled “CONTINUE” in all caps, white bold text (approx. 18–20px, 700 weight), pill background hot pink (match step pink), pill width ≈ 220–260px, height ≈ 56–64px, corner radius ≈ 32px. The CTA casts a subtle shadow (rgba(0,0,0,0.12)) and sits above the bottom safe area with 24–32px margin. Overall visual style: playful, friendly onboarding with large generous white space, bold headline, bright accents (hot pink and cyan), and a flat illustrated phone mock. Color palette (primary + accents): - Dark text / headline: #382D27 (provided) - Accent cyan (illustration tile): #05ABCC (provided) - Accent purple (support color if needed): #9136E8 (provided; low usage) - Accent gold (rare highlight): #CBAB05 (provided; not heavily used) - Neutral gray: #9B9BA1 (provided; for secondary text) - Hot pink (call-to-action & step badges): #FF2C7A (approx; prominent in screenshot) - White background: #FFFFFF Typography: large rounded sans-serif for headings (36–44px, 700), body/instruction text medium rounded sans-serif (18–20px, 600), secondary/help text small (12–14px, 400, color #9B9BA1). Spacing & grid: center-aligned single column; horizontal content constrained to ~320–340px on mobile with large vertical rhythm. UI elements: circular badges (36–44px), CTA pill (220–260×56–64px), phone mock (approx. 60% of content width) with 24px inner padding. States & interactions: CTA active state slightly darker hot pink; press animation: scale down to 0.98 over 120ms with ease-out. Illustration can fade/slide up when the screen appears (duration 320ms, ease-out), step badges can appear with staggered 80ms delays. Accessibility: high-contrast headline color, large tap target for CTA (≥44px high), descriptive alt text for phone mock image.
content.layout: Single centered column layout. Top safe area + status bar, then large centered headline. Under headline two stacked step rows (each a two-column inline composition: left column = circular badge; right column = instruction text). Middle area dominated by an illustrated hero block: a rounded-corner cyan rectangle (1 group) containing a centered phone mock (1 column within the tile). Bottom area contains a single centered CTA pill. Column/group counts: 1 main column; hero group contains 1 internal column for the mock. Grids: not a multi-column responsive grid — single column with centered alignment. Key paddings: left/right page margins ≈ 16–20px; hero tile horizontal margin larger to give breathing room. Vertical rhythm: large top margin above headline, moderate spacing between headline and steps, generous spacing between steps and hero, large gap between hero and CTA. Alignment: everything centered horizontally; step contents left-aligned relative to each other under the centered headline.
content.functions: Specific actions users can take on this screen: - Read instructions: users scan the headline and two numbered steps to learn how to enable Apple Health access. - Visual recognition: users view the phone mock to see exactly where the iOS permission controls are located ("Turn On All" and "Allow"). - Tap CTA: users tap the large pink CONTINUE button to proceed to the next step in onboarding or to open system settings. How UI supports these actions: - Headline hierarchy and large size make the task clear immediately. - Numbered circular badges guide attention and create a simple concrete order of operations (1 then 2). - The phone mock acts as a visual affordance showing real system UI so users can easily complete the steps in the system permission dialog. - The large pill CTA provides a single, clear next-step action with an obvious tap target and visual prominence. Medium-level tasks / workflows: - The user follows the two-step instruction to grant Health permission in the system modal (they may leave the flow briefly to interact with iOS permission dialog), then returns by tapping CONTINUE to resume or confirm. - The screen is part of an onboarding sequence (walkthrough) that ensures required permissions are granted before the product can record data. Broader goal: allow the product to access and write Health data on the device. The screen reduces friction by showing exactly which buttons to tap and by providing a single clear CTA to continue only after the user has completed the permission steps. Microcopy and visual examples reduce uncertainty and improve completion rate.

steps.name: iOS Health Permission Sheet
