content.description:
High-level overview
- This is an iOS-style permission/consent modal (bottom sheet) asking the user to grant read/write access to Health data for a third-party application. The modal covers most of the screen vertically with a generous top safe-area, rounded top corners, and a subtle blurred/dimmed background behind it.
Overall style
- Platform: iOS native (SF Pro typography, layered translucent/blur effects). Clean, minimal, heavy use of white space and rounded corner containers. Visual hierarchy is driven by large bold headings, subdued gray explanatory text and bright CTA color for the primary action.
Color palette (recommended HEX values)
- Primary CTA blue: #1083FB (Allow button main)
- Primary CTA blue (darker shade for subtle gradient / pressed state): #0A6FE5
- Toggle green (on state): #5AB743
- Accent orange (provided by developer list, not visually dominant in this specific screen): #FC8505 (can be reserve color)
- Body / heading text color (dark): #13122A
- Muted body text / secondary copy: #929493
- Card / pill background / subtle surface gray: #F6F7F8
- Dividers / subtle border: #E8E8EA
- White background: #FFFFFF
Typography
- System font: SF Pro (Display/Text)
- Sheet title (small header at very top, centered): SF Pro Display - 17pt - Semibold - center; letter spacing 0; color #13122A
- App/feature heading (“Health”): SF Pro Display - 28pt - Bold - left-aligned inside the sheet area (large visual weight) - color #13122A
- Explanatory text ("“Waterllama” would like to access..."): SF Pro Text - 17pt - Regular - line-height ~24pt - color #929493 - left-aligned, multi-line
- Section labels ("Allow 'Waterllama' to write"): SF Pro Text - 15-16pt - Medium - color #6B6B6D (slightly darker than the body muted color)
- List item title (e.g., "Alcohol Consumption"): SF Pro Text - 17pt - Regular - color #13122A
- Link / secondary control ("Turn Off All"): SF Pro Text - 16pt - Semibold - color #1083FB
- CTA button text (Allow): SF Pro Display - 17pt - Semibold - color #FFFFFF
Spacing & layout
- Screen safe area top spacing: ~24-34pt from top system status bar to sheet top content
- Modal sheet width: full device width with 20-24pt horizontal content inset on each side for internal elements
- Modal corner radius: 28-36pt on top corners (very rounded), bottom corners extend off-screen because sheet anchors to bottom
- Global vertical rhythm: 12-20pt spacing between small elements; 28-36pt between major sections
- App icon: centered below the sheet header; size ~64x64pt; rounded square container with subtle border 1px #E8E8EA; icon (heart) centered with slight drop shadow/gradient
- Large heading "Health": left-aligned, margin-left aligns with list left edge; margin-top from icon ~18-24pt
- Explanatory body copy: left aligned under heading with 12-16pt top margin; uses multi-line layout with generous line-height
- “Turn Off All” pill: horizontally full but inset from sides; height ~48pt; background #F6F7F8; rounded pill radius ~24pt; link text aligned left with 16pt left padding; blue text #1083FB
- Permission list card: a rounded rectangle with background #FFFFFF but with subtle inner shadow or blur to make it appear elevated; border 1px #E8E8EA; padding ~12-16pt; each row has an icon on the left (24-28pt), title text center-left, and a Toggle on the far right
- List rows: height ~56pt per row with subtle horizontal separator lines (#E8E8EA) between rows
- Toggle controls: standard iOS switch; on-state background #5AB743; thumb white; switch control size ~51x31px; vertical center aligned within list row
- Primary CTA (Allow): large pill-style button, full width (inset horizontally same as other edges), height ~58-64pt, background bright blue (#1083FB) with subtle linear gradient to #0A6FE5; corner radius ~30pt; white bold text centered; drop shadow: 0px 8px 20px rgba(16,131,251,0.18)
- Secondary CTA (Don’t Allow): pill-style, same width and height as primary, background #FFFFFF with subtle border 1px #E8E8EA, text color #13122A (semibold), margin-top ~12-16pt below primary
- Visual layering: the Allow button visually overlaps the list slightly in this screenshot (the list is visible behind the CTA) — implement with z-index so CTA floats above list area
Icons & imagery
- App icon: rounded square white container with heart-shaped gradient glyph (pink to red) centered.
- List icons: small blue plus icon for Alcohol Consumption, green apple icon for Caffeine, etc. Use simple 2-color line + filled icon style, ~22-28pt size, left padding ~12pt
Borders & shadows
- Subtle border for card and toggles: #E8E8EA 1px
- Buttons use soft shadow for elevation; card uses subtle inner blur to suggest layering
States
- Toggle states: ON green (#5AB743), OFF light grey track (#E6E6E6) and thumb white
- Button pressed state: slightly darker gradient and decreased shadow (e.g., scale 0.98)
Animations
- Entrance: sheet slides up from bottom over 300ms with ease-out cubic; background behind it cross-fades to a dim/blur in 200ms
- Toggles: switch flip uses iOS spring easing (~300ms) with small thumb elevation movement
- Button press: quick scale down (0.98) with 120ms spring and color darkening
Accessibility
- Large dynamic type compatibility; minimum tappable controls 44x44pt; high contrast text versions available
Pixel & asset spec
- App icon: 64x64pt inside 92x92pt rounded container; 3px inner border in #E8E8EA
- Allow button: width = device width - (2 * 20pt) ; height ~58-64pt; radius 30pt
- Toggle control: 51x31px (standard)
- Dividers: 1px hairline #E8E8EA with 12pt left inset after icon
Recreation notes
- Use SF Pro system fonts and native iOS switch component to match exactly. Use a full-screen dim + blur behind the sheet. Position the CTA button fixed near the bottom of the sheet with overlapping z-index over the permission list to match the layered look.
content.layout:
General structure
- Single-column vertical layout contained within a full-width bottom sheet/modal.
- The sheet visually divides into stacked groups: (1) compact sheet header + app icon; (2) main heading + explanatory copy; (3) a link-style action pill; (4) a section label + permission list card; (5) primary and secondary CTAs stacked at the bottom.
Columns & grouping
- Columns: effectively a single logical column for the sheet content. Internally, the permission list rows form a two-column layout per row: left column (icon + label) and right column (switch control).
- Groups: 5 stacked groups as listed above. The permission list card is a grouped component containing multiple rows (repeating pattern) each representing one permission item.
Grid & rows
- Permission list uses a single-column vertical list (rows stacked). Visible rows in screenshot: at least two full rows (Alcohol Consumption, Caffeine) plus glimpses of others below. Each row count = variable; each row height ~56pt; rows are separated by 1px dividers.
- Number of columns in rows: 2 (content area and control). Icon sits left inside content column; switch sits far right in control column.
Alignment & padding
- Horizontal padding for content: ~20-24pt left and right inside the sheet
- Left alignment for text blocks (heading, explanatory copy, list labels) except the very top small sheet header which is centered
- CTA buttons are full-width within the sheet’s horizontal padding and centered horizontally
Key layout values (approx)

- Sheet top inset from top status bar: ~24-34pt
- Icon size: 64x64pt; centered
- Heading margin-top after icon: 18-24pt
- Inter-group vertical spacing: 12-28pt depending on importance

content.functions:
Specific actions (what users can do on this screen)
- Read the request: Users can read the title, the app name ("Waterllama") and the explanatory copy stating what kind of Health data access is being requested.
- View app icon: Users can visually identify the requesting application via the centered app icon.
- Toggle individual permissions: For each health category listed (e.g., Alcohol Consumption, Caffeine), users can switch the toggle on or off to allow or disallow writing that specific data.
- Turn off all: Users can tap the "Turn Off All" pill to disable all writable categories in one action (this toggles all switches to OFF and updates visual state and internal settings).
- Scroll list: If there are more health categories than fit the visible area, users can scroll the permission list up and down to reveal additional entries and toggles.
- Confirm or deny: Users can choose the large primary "Allow" button to grant the requested permissions (persisting chosen toggles) or choose the secondary "Don't Allow" button to deny access.
- Dismissal behavior: The sheet may be dismissed implicitly when a decision is made (Allow/Don't Allow) or explicitly by swiping down on the sheet header if supported; toggles should remain interactive until dismissal.
- Visual feedback: Tapping actions provide immediate visual feedback: toggles animate; buttons show pressed state; the "Turn Off All" pill shows a pressed/highlighted state and updates toggles accordingly.
Medium-level tasks (combined actions)
- Configure selective permissions: Users can enable or disable a subset of health categories and then tap "Allow" so the app receives only the permitted categories.
- Quickly revoke all writing permissions: Tapping "Turn Off All" and then "Allow" or leaving the sheet will persist the all-off configuration.
Broader purpose
- The overall goal of the screen is to obtain explicit user consent for a third-party application to write (and possibly read) Health data. It provides fine-grained control (per-data-type toggles) and a clear primary action (Allow) and secondary option (Don't Allow) to ensure the user can make an informed choice. The layout and controls promote clarity, low friction, and immediate feedback to support secure, privacy-focused permission management.

steps.name: Sync Settings Screen
steps.goal: Show the Health sync setting state and provide the option to sync all historical data now.
steps.action: Toggle 'SYNC YOUR DATA' on/off or tap 'Sync all-time data now' to start a historical import.
steps.system_response: If toggle enabled, the app persists the sync preference. If user initiates 'Sync all-time data now', the app starts the import/export process and displays a progress modal.

content.description:
A clean single-column iPhone settings-style screen for managing an Apple Health integration. Overall style: modern, friendly, airy with lots of white space, rounded shapes, soft shadows and a prominent cyan/blue pill CTA. Layout uses a large centered page title at the top, a rules/section header row with an aligned right toggle, body explanatory copy in a neutral gray, a small inline emoji callout paragraph, a centered illustration row (two rounded-square icons with a two-way arrow between them) and a large rounded CTA button anchored toward the lower part of the safe area.

Color palette (primary + neutrals, with approximate hex codes):
- Bright cyan (CTA accent / toggle on): #09C5E5
- Vivid blue (secondary CTA gradient end): #307CFB
- Dark neutral for headings and primary text: #5D5C5D
- Medium neutral for body text (muted gray): #7F7F7F (approx)
- Accent yellow (illustration detail): #E4C405
- Accent purple/pink (illustration detail): #B0538E
- White background: #FFFFFF
- Soft light divider / faint border: #F0F0F0
- Heart/icon gradient (Apple Health heart): pink -> red gradient: approx #FF6B9A to #FF2D55

Typography (approx / recommended to match):
- Page title: rounded geometric sans (e.g., Poppins / Avenir Next Rounded), 34px, 600/semibold, letter-spacing 0, center aligned, color #5D5C5D. Generous top margin from status bar (safe area).
- Section label ("SYNC YOUR DATA"): 12–13px, 700/semibold, all-caps, left aligned, color #5D5C5D.
- Body paragraph text: 16px, 400/regular, line-height 24px, left aligned, color #7F7F7F. Copy block spans full content width with comfortable vertical spacing from header.
- Inline callout emoji paragraph: same base font 16px but slightly lighter color (#7F7F7F) and uses a small emoji at start to draw attention.
- CTA button text: 18px, 700/semibold, white (#FFFFFF), centered in the pill.

UI elements & visual specs:
- Navigation / back: circular white button (44x44 px) with subtle drop shadow, left edge inside safe area, contains a left chevron icon (thin stroke, color #5D5C5D). Positioned top-left overlapping the header area.
- Title: centered below the top area with a thin horizontal divider below it (1px line, #F0F0F0).
- Section row: left-aligned small section title "SYNC YOUR DATA" with a right-aligned toggle/switch. Row padding: 18–20px left/right, 12–16px top/bottom. Divider lines above and below the row (1px, #F0F0F0) to separate from content.
- Switch / Toggle: iOS-style rounded switch (approx 44px width x 28px height). When ON, track filled with bright cyan (#09C5E5) and the knob is white with subtle inner shadow. When OFF, light gray track with white knob.
- Body text block: multi-line paragraph with ~20–24px vertical spacing to next block.
- Illustration row: three-column visual group centered horizontally: left rounded-square icon (120x120 px container, border-radius 22–24px, white background, thin inner shadow), middle two-way arrow icon (two small cyan arrows stacked, color #09C5E5, approx 28–36px), right rounded-square icon (120x120 px). Spacing between the three items ~24–32px. Icons have large safe padding inside their rounded-square containers. The left icon is a colorful mascot/llama (multi-color: #B0538E, #E4C405, #307CFB, #09C5E5), the right icon is a pink-to-red heart gradient. Both icon containers have a subtle outer shadow (rgba(0,0,0,0.06), blur 8px) and a faint border (#F0F0F0).
- CTA button: large rounded pill in lower area, width ~82–86% of screen width, height 56px, border-radius 28px. Background uses a horizontal gradient from #09C5E5 (left) to #307CFB (right). Button has a soft drop shadow (rgba(3, 100, 200, 0.16), blur 18px, y-offset 8px). Label: white, centered, semibold. Vertical spacing above button from illustration ~56–72px and from bottom safe area ~24–32px.
- Spacing & container: horizontal content padding ~20px; top safe area ~44px; consistent 20–28px vertical rhythm between major blocks.
- States & microcopy: toggle ON state visible, CTA is enabled and visually prominent. Informational text suggests a secondary action "Sync all-time data now" and hints a possible in-progress animation (not shown), and a potential success state after sync.

Animations (if implemented):
- Toggle: smooth 200ms transition with ease-out for knob and track color.
- CTA press: quick 120–160ms scale down to 0.98 then ease back.
- Illustration arrows: small two-way arrow could have a subtle looping micro-animation (translateX ±6px) with 800–1000ms duration and ease-in-out for clarity when syncing.

Iconography & imagery: friendly, colorful mascot on the left to communicate the app brand, and the Apple Health heart on the right to show a connection. Use rounded squares for both icons to visually match iOS iconography and increase recognition.
content.layout:
Overall layout: single centered column with stacked vertical content blocks. Safe-area aware design consistent with iPhone native settings screens. Content flows top to bottom in this order: status bar/safe area -> circular back button (top-left) -> centered page title -> thin divider -> section header row with left-aligned section label and right-aligned toggle -> Body / explanatory paragraphs -> centered three-item illustration row (left icon, two-way arrow, right icon) -> large centered CTA button near bottom -> bottom safe area.

Column / group counts:
- Main layout: 1 primary content column (centered). All content uses the same column width constrained by left/right horizontal padding (~20px).
- Illustration group: effectively a 3-column inline group horizontally centered. The group contains 3 visual columns: column 1 (left rounded icon tile), column 2 (arrow symbol), column 3 (right rounded icon tile). Spacing between columns is consistent (approx 24–32px).

Grids & alignment:
- Text blocks are left-aligned within the main column for readability, while the page title and illustration group are center-aligned for prominence and visual balance.
- Section header row uses a 2-column layout within the row: label (left) and control (right). The label is left-anchored and control right-anchored, with the row taking full column width and a divider above/below.

Spacing and padding:
- Horizontal padding: ~20px each side.
- Vertical rhythm: title margin-top ~18–24px from safe area; vertical gaps between major sections range from 16–72px depending on element (tight between label and copy; wide before CTA).

Keywords to describe the layout: single-column, center-aligned title, left-aligned body, two-column section row, three-item illustration group, pill CTA, large whitespace, rounded icon tiles, toggle control, safe-area aware.
content.functions:
Specific (screen-level) actions the user can perform:
- Toggle sync on/off: the right-aligned switch allows users to enable or disable automatic data sync between the app and Apple Health. Visual feedback: switch fills cyan when ON, track/grip moves smoothly.
- Read descriptive text: the user can scan explanatory copy explaining which data types are exported/imported (Water, Caffeine, Alcohol) to understand behavior before toggling.
- Tap the back-control: the circular back button in the top-left returns the user to the previous screen.
- Trigger a manual sync: the large bottom CTA "Sync all-time data now" starts a manual full-sync operation (possibly showing progress/loader afterward). The CTA is visually dominant to encourage immediate action.
- Interpret iconography: the two rounded app icons with a two-way arrow communicate bidirectional data transfer; users can understand visually that the app and Apple Health exchange data.
- Read guidance and troubleshooting hint: the emoji callout paragraph educates about "Sync All Data" to resolve inconsistencies and sets expectations about sync duration.

Medium-level tasks / workflows supported:
- Enable continuous background sync by turning on the toggle, which configures automatic export/import and persists the state in the app settings.
- Manually reconcile data by running a one-off full sync from the CTA, used when users notice differences between the two sources.
- Understand and confirm what data types are involved in the integration through the descriptive copy — this helps users decide whether to enable sync.

Broader purpose / goal the screen achieves:
- This screen is part of integration/settings management enabling users to connect and control data flow between the app and Apple Health. It balances clarity (explanatory text and friendly icons) with actionability (switch + prominent manual sync CTA), enabling users to either enable continuous synchronization or perform an immediate one-time sync. The clear visual hierarchy (title -> section toggle -> explanation -> icons -> CTA) ensures efficient decision-making and reduces friction for users managing sensitive health data.

steps.name: Sync Progress Modal
steps.goal: Inform the user that a full sync is running and that the app must remain open until completion.
steps.action: Wait while the app performs the sync (user instructed not to close the app).
steps.system_response: App shows the number of records being processed and a spinner. The background sync proceeds and updates progress until complete or interrupted.

content.description:
General visual summary
- Overall style: Clean, iOS-style native look with generous spacing, rounded corners and muted, neutral colors. Uses a single-column content flow with a translucent/dimmed background when the bottom sheet is shown. Visual language: large friendly headings, uppercase section labels, light body copy and soft dividers. The design prioritizes legibility and calm microcopy with a minimal affordance set (one toggle and a progress state). Uses soft shadows and a white modal surface for the bottom sheet.

Color palette (use these HEX values exactly for reproduction)
- Dark text (primary headings / icons): #3B3B39 (0x3B3B39)
- Secondary text / body copy: #9B9B9B (0x9B9B9B)
- Accent / subtle brown/olive: #6F6A48 (0x6F6A48) — used in small decorative items / muted accents
- White / sheet surface: #FBFBFB (0xFBFBFB)
- Muted divider / secondary surface: #B3AEAB (0xB3AEAB)
- Additional (toggle active color seen on screenshot; approximate): #00C2A8 (teal/green) — use to style the active toggle track and thumb glow. (This is an added accent color; main palette above should dominate.)

Typography
- Primary headings (screen title and modal title): Use a rounded humanist sans (e.g., SF Pro Display / Inter / Nunito) bold weight.
  - Screen title "Apple Health Sync": 28–32px, weight 700, letter-spacing: -0.2px, color #3B3B39, center-aligned horizontally; top safe area spacing applied.
  - Modal title "Keep the app open": 28px, weight 700, color #3B3B39, center-aligned inside bottom sheet. Line-height ~1.05.
- Section label (uppercase): "SYNC YOUR DATA": 13–14px, weight 700, uppercase, letter-spacing 1px, color #3B3B39, left aligned within the content column.
- Body paragraph copy: 15–17px, weight 400 (regular), color #9B9B9B, line-height 1.45–1.6, left aligned, paragraph spacing ~12–16px.
- Emphasized small labels (e.g., "67 records"): 15px, weight 700 (semi-bold), color #3B3B39, center aligned inside modal content row.

Important UI elements & styles
- Navigation / back button: circular soft translucent button in top-left with a left chevron icon. Button size ~44–48px diameter, background a very light gray (10% black on #FBFBFB) with subtle inner shadow; chevron icon ~18–20px stroke, color #3B3B39. Positioned at approximately 16px from the left edge and aligned to safe area top.
- Header title placement: centered horizontally, vertically placed below top safe area (~20–28px below). A thin horizontal divider (1px) separates header block from content area.
- Section row ("SYNC YOUR DATA" + toggle): horizontal row, left-aligned label, right side toggle. Row height ~56px. Use a 1px light divider above and below the row.
- Toggle / Switch: width ~48–56px, height ~28–32px. Track radius fully rounded (~16px). Active track color #00C2A8, inactive track color #E6E6E6. Thumb diameter ~20–22px, white with subtle drop shadow. Provide pressed/focus state (slightly larger thumb shadow). The toggle sits flush with the right padding (16–20px from the edge).
- Body copy block: top padding ~12–18px under the section row, left/right padding 20–24px. The text block contains multiple paragraphs; a small emoji inline (pointing finger) appears at the beginning of the second paragraph (render as inline text with the same line-height). Use soft paragraph spacing.

Bottom sheet (modal) details
- Placement & shape: A sheet that slides up from the bottom and covers roughly the lower 45–55% of the viewport. Top corners gently rounded ~18px. The sheet surface color = #FBFBFB (white). A very faint drop shadow under the sheet to provide separation from the dimmed background.
- Background overlay: a full-screen translucent dim layer covering the main content; color black with opacity ~18–26% to mute the background content (do not fully hide the header; a subtle blurred effect is acceptable if supported). The primary content remains visible but de-emphasized.
- Internal sheet layout: content vertically stacked, centered alignment for the modal title and support text. Top padding inside sheet ~28px, side padding 24px. A thin 1px divider line runs above the "67 records" row and below it, visually separating the main message from the record count block.
- Modal title: large, center-aligned (see Typography above). Followed by a one-paragraph helper text in secondary color (#9B9B9B), center-aligned, width constrained for easier reading (~80% of sheet width).
- Record count row: centered text "67 records" in semi-bold (see typography), with top and bottom padding ~18–20px and a 1px divider above and below.
- Spinner: indeterminate circular loader centered near the bottom of the sheet. Size ~36–44px diameter. Use 8–10 segments with a portion darker (#3B3B39) and the remainder light (#B3AEAB) to mimic the screenshot. The spinner rotates continuously (see Animations).

Dividers & separators
- Thin 1px lines using #B3AEAB at 10–18% opacity for subtle separation. Spacing around dividers is generous to keep the layout airy.

Iconography
- Use thin, geometric icons matching the typography (stroke width ~2px). Chevron/back, toggle thumb accents, and the spinner are the most important icons in this composition.

Micro-interactions & animation
- Bottom sheet entrance: slide up with easing cubic-bezier(.22,.9,.2,1) over 300–420ms. When opening, overlay opacity animates from 0 to final in 180–260ms.
- Spinner: continuous rotation, 1s per full rotation, linear timing. The segments can fade in/out to create a smooth loop.
- Toggle: thumb moves with 160–200ms ease-out; track color cross-fades. Provide haptic feedback on iOS.

Accessibility notes
- Large text for main headings and modal title for readability.
- Ensure sufficient contrast between primary text (#3B3B39) and white background (#FBFBFB). Secondary text (#9B9B9B) meets mid-size contrast but consider slightly darker shade if accessibility tests fail.
- Make toggle reachable and make the bottom sheet accessible via VoiceOver with labels for the spinner ("Syncing"), record count ("67 records"), and a hint to keep the app open.

Measurements & spacing summary (px reference for a 375pt wide iPhone screen)
- Safe area top: 44px
- Horizontal content padding: 20–24px
- Header top margin: 18–22px below safe area
- Section row height: 56px
- Section divider spacing: 12–14px top/bottom
- Modal sheet top corner radius: 18px
- Modal internal top padding: 28px
- Modal side padding: 24px
- Spinner size: 40px

Reproduction tips
- Build as a single-column layout with a stacked bottom sheet overlay. Use native toggle control for correct proportions. Keep the background content visible but dimmed when the sheet is active. Use consistent rounded corner radii across all circular elements (back button, toggle thumb, sheet corners). Match typography weights and spacing carefully: large headline, small uppercase section heading, readable body text, centered modal title and one-line helper text, bolded centered record count, spinner below.
content.layout:

content.functions:
Specific user actions supported on this screen
- Tapping the circular back icon: navigates back to the previous view (standard navigation affordance). The back control is a tappable icon-only button placed in the top-left safe area.
- Toggling synchronization on/off: user can tap the switch to enable or disable automatic data sync with Apple Health. Visual state toggles the track color and moves the thumb; the app should update a persisted setting when changed.
- Reading contextual information: the screen provides explanatory paragraphs about what is synced (Water, Caffeine, Alcohol) and how data from Apple Health is imported/exported. Inline emoji is used for emphasis in the second paragraph.
- Initiating sync (implicit action): toggling the switch or tapping a separate sync control (not visible in this screenshot) triggers a sync action. When syncing begins, a bottom sheet appears to communicate progress and instructions.
- Viewing progress and counts: when sync is active, a bottom sheet modal appears with a headline "Keep the app open", helper copy describing what to do if the process is interrupted, a centered count of records being processed (e.g., "67 records") and a centered indeterminate spinner that visually communicates active work.
- Monitoring state but no direct cancel: there is no visible cancel button in the sheet; the user’s primary action is to keep the app open until completion. The UI communicates that an interrupted process must be restarted.

Medium-level workflows enabled by this screen
- Configure automatic data sharing between the app and Apple Health: the toggle acts as the gateway, enabling background export/import of selected data types.
- Start a manual or background sync routine and monitor its progress: the sheet provides a focused status screen where users can confirm the app is syncing and how many records are being processed.
- Diagnose inconsistencies: the explanatory text instructs users to use a "Sync All Data" action elsewhere if they find mismatches in Apple Health; this screen informs and routes users toward remediation steps.

Broader purpose the user achieves
- The ultimate goal is reliable, transparent synchronization of health-related data between the product and Apple's Health store. The screen combines settings management (enable/disable), information (what is synced and how), and operational feedback (progress during a sync). It is designed to keep users informed and to reduce confusion about whether or when data was transferred. The sheet explicitly prevents accidental interruption by asking users to keep the app open, thereby increasing the success rate of the data transfer process.

steps.name: Sync Completion Confirmation
steps.goal: Confirm successful completion of the sync to the user.
steps.action: Tap 'OK' on the success alert to dismiss.
steps.system_response: Success alert dismisses and the app returns to the Apple Health Sync settings screen with sync enabled (end state).

content.description:
Mobile settings-style screen (iPhone) titled "Apple Health Sync" with an iOS aesthetic: large centered page title near the top, a left circular back button, and a system status bar at the very top. Overall background is a very light gray (main palette includes 0xCBCBCB and 0xECECEC) with subtle inner shadows and soft contrast. Typography: the title uses a rounded, heavy sans (looks like SF Pro Rounded or similar) ~34–36pt, bold/black with tight tracking and center alignment. A horizontal divider below the title is a thin 1px line in a muted gray (#CBCBCB). Immediately below, a section header in uppercase reads "SYNC YOUR DATA" in small bold sans ~12–14pt, letter-spaced and left-aligned. To the right of that header is an iOS-style switch (active state) with a teal/cyan fill (accent color from palette — use 0x3168A9 for primary accent; actual switch thumb is white). Body copy is a multi-line paragraph describing what sync does. Body text is medium-gray (approx #4A4A4A), ~16–18pt, regular weight, 1.4–1.6 line-height, left-aligned with generous left/right margins. Under the paragraph there are three rounded square “cards” (icon tiles) arranged horizontally — each tile has a pale rounded rectangle background and contains a colorful flat illustration/icon: a stacked multicolor shape, a sync arrows icon, and a heart. The icons use accent colors from the provided palette (0xC1AF12 gold, 0x3168A9 blue, 0x8B4371 purple) and have about 12–16px internal padding within each tile. At the lower portion of the screen there is a large pill-shaped primary CTA button with a bright cyan/teal fill (use 0x3168A9 or slightly lighter/cyan variant) and white centered label: "Sync all-time data now". Button is horizontally centered, wide (approx 80–90% width), height ~56px, border-radius ~28px, subtle drop shadow. Visual hierarchy is clear: title > section header + switch > body copy > icon tiles > CTA.

A centered modal/alert overlays the middle of the screen: an iOS-style rounded rectangle with a blurred/dimmed background behind it (full-screen overlay). The alert has a soft white fill (#FFFFFF with slight translucency), corner radius large (~16–20px), and a subtle inner shadow to create the raised look. The alert contains a short message "Success!" (centered, medium-large bold text) and a large pill-shaped action button below it labeled "OK". The OK button inside the alert is a pale gray rounded pill (approx #ECECEC->#DCDCDC) with dark text. The alert is horizontally centered, width ~70–80% of the screen, and its vertical position sits slightly above the absolute center of the screen.

Spacing & alignment: generous top safe area (status 44px), title top margin ~16–24px, horizontal content padding ~20–28px. Body paragraphs have 20–24px vertical spacing between sections. The primary CTA sits above the bottom safe area by ~24–32px. Visual language: soft rounded geometry, large touch targets, high-contrast headline, muted supporting text, colorful illustrative icons to indicate data types. Microcopy: friendly, instructional tone. Shadows & elevation: subtle drop shadows under the alert and under the primary CTA to emphasize prominence. The overall style is modern iOS, friendly and approachable with rounded corners, muted neutrals and a bright accent color for actions.
content.layout:
Single-column vertical layout (one primary column). The page is organized into distinct stacked groups from top to bottom:
1) Top safe area and navigation header (status bar + back button at left). The header group includes the large centered title "Apple Health Sync" with a thin divider line below it.
2) Sync control row: left-aligned small uppercase section label "SYNC YOUR DATA" and right-aligned iOS-style switch (grouped on the same horizontal row). This is visually separated from content above and below by thin dividers, forming a small two-column arrangement inside the single-column layout (label column and control column).
3) Informational text block: multi-line paragraph with left alignment and wide horizontal padding. This block occupies full column width.
4) Icon tiles row: a horizontally arranged set of icon cards (3 tiles across on wide phones) — each tile is a rounded square; tiles are evenly spaced and center-aligned horizontally. Treat this as a 1 row × 3 column grid of icon cards.
5) Large primary CTA: centered pill button anchored near the bottom with large horizontal padding and ample vertical spacing above.
Overlay: a centered modal/alert sits above content in a separate overlay layer (Full-screen overlay + centered dialog). The alert is single-column internally: title text, spacer, then a single pill action button.
Spacing & paddings: page horizontal padding ~20–28px; vertical gaps between groups vary from 12–32px; icon tiles have ~12–16px gaps between them. Use a consistent grid baseline (8px increments) for spacing. No multi-column body content beyond the small label/control row and the 3-column icon tile group.
content.functions:
Specific actions (micro-level):
- Tap the circular back icon in the top-left to return to the previous screen. The back icon is a left chevron inside a subtle circular background.
- Toggle the on/off Switch (to the right of the "SYNC YOUR DATA" label) to enable or disable continuous syncing between the app and Apple Health. The switch provides immediate visual feedback (thumb moves, fill color appears when enabled).
- Read the description text to understand what types of data are synced (water, caffeine, alcohol) and how import/export works.
- Interact with the illustrative icon tiles (if tappable) to view mapping or details for each data type — the screen visually groups these as informational tiles.
- Tap the large primary CTA button labeled "Sync all-time data now" to initiate a manual full sync of historical data. This triggers a process that displays progress/feedback and ultimately a success confirmation.
- Dismiss the success modal by tapping the prominently displayed "OK" button inside the dialog.

Medium-level tasks (flows):
- Turn on sync and grant any necessary permissions (the toggle indicates the user's desire to sync; pressing the CTA or toggling may trigger OS-level permission dialogs). The UI supports immediate enable/disable and a clear next step for manual full sync.
- Initiate a manual full-data synchronization and receive confirmation feedback (the success modal confirms completion). The CTA is large and visually distinct to encourage the user to run the sync if they want all historical data transferred.
- Learn what data types are shared via the descriptive copy and illustrative tiles, enabling informed consent and transparency about what will be exported/imported.

High-level goal (macro-level):
- The user connects and synchronizes health-related data between this product and Apple Health. The screen's purpose is to configure and trigger syncing, communicate what kinds of data are involved, and provide confirmation once a sync completes successfully. The design prioritizes clarity (clear header, toggle state), control (manual sync CTA), and feedback (success alert) so the user can confidently enable cross-app data exchange.
